findings.correction: none — all four verified: DESCRIPTION:3 `Version: 3.10.0`; README.md:1727 "(Version 2.8.0)" and README.md:1734 `version = {2.8.0}`; CITATION.cff:109 `version: "2.1.0"` with :110 `date-released: "2026-04-23"`; preferred-citation `version: "1.6.0"`. `ls inst/CITATION` -> No such file. CITATION.cff:7 "organised across six research pillars" vs DESCRIPTION:8-9 "ten research pillars". Of 2.8.0 / 2.1.0 / 1.6.0 only v1.6.0 is a real tag (tag list ends v1.6.0 then jumps to v3.10.0).
findings.evidence: DESCRIPTION:3 `Version: 3.10.0`. README.md:1727 "Rodrigues, H. (2026). *edaphos ...* (Version 2.8.0) [Software]. Zenodo." and README.md:1734 bibtex `version   = {2.8.0}`. CITATION.cff:109 `version: "2.1.0"` with CITATION.cff:110 `date-released: "2026-04-23"`. CITATION.cff:184 `preferred-citation: ... version: "1.6.0"` -- i.e. the block CFF consumers prefer names a fifth-oldest release. `ls inst/CITATION` -> ABSENT, so `citation("edaphos")` falls back to DESCRIPTION and returns yet another answer (3.10.0), which README.md:1745-1747 actively directs users to ("An auto-generated citation is also available in R: `citation("edaphos")`"). CITATION.cff's abstract is also frozen: CITATION.cff:7 "It is organised across six research pillars" and the narrative stops at v2.1.0 (CITATION.cff:97-107), so the .cff describes a 6-pillar package while DESCRIPTION:8-9 describes a 10-pillar one.
findings.impact: GitHub renders the "Cite this repository" widget from CITATION.cff, so the repo's most prominent citation surface advertises v2.1.0 released 2026-04-23. Zenodo, Zotero, and rOpenSci tooling ingest the same file. A reader who cites via GitHub gets 2.1.0, via README gets 2.8.0, via `citation()` gets 3.10.0, via a CFF parser honouring preferred-citation gets 1.6.0. None of 2.8.0, 2.1.0 or 1.6.0 corresponds to a resolvable git ref except 1.6.0. This is unfixable after publication -- wrong versions propagate into other people's bibliographies.
findings.action: Make CITATION.cff the single source and derive it: set CITATION.cff:109 `version` and :110 `date-released` to the real release, delete or sync the redundant :184 `version` inside preferred-citation, refresh the :4-107 abstract to the 10-pillar description from DESCRIPTION:8-28, and update README.md:1727 and :1734 to the same number. Add a release-checklist step (or a CI job running `cffconvert --validate` plus a version-equality assertion against DESCRIPTION) so the four never drift again.

findings.title: The "1 345 tests" figure is unreproducible, mis-attributed, and the NEWS test-count chain contains two arithmetic breaks
findings.correction: none — independently measured: 68 `test-*.R` files, 460 `test_that(` blocks, 1089 `expect_` calls, 75 `skip_if_not_installed(`. README.md:12 badge `tests-1345%20pass`, NEWS.md:72, cran-comments.md:30-35, inst/rosc/submission.md:69 all verified verbatim. Arithmetic breaks verified: NEWS.md:299 (3.6.0)=1274, NEWS.md:242 (3.7.0)=1282 but 1274+7=1281 (off by 1); NEWS.md:195 (3.8.0)=1308 but 1282+20=1302 (off by 6). The Ollama attribution is verified impossible: `grep -rn 'skip_on_cran|skip_if_offline|skip_on_ci' tests/testthat/` returns exactly one hit (test-quantum-kernel-rcpp.R:46). Commit 4b15fb7 "fix(ci/windows): suppress cosmetic sweep() warning in test-pilar8-no-edge.R:42" exists in `git rev-list v3.10.0..HEAD`, confirming the blamed warning was already suppressed. README.md:1672 "**109+ unit and integration tests**" confirmed self-contradictory with the 1345 badge.
findings.evidence: Claims: README.md:12 badge `tests-1345%20pass`; NEWS.md:72 "1 345 tests pass (+17 vs v3.9.0)."; cran-comments.md:30-35 "`devtools::test()` -- **1 345 unit tests**, 0 failures, 4 warnings, 2 skips. The 4 warnings are documented cosmetic stats::sweep recycling on odd column counts (Pilar 8); the 2 skips are LLM-benchmark tests that require a live Ollama instance."; inst/rosc/submission.md:69 "**Unit tests**: 50+ test files, **1 345 expectations**." Measured in this tree: 68 test-*.R files, 460 `test_that(` blocks, 1089 `expect_` calls, 75 `skip_if_not_installed(` calls. Live run: 1022 pass, 109 skip, 2 errors, 2 warnings. Every sub-claim of cran-comments.md:30-35 is wrong: the skip count is 109 not 2; the skip REASONS are 74x torch, 22x dagitty, 9x bnlearn, 3x dbarts, 1 other -- zero Ollama-related; and the sweep warning it blames was already suppressed by commit 4b15fb7 "fix(ci/windows): suppress cosmetic sweep() warning in test-pilar8-no-edge.R:42", while the actual 2 live warnings are "NAs produced" from `bhs_fit` at tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:61 (Pilar 7, not 8). The NEWS chain also does not add up: NEWS.md:299 (3.6.0) 1274, NEWS.md:242 (3.7.0) "1 282 (+7 vs v3.6.0)" -> 1274+7=1281, off by 1; NEWS.md:195 (3.8.0) "1 308 (+20 vs v3.7.0)" -> 1282+20=1302, off by 6. The rest of the chain is internally consistent (3.0.0=1177 -> 3.1.0=1213 -> 3.2.0=1239 -> 3.3.0=1239 -> 3.4.0=1256 -> 3.5.0=1269 -> 3.6.0=1274; 3.9.0=1328 -> 3.10.0=1345), so 7 tests were introduced by arithmetic rather than by code. README is additionally self-contradictory: the badge says 1345 while README.md:1672 in the same file says "**109+ unit and integration tests**".
findings.impact: 1345 is defensible ONLY on a machine with torch, dagitty, bnlearn and dbarts installed (the 109 gated blocks would then execute and multiply into expectations) -- but that is nowhere stated, and no environment in the repo reproduces it. As published, the number is unverifiable by any reader and demonstrably wrong in the environment cran-comments.md itself designates as the base case. inst/rosc/submission.md:69's "50+ test files" understates 68, and calling 1345 "expectations" in one file and "unit tests" in another means the project does not know which quantity it is quoting.
findings.action: Pick one measured quantity and state the environment with it, e.g. "460 test_that blocks / 1089 expectations; 1022 pass + 109 skipped without torch/dagitty/bnlearn/dbarts (R 4.6.1 aarch64-darwin)". Regenerate the README.md:12 badge from that number, delete or correct the contradictory README.md:1672 "109+", fix the +7/+20 arithmetic at NEWS.md:242 and NEWS.md:195, and rewrite cran-comments.md:30-35 to report the true skip count and the true warning source (test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:61, not Pilar 8 sweep).

findings.title: The README's only install command pins a git ref that does not exist (`@v2.8.0`)
findings.evidence: README.md:339-340: `remotes::install_github("HugoMachadoRodrigues/edaphos@v2.8.0", build_vignettes = TRUE)`. `git rev-parse -q --verify v2.8.0` -> not found (see the tag list: tags stop at v1.6.0 then jump to v3.10.0). This is the sole install instruction in the 84 KB README (`grep -rn install_github` over the repo returns only README.md:339 and Dockerfile:67). Cross-check: NEWS.md:805 documents a `# edaphos 2.8.0` release and the roadmap row README.md:1713 marks v2.8.0 as shipped -- so the pin is not a typo, it points at a release the project believes it made but never tagged.
findings.impact: Every new user's first command fails with `Error: Failed to install 'edaphos' from GitHub: reference 'v2.8.0' not found`. The package is effectively uninstallable by its documented path. It also silently pins users two major-minor arcs behind (2.8.0 vs 3.10.0) even if the tag were created.
findings.action: Change README.md:339 to install the current release (`edaphos@v3.10.0`, once #2 is resolved) or drop the pin entirely (`install_github("HugoMachadoRodrigues/edaphos", build_vignettes = TRUE)`). Add a CI step or a pre-release checklist item that greps README.md for `@v[0-9]` and verifies the ref resolves.

findings.title: CITATION.cff assigns the identical DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19710162 to twelve different "Version DOI" entries
findings.evidence: CITATION.cff:122-157 declares `type: doi, value: "10.5281/zenodo.19710162"` twelve times, labelled "Version DOI (v1.6.0)", "(v1.7.0)", "(v1.7.1)", "(v1.7.2)", "(v1.8.0)", "(v1.8.1)", "(v1.8.2)", "(v1.9.0)", "(v1.9.1)", "(v1.9.2)", "(v2.0.0)", "(v2.1.0)". Only two distinct DOIs appear besides it: :118 concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19683708 and :121 "Version DOI (v1.5.0)" 10.5281/zenodo.19709560. Zenodo mints a unique version DOI per deposit, so a single id cannot be the version DOI of twelve versions -- meaning eleven of these entries are fabricated, and (consistent with #2) no Zenodo deposit was ever made for v1.7.0 onward.
findings.impact: Anyone resolving 10.5281/zenodo.19710162 expecting v2.1.0 lands on whatever single record it actually is (v1.6.0/v1.7.0-era at best). The identifiers block makes the archival record look complete when eleven of thirteen versions were never archived. This is exactly the kind of provenance defect an rOpenSci reviewer or a journal data-availability check catches.
findings.action: Delete the eleven duplicate entries at CITATION.cff:125-157, keeping only DOIs that resolve (:118 concept, :121 v1.5.0, and whichever single record 19710162 really is, correctly labelled). Add real version DOIs only after each Zenodo deposit is actually published -- which per RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:51-71 has not happened for v3.10.0.

findings.title: DESCRIPTION promises ten research pillars; every document shipped in the CRAN tarball documents six, and pillars 7-10 have no roadmap row, no README section and no vignette
findings.evidence: DESCRIPTION:8-25 enumerates ten pillars. Against that: `R/pillars_roadmap.R:1` is titled "Roadmap and status of the six pillars of edaphos" and its table (lines 8-15) has exactly 6 rows; the generated `man/edaphos-roadmap.Rd:5` inherits that title. `R/edaphos-package.R:10,14` say "**six research pillars**" / `@section Six research pillars:`, rendered into `man/edaphos-package.Rd:13,20`. README.md:371 heading is `## The six pillars at a glance` and its table has 6 pillar rows plus 2 non-pillar rows; there is no `## Pillar 7/8/9/10` section (README pillar headings stop at :1288 `## Pillar 6 — Quantum ML`). `vignettes/` contains pilar1..pilar6 Rmd files only — no pilar7/8/9/10 vignette. README.md:10 badge reads `pillars-10%2F10%20shipped` and links to `#the-six-pillars-at-a-glance`. What DOES cover 7-10: `_pkgdown.yml:161-180` (four reference groups), `cheatsheets/pilar7.md`..`pilar10.md`, `vignettes/getting-started.Rmd:135-183`, `INTRO.md:42-59`, and man pages `bhs_fit.Rd`, `no_fno_fit.Rd`, `no_deeponet_fit.Rd`, `dm_fit.Rd`, `dm_sample.Rd`, `gnn_build_graph.Rd`, `gnn_fit.Rd`. Note `.Rbuildignore` excludes `^cheatsheets$`, `^INTRO\.md$`, `^_pkgdown\.yml$` — so of the artifacts covering 7-10, only getting-started.Rmd and the .Rd pages reach a CRAN user.
findings.impact: A CRAN reviewer reading DESCRIPTION then `?edaphos-package` or `?edaphos-roadmap` sees a direct contradiction (ten vs six) inside the tarball itself — a likely rOpenSci/CRAN comment. Users of pillars 7-10 get man pages with no narrative: no derivation vignette in the style promised at README.md:384-388 ("one or more vignettes deriving the object from first principles"), and no status/governing-object row in the roadmap landing page the docs designate as the API entry point.
findings.action: Four concrete gaps to close: (1) add rows 7-10 to the `R/pillars_roadmap.R` table and retitle to "ten pillars", then re-roxygenise; (2) change `R/edaphos-package.R:10,14` to ten and add \item blocks for pillars 7-10 mirroring the existing 1-6; (3) add `## Pillar 7`..`## Pillar 10` sections to README.md after :1288 and expand the at-a-glance table to 10 rows (also fix the anchor in the badge at :10); (4) promote at least `cheatsheets/pilar7.md`-`pilar10.md` content into real vignettes, or explicitly state in the roadmap that 7-10 are documented via cheatsheets + getting-started only.

findings.title: R² is floored at zero in three benchmark code paths, censoring negative values and turning them into a "statistically indistinguishable" conclusion
findings.evidence:
Three sites clip R² before it is averaged across folds and published:
```
R/quantum_foundation.R:279            r2 = max(0, 1 - sum(err^2, na.rm = TRUE) / ...)
data-raw/benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7.R:244  r2_val <- max(0, 1 - mean((point_pred - truth)^2, ...) / mean((truth - mean(truth))^2))
data-raw/benchmark_wosis_6pilar.R:157   r2_val <- max(0, 1 - ...)
```
Effects visible in shipped artefacts and README:
- `inst/extdata/quantum_foundation_cerrado.rds$cv_table$r2` is exactly `0` for "RBF-KRR on foundation PCs", "Quantum KRR on raw covariates" and "Quantum KRR on foundation PCs" in **every** fold; `cv_summary$r2_mean` = 0, 0, 0, 0.0807.
- `README.md:1406-1411` publishes "R² 0.00" for three methods and concludes "The four regressors are **statistically indistinguishable** on this benchmark."
- `inst/extdata/benchmark_wosis_6pilar.rds$cv_aggregate` shows `r2_mean` exactly `0.00000000` for P6 Quantum KRR and P10 GAT ensemble, reproduced in `NEWS.md:427-428`.

Because the clip is applied per fold before averaging, even a method with mildly positive mean R² has its cross-fold average biased upward, and a method that is systematically worse than the intercept-only model is indistinguishable from one that exactly matches it.
findings.impact: A method that predicts worse than the training mean is published as "R² = 0.00", identical to a method that ties it. This directly underwrites the README's "statistically indistinguishable" and "matches but does not surpass ranger" conclusions and the NEWS "RMSE is a flat band" reading — conclusions drawn from a censored metric. Any reviewer recomputing R² from the stored predictions gets negative values that the package never reports.
findings.action: Remove `max(0, ...)` from all three sites and let R² go negative; a negative R² is the informative result. Re-run `data-raw/benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7.R`, `data-raw/benchmark_wosis_6pilar.R` and the quantum benchmark, and update `README.md:1406-1411`, `NEWS.md:601-608` and `NEWS.md:421-428`. Add a unit test that `benchmark`-family R² is not clipped (e.g. feed a constant predictor worse than the mean and assert the returned R² < 0).

findings.title: The v1.8.0 multi-backend LLM benchmark is entirely simulated and its headline F1/latency values are hard-coded function arguments
findings.correction: Verified end to end: inst/extdata/llm_benchmark_results.rds has `mode = "simulated"`, `version = 1.7.2`, `date_computed = 2026-04-23 16:52:56` (predating the v1.8.0 release it documents); data-raw/llm_benchmark_run.R:128/:142/:156 carry the hard-coded `sim_args` exactly as quoted (latency_mean 15.2 / 3.1 / 5.7; precision_target 0.85 / 0.80 / 0.90); R/llm_benchmark.R:334-338 derives false positives analytically from `precision_target`, and :351-361 draws them iid from a shared 17-token `noise_pool`, so near-zero pairwise kappa is structural — the shipped `kappa_matrix` off-diagonals (-0.0811, 0.1216) match README's "κ ≈ −0.08 to 0.12" precisely. Two refinements: the tabulated P/R/F1 are simulator *outputs*, not the literal inputs (Claude prints precision 0.82 against a precision_target of 0.90), so "the reported values are inputs" overstates slightly; and README.md:697-700 does disclose the simulation — but four lines BELOW the table, framed as "runs reproducibly in CI", and without retracting "The first quantitative validation" or any of the "Key findings". Vendor-attributed numbers for three named commercial products remain unmeasured.
findings.evidence:
`README.md:668-695` presents "### v1.8.0 — Multi-backend LLM extraction benchmark ... **The first quantitative validation** of the Gemma 4 extractor" with a table of Precision / Recall / F1 / Cost / "Latency (median)" for Gemma 4, GPT-4o-mini and Claude Sonnet-4.5, followed by "**Key findings.**"

The shipped artefact `inst/extdata/llm_benchmark_results.rds` has `mode = "simulated"` and `version = 1.7.2` (`date_computed = 2026-04-23`, i.e. predating the v1.8.0 release it documents). No API was ever called.

The reported values are inputs, not measurements. `data-raw/llm_benchmark_run.R`:
```
128:  sim_args = list(recall = 0.80, precision_target = 0.85, ... latency_mean = 15.2, latency_sd = 4.1)   # Gemma 4
142:  sim_args = list(recall = 0.88, precision_target = 0.80, ... latency_mean = 3.1,  latency_sd = 0.8)   # GPT-4o-mini
156:  sim_args = list(recall = 0.84, precision_target = 0.90, ... latency_mean = 5.7,  latency_sd = 1.4)   # Claude
```
and `R/llm_benchmark.R:327-338` shows `llm_benchmark_simulate(gold, recall = 0.82, precision_target = 0.86, ...)` derives false positives analytically from `precision_target`.

Each README "key finding" is therefore a restatement of an author-chosen constant:
- "**Claude has the best F1** (0.82)" ← Claude has the highest `precision_target` (0.90) by construction.
- "**GPT-4o-mini is the fastest** (2.8 s vs. 5.4 s vs. 16 s median latency per abstract)" ← `latency_mean = 3.1 / 5.7 / 15.2`; the seconds are draws from `rnorm`, not wall-clock timings.
- "**Backends disagree strongly on which abstracts to extract** (κ ≈ −0.08 to 0.12 pairwise), which means ... This finding **justifies the three-backend architecture** already shipped." ← false positives are drawn iid per backend from a shared `noise_pool` (`R/llm_benchmark.R:353-361`), so near-zero pairwise κ is a mathematical necessity of the simulator, not an empirical discovery.

The disclosure at `README.md:697-700` ("runs reproducibly in CI using `llm_benchmark_simulate()`") appears *after* the table and does not retract the "Key findings".
findings.impact: An architecture decision ("justifies the three-backend architecture") and a cost/quality tradeoff recommendation ("switching from Claude to Gemma 4 saves ~$37.50 at the cost of 11 F1-points") are presented as empirical results derived from a simulator whose per-backend parameters the author selected. Vendor-attributed performance numbers for three named commercial products, published in a citable package, are fabricated in the technical sense that no measurement was taken. This is the single highest-reputational-risk item in the repository.
findings.action: Either (a) run the real benchmark once with `EDAPHOS_USE_REAL_LLM=1`, commit the resulting `mode = "real"` bundle, and report those numbers; or (b) if a real run is out of scope, delete the vendor-named table from `README.md:676-695` entirely and replace it with a statement that the harness is validated on a deterministic simulator and carries no empirical vendor comparison. Do not keep vendor-attributed P/R/F1/latency figures sourced from `sim_args`. Add a guard in `data-raw/llm_benchmark_run.R` that refuses to write to `inst/extdata/` when `USE_REAL` is FALSE, or writes to a `*_simulated.rds` filename.

findings.title: No test validates any headline number or any of the twelve committed result bundles
findings.correction: Core claims CONFIRMED: only tests/testthat/test-llm-annotation.R:111 reads inst/extdata (the gold-standard JSONL); no .rds bundle is opened by any test; the headline-number grep hits only the comment at test-benchmark-6pilar.R:4; NEWS.md:357 "1 269 tests pass" and cran-comments.md:5 "0/0/0"; the Sargan divergence is real (README.md:852 "0.343 ✅" vs causal_iv_cerrado_real.rds benchmark_table$sargan_p[2] = 3.22e-08). One detail is wrong: there is no 0.2188 or "1095" match at test-llm-annotation.R:95 -- the grep returns exactly one hit repo-wide in tests/, the comment at test-benchmark-6pilar.R:4.
findings.evidence:
A grep for the published figures across the whole suite returns nothing: `grep -rn "13\.51|14\.07|13\.86|0\.2188|1095" tests/testthat/` matches only a comment (`tests/testthat/test-benchmark-6pilar.R:4`, "the full 1 095-profile run lives in") and an unrelated confidence value (`test-llm-annotation.R:95`).

Exactly **one** of 69 test files reads anything from `inst/extdata/`: `tests/testthat/test-llm-annotation.R:111` (`system.file("extdata", "cerrado_gold_standard_v1.jsonl", ...)`), and only to parse the gold-standard JSONL. None of the twelve `.rds` result bundles — `case_cerrado_results.rds`, `causal_cerrado_real.rds`, `causal_iv_cerrado_real.rds`, `benchmark_wosis_6pilar.rds`, `quantum_foundation_cerrado.rds`, `llm_benchmark_results.rds`, and the rest — is opened by any test.

The consequence is demonstrable: the Sargan sign-flip (README 0.343 ✅ vs bundle 3.2e-08) survived commit `05cb516 feat(v1.9.3): close roadmap promise -- IV refit with real 31-channel ... stack`, whose entire purpose was to refit that analysis. Likewise every β in `README.md:632-636` drifted from `causal_cerrado_real.rds` undetected across ~30 releases. Meanwhile `NEWS.md:357` claims "1 269 tests pass" and `cran-comments.md:5` claims "0 errors / 0 warnings / 0 notes", so the suite's green status is actively reassuring about claims it never checks.
findings.impact: For a package whose product is its claims, the test suite covers the code but not the science. 1022 passing expectations provide no protection against the exact failure mode that has already occurred three times (IV Sargan, causal β table, LLM benchmark mode). Any future refit will silently desynchronise the README again.
findings.action: Add `tests/testthat/test-headline-claims.R` that loads each `inst/extdata/*.rds` and asserts the values quoted in `README.md` and `NEWS.md` to the published precision — Sargan p-values, the six causal β, the 6-pillar RMSE/R²/PICP/CRPS aggregate, the case-study RMSE/MAE/R²/PICP, and `mode == "real"` for `llm_benchmark_results.rds`. Also assert artefact provenance: `as.character(r$version) == "3.10.0"` (or an explicit allow-list of intentionally frozen artefacts) so staleness surfaces as a test failure. Best of all, generate the README tables from the bundles via `README.Rmd` so drift becomes structurally impossible.

findings.title: `.bench_inject_aleatoric()` manufactures the published PICP with author-chosen noise and silently degrades the published RMSE
findings.correction: none — verified end to end. R/benchmark_wosis.R:24-34 states the intent and the 0.20→0.85 target verbatim; :35-41 is the injector; call sites are :126 (P1), :184 (P6), :254 (P10); `.bench_residual_sd` at :47-52 is applied to in-sample fits (`stats::fitted(full_lm)` at :125). NEWS.md:386-389 reports PICP 0.232→0.953 / 0.249→0.601 / 0.073→0.825 and NEWS.md:430-433 concedes the in-sample no-LOO estimator. The RMSE corruption is arithmetically confirmed against the shipped bundle: `posterior_bank[[6]]$p1$metadata$sigma_resid` = 15.19607, `cv_aggregate` gives P10 rmse_mean = 15.19945 against NEWS.md:605's pre-injection 14.07, and sqrt(15.199² − 14.07²) = 5.75 ≈ sigma_resid/sqrt(n_ensemble=8) (data-raw/benchmark_wosis_6pilar.R:124), exactly the predicted colMeans residual offset; P1 with n_boot = 300L (:97) moves only 13.94→13.92 as predicted. P10's R² is 0.000 and it falls from rank 3 (NEWS.md:605-607, tied 14.07) to rank 6 in the re-sorted v3.4.0 table. NEWS.md:391-395 advertises only the CRPS gains; the RMSE regression appears in the :421-428 table but is never named. Severity honest: this is the package's own head-to-head, three of six methods affected, and it changes the ranking that data-raw/benchmark_wosis_6pilar.R:194 presents.
findings.evidence:
`R/benchmark_wosis.R:24-41` documents the intent explicitly: "v3.4.0 adds the missing ALEATORIC term: an estimate of the in-sample residual standard deviation `sigma_resid` is injected as iid Gaussian noise on every (sample, test-row) entry of the posterior matrix ... **PICP at the v3.1.0 head-to-head settings moves from ~0.20 to ~0.85, matching P4/P5/P7.**"

```r
35: .bench_inject_aleatoric <- function(pred_mat, sigma_resid, seed = NULL) {
37:   if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed + 13579L)
38:   noise <- matrix(stats::rnorm(length(pred_mat), 0, sigma_resid), nrow(pred_mat), ncol(pred_mat))
40:   pred_mat + noise
```
Called at `:126` (P1), `:184` (P6), `:254` (P10). `sigma_resid` comes from `.bench_residual_sd()` (`:47-52`) applied to **in-sample training** residuals.

Two distinct defects:

**(a) Coverage is set, not measured.** `NEWS.md:384-389` reports PICP_90 jumping "to nominal coverage": P1 0.232→0.953, P6 0.249→0.601, P10 0.073→0.825. `NEWS.md:430-433` concedes "P1 PICP is now mildly OVER-covered (0.95 vs nominal 0.90) because the OLS residual SD is computed in-sample without a leave-one-out adjustment". The published PICP is therefore a function of an undisclosed estimator choice, not a property of the model.

**(b) The injected noise corrupts the point predictions and thus RMSE/R².** Point predictions are `colMeans(post$samples)` (`data-raw/benchmark_wosis_6pilar.R:153`). Averaging `n` rows of injected noise leaves a residual offset of sd `sigma_resid/sqrt(n)`. Verified against the shipped bundle: `inst/extdata/benchmark_wosis_6pilar.rds$posterior_bank[[6]]$p1$metadata$sigma_resid = 15.196`. With `n_ensemble = 8L` for P10 (`data-raw/benchmark_wosis_6pilar.R:124`), the injected error is ≈15.2/√8 ≈ 5.4 g/kg — and the bundle's `cv_aggregate` shows **P10 RMSE = 15.199** against `NEWS.md:605`'s pre-injection **14.07** (sqrt(14.07² + 5.66²) = 15.17 ✓). P1, with `n_boot = 300L`, moves only 13.94 → 13.92 as predicted (15.2/√300 = 0.88). P10's R² is driven to exactly 0.000 and it drops from rank 3 to rank 6 in the re-sorted table (`NEWS.md:421-428`), with `NEWS.md:391-395` advertising only "CRPS also improves materially across the board" and no mention of the RMSE regression it caused.
findings.impact: Three of the six methods in the package's 6-pillar head-to-head have their calibration metric manufactured and their accuracy metric degraded by a fixed-seed noise draw. A reader comparing PICP across the six methods is comparing a real QRF quantile grid (P4/P5) against three numbers tuned to sit near 0.90. The reported P10 RMSE of 15.20 is 8% worse than the model's actual out-of-sample error purely because of the injection, which materially changes the ranking that `data-raw/benchmark_wosis_6pilar.R:194` (`arrange(rmse_mean)`) presents.
findings.action: Stop mutating the posterior samples. Instead (1) estimate the aleatoric term out-of-sample — CV residuals or a leave-one-out/OOB adjustment, not `stats::sd` of in-bag residuals; (2) widen the *intervals* analytically (convolve the epistemic spread with the aleatoric variance when computing PICP/MPIW/CRPS) so the point prediction is untouched and RMSE/R² are unaffected; (3) report both the epistemic-only and total-uncertainty PICP side by side; (4) in `NEWS.md:415-433` disclose the P10 RMSE regression from 14.07 to 15.18 as a consequence of the change rather than presenting only the CRPS improvement.

findings.title: The P4 "Foundation" row of the headline "first honest cross-pillar comparison" is computed on a pure Gaussian-noise raster
findings.correction: none — every cited line verified in data-raw/benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7.R: the template raster is filled with `stats::rnorm(terra::ncell(tpl))` and every one of the 31 encoder channels is overwritten with `stats::rnorm` in the following loop (the script's own message even prints "synthetic stack"); `dataset_meta` normalisation is `means = rep(0, ...), sds = rep(1, ...)`; `train_bhs <- if (n_tr > 300L) train[sample(n_tr, 300L), ] else train` caps P7 at 300 rows while P4/P5 get the full training fold; and the P7 "posterior" is rebuilt as `stats::rnorm(200L, pr$mean[j], pr$sd[j])`. README.md:243-255 carries no caveat, in direct contrast to README.md:1404/:1413 which does label the quantum table "(synthetic-stack mode)" / "random Gaussian rasters". The propagation into the 6-pillar table is consistent with the shipped benchmark_wosis_6pilar.rds reusing the same P4/P5/P7 rows.
findings.evidence:
`README.md:243-255` heads the section "**v2.8.0 — Real head-to-head benchmark on 1 095 WoSIS profiles.** First honest cross-pillar comparison" and reports `P4 Foundation+QRF | 14.1 | 0.034 | **0.889** | 37.6 | 5.93`, concluding "P4 best-calibrated at 0.89 ≈ nominal 0.90".

The covariate stack the MoCo encoder is run over is `rnorm()`. `data-raw/benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7.R:160-169`:
```r
166: terra::values(tpl) <- stats::rnorm(terra::ncell(tpl))
167: stk <- terra::rast(replicate(moco$n_channels, tpl, simplify = FALSE))
168: for (k in seq_len(moco$n_channels))
169:   terra::values(stk[[k]]) <- stats::rnorm(terra::ncell(stk))
```
with `dataset_meta` normalisation also placeholder (`means = rep(0, ...), sds = rep(1, ...)`, lines 154-157). The "foundation-model embedding" therefore carries zero information about location; the P4 row is P5's QRF plus 64 columns of noise.

Two further undisclosed asymmetries in the same script:
- `:208` `train_bhs <- if (n_tr > 300L) train[sample(n_tr, 300L), ] else train` — P7 BHS is fit on **300** training rows while P4 and P5 get all ~876. `README.md:250` credits P7 with the best R² and MPIW without noting it saw a third of the data.
- `:139-144` P7's "MCMC posterior" is discarded and replaced by `stats::rnorm(200L, pr$mean[j], pr$sd[j])` — a Gaussian re-simulation of a summary. P7's CRPS and PICP measure that Gaussian approximation, not the Gibbs posterior.

The honest counterpart exists and is correctly labelled: `README.md:1404` marks the quantum table "(synthetic-stack mode)" and `README.md:1413` says "Under synthetic embeddings (random Gaussian rasters)". The v2.8.0 section carries no such caveat.
findings.impact: The result advertised as the package's "first honest cross-pillar comparison" attributes a calibration win to a foundation model that was fed noise, and awards R²/MPIW honours to a method trained on 34% of the data whose posterior was replaced by a Gaussian. Because `data-raw/benchmark_wosis_6pilar.R:59-62,179,210` reuses this bundle wholesale for the P4/P5/P7 rows, the defect propagates into the 6-pillar table in `NEWS.md:601-608` and `NEWS.md:421-428` and into `inst/extdata/benchmark_wosis_6pilar.rds`.
findings.action: Either supply the real 31-channel Cerrado stack (the same one `data-raw/causal_iv_benchmark_real.R` builds via `foundation_build_cerrado_stack()`) with correct per-channel normalisation, or drop the P4 row and state that Pillar 4 is not benchmarkable without the raster download. Equalise P7's training set with P4/P5 or disclose the 300-row cap in every table caption. Replace the `rnorm(200, mean, sd)` reconstruction at `:139-144` with the actual Gibbs draws from `bhs_fit`. Add a "synthetic-stack mode" caveat to `README.md:243-255` matching the one already at `README.md:1404`.

findings.title: edaphos-cerrado-moco-v2 ships as an all-NA placeholder row in the exported public registry, keyed to a nonexistent package version 3.11.0
findings.evidence:
R/foundation_weights.R:48-85, row 2 of the data frame returned by the exported `foundation_weights_list()` (R/foundation_weights.R:104-106):
- line 67: `NA_character_           # filled after the user's Zenodo upload` (url)
- line 71: `NA_character_           # filled by tools/pretrain/package_v2_for_zenodo.R` (sha256)
- line 75: `NA_character_           # filled after the user's Zenodo upload` (doi)
- line 80: `NA_character_` (published_at)
- line 82: `edaphos_version = c("1.2.0", "3.11.0")`
The description at line 55 is written in the future tense about its own training: "Final InfoNCE loss **expected** ~0.4 at step 200000". DESCRIPTION:3 says `Version: 3.10.0`; there is no `# edaphos 3.11.0` section in NEWS.md. The same phantom version is baked into shipped documentation: R/foundation_embed_coords.R:186 ("As of v3.11.0"), :204 ("the v3.11.0 rewrite closes that gap"), :220, propagated to man/foundation_build_cerrado_stack.Rd:31,39,58.
findings.impact: `foundation_weights_list()` is an exported catalogue documented (R/foundation_weights.R:87-100) as describing "every pretrained encoder published by the `edaphos` project". Half its rows describe an artefact that does not exist, with a `license = "CC-BY-4.0"` and a full hyperparameter spec that make it look publishable. Users reading the table, or scripting over it, cannot distinguish published from aspirational except by NA-checking four columns. The `edaphos_version = "3.11.0"` column tells a user the weights need a package release that is not on CRAN, GitHub, or in NEWS.
findings.action: Either (a) drop the v2 row from `.foundation_weights_registry()` until the Zenodo deposit exists and re-add it in the release that publishes it, or (b) add an explicit `status` column (`"published"` / `"pending"`) so the placeholder is machine-readable, document it in the `@return` block at R/foundation_weights.R:100, and change `edaphos_version` to the version that will actually ship it. Separately, replace the v3.11.0 references in R/foundation_embed_coords.R:186,204,220 with 3.10.0 and re-roxygenise so man/foundation_build_cerrado_stack.Rd stops advertising a nonexistent release.

findings.title: foundation_build_cerrado_stack() silently writes a truncated stack to the cache when any geodata fetch fails, then reuses it forever
findings.impact: A transient WorldClim outage during the first call yields a 7-layer stack (5 SoilGrids + 2 SRTM) cached under the filename `cerrado_stack_v1_encoder_<hash>.tif`, which claims to be the v1_encoder schema. Every subsequent call returns that poisoned cache with only an informational "Using cached stack" message -- `force = TRUE` is the only escape and the user has no signal they need it. Feeding it to the 31-channel v1 encoder produces a torch conv2d channel-mismatch error far from the cause; feeding it to any user code that indexes layers positionally silently reads the wrong covariate. The docstring at :202-204 says this rewrite exists specifically to stop the IV benchmark falling back to a synthetic stack, so a silently-truncated real stack is the exact failure mode it was built to prevent.
findings.action: After line 361 in R/foundation_embed_coords.R, assert the schema's channel count before writing: `expected <- if (schema == "v1_encoder") 31L else 10L; if (terra::nlyr(stk) != expected) stop(sprintf("schema '%s' expects %d layers but only %d could be fetched (%s). Re-run when the sources are reachable.", schema, expected, terra::nlyr(stk), paste(names(layers), collapse=", ")))`. Also convert the five `message("      [warn] ", ...)` calls to `warning(...)` so partial failures are visible to `withCallingHandlers` and to test suites, and validate `terra::nlyr()` on the cache-hit path at line 245 before returning.

findings.title: qf_krr_benchmark() clamps R-squared at zero, contradicting the package's own edaphos_r2() and hiding worse-than-mean quantum models
findings.correction: Confirmed and stronger than argued. R/quantum_foundation.R:279 `r2 = max(0, 1 - ...)` is the only `max(0, 1 -` in R/; edaphos_r2 (R/edaphos_metrics.R:63-70) is unclamped and its header at :7-10 documents it as Nash-Sutcliffe. New evidence the auditor did not have: the clamp demonstrably fired in the SHIPPED bundle. `inst/extdata/quantum_foundation_cerrado.rds$cv_table` has `r2 == 0.00000000` in 9 of the 12 rows I inspected — in fold 2, RBF-KRR (RMSE 9.57) and ranger (RMSE 13.51) both report 0.00 despite a 4 g/kg RMSE gap, i.e. the clamp erased a real ordering. That bundle is what README.md:1406-1411 prints (0.00 for three of four methods) under the conclusion "The four regressors are statistically indistinguishable on this benchmark" — a conclusion the clamp manufactures.
findings.evidence:
R/quantum_foundation.R:274-283, the local `metrics()` helper used for every row of the benchmark table:
```r
r2     = max(0, 1 - sum(err^2, na.rm = TRUE) /
                    sum((truth - mean(truth, na.rm = TRUE))^2)),
```
The package's canonical metric does the opposite -- R/edaphos_metrics.R:63-69 returns the unclamped value, guarding only the degenerate case:
```r
edaphos_r2 <- function(observed, predicted) {
  ...
  if (ss_tot == 0) return(NA_real_)
  1 - ss_res / ss_tot
}
```
and documents itself at R/edaphos_metrics.R:7-10 as "Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency when the mean is the trivial model" -- a quantity whose whole diagnostic value is that it goes negative. `grep -rn "max(0, 1 -" R/*.R` returns exactly one hit, R/quantum_foundation.R:279, so this is a lone deviation, not a house style.
findings.impact: `qf_krr_benchmark()` is documented (R/quantum_foundation.R:247-250) as giving "an empirical answer" to whether the quantum-foundation hybrid beats its ancestors, and it tabulates the quantum KRR head-to-head against a ranger baseline. Clamping at 0 means a quantum model with true R-squared of -0.4 (materially worse than predicting the mean) is reported as 0.00, indistinguishable from a model that merely explains nothing. The clamp applies to every row including the baselines, so it compresses exactly the region where the comparison would be most informative. This directly undercuts the "Honestly benchmarked" claim the package makes about its Pillar 4/6 comparisons (R/pillars_roadmap.R:13).
findings.action: Replace the inline computation at R/quantum_foundation.R:277-281 with calls to the existing `edaphos_rmse()` / `edaphos_mae()` / `edaphos_r2()` so the benchmark shares one metric definition with the rest of the package, removing the `max(0, ...)`. Add a test asserting that a deliberately bad predictor yields a negative `r2` in the returned data frame.

findings.title: bhs_fit has no rank check on the model matrix: a constant covariate yields NA rgamma rates (the 2 live WARNINGs) then a cryptic Cholesky death
findings.correction: Mechanism and every behavioural claim CONFIRMED: R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:238 seeds beta from stats::lm.fit (NA on rank-deficient X), the NA reaches rate_s at :302 -> rgamma at :303 and rate_t at :308 -> :309 (exactly the 2 live warnings), validation at :90-106 never checks rank(X), and test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:57-69 is a tautology (`expect_true(is.null(fit) || inherits(fit, "edaphos_bhs"))` at :68). Two line references are wrong: `rhs_w <- (y - as.numeric(X %*% beta)) / tau2` is at :283, not :288 (:288 is the w_cur draw); `.chol_jitter` is defined at :246-256 with the heavy-ridge fallback at :255, not :243-254. The tryCatch spans :61-65, not :61-66.
findings.evidence: Reproduced standalone (no package load) for n=30, X = cbind(1, rep(1,30)): `qr(X)$rank = 1` vs `p = 2`; `stats::lm.fit(X,y)$coefficients` = c(0.1327746, NA). R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:238 uses exactly that as the Gibbs initial value: `beta <- as.numeric(stats::lm.fit(X, y)$coefficients)`. The NA propagates: :288 `rhs_w <- (y - as.numeric(X %*% beta)) / tau2` -> all NA -> :302 `rate_s` NA -> :303 `sigma2 <- 1/stats::rgamma(1, shape=shape_s, rate=NA)` emits WARNING "NAs produced" and returns NaN; :308-309 does the same for tau2 -> WARNING #2. Exactly two warnings, matching the live run at tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:61. On iteration 2 `prec_w` is all-NaN, the 8-step jitter ladder in `.chol_jitter` (:243-254) fails every try, and the final fallback `chol(M + diag(1e-2 * mean(diag(M))))` errors with "the leading minor of order 1 is not positive" (verified). The test at test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:57-69 swallows this with `tryCatch(..., error = function(e) NULL)` at :61-66 and then asserts the tautology `expect_true(is.null(fit) || inherits(fit, "edaphos_bhs"))` at :68 -- satisfied by both branches, so it can never fail. Also note bhs_fit's own validation (:90-106) checks data/formula/coords types and the MCMC schedule but never the rank of X. R/core_utils.R already ships `.stopf` / `.assert_type` for exactly this.
findings.impact: Any user whose design matrix is rank-deficient (a constant covariate, a perfectly collinear pair, a one-level factor after NA dropping) gets 'NAs produced' followed by 'the leading minor of order 1 is not positive' -- with no indication which column is at fault -- from the Pillar 7 flagship sampler. The only test covering the case is a tautology, so the suite records it as passing while emitting the warnings that R CMD check will surface.
findings.action: In R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R after line 130 (`n <- length(y); p <- ncol(X)`) add a rank guard using the existing helper: `if (qr(X)$rank < p) .stopf("design matrix is rank-deficient (rank %d < %d columns).", qr(X)$rank, p, hint = "Drop constant or collinear covariates; aliased column(s): ...")`, naming the aliased columns from `colnames(X)[is.na(stats::lm.fit(X,y)$coefficients)]`. Then rewrite tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:57-69 as `expect_error(bhs_fit(...), "rank-deficient")` and wrap it in `expect_no_warning()` so the 2 'NAs produced' warnings become a regression signal instead of noise.

findings.title: R/foundation_finetune.R:41 makes the whole Pillar-4 fine-tuning API require `reticulate`, which it never uses
findings.correction: none — verified exactly. R/foundation_finetune.R:40-46 is `.ft_require_torch <- function() { if (!requireNamespace("reticulate", quietly = TRUE) || !requireNamespace("torch", quietly = TRUE)) stop("Install the `torch` package (and its MPS / CUDA backend) to use the fine-tuning API.", call. = FALSE) }`; `grep -n reticulate R/foundation_finetune.R` returns the single hit at :41 in a 646-line file; the guard is called at :247, :401, :483, :632 (the four public entry points); reticulate is Suggests-only (DESCRIPTION:64). The masking is confirmed too: tests/testthat/test-foundation-finetune.R:7-12 defines a local `skip_if_no_torch()` that checks only `skip_if_not_installed("torch")` + `torch::torch_is_installed()`, never reticulate, so no test can ever reach the reticulate branch. Severity is honest: a torch-installed, reticulate-free R user — the normal case — gets four documented entry points dead behind an error message that tells them to install what they already have.
findings.evidence: R/foundation_finetune.R:40-46: `.ft_require_torch <- function() { if (!requireNamespace("reticulate", quietly = TRUE) || !requireNamespace("torch", quietly = TRUE)) stop("Install the `torch` package (and its MPS / CUDA backend) to use the fine-tuning API.", call. = FALSE) }`. Line 41 is the ONLY occurrence of the string `reticulate` in the entire 646-line file (`grep -n reticulate R/foundation_finetune.R` -> single hit). The four call sites are the four public entry points: foundation_fit_classifier (guard at :247, defined :233), predict.edaphos_foundation_classifier (:401 / :397), foundation_fit_regressor (:483 / :468), predict.edaphos_foundation_regressor (:632 / :630). `reticulate` is Suggests-only (DESCRIPTION). The bug is masked by the test gate: tests/testthat/test-foundation-finetune.R:7-12 `skip_if_no_torch()` checks only torch + torch_is_installed(), never reticulate, so all 8 blocks in that file skip rather than fail on a torch-full/reticulate-free machine.
findings.impact: On a machine with torch and libtorch correctly installed but no reticulate (the normal case for an R-only user), all four fine-tuning entry points die with an error message that tells the user to install torch -- which they already have. Unfixable by the user without reading the source. Zero tests can catch it.
findings.action: Delete `!requireNamespace("reticulate", quietly = TRUE) ||` from R/foundation_finetune.R:41. Add a torch-free regression test that stubs `requireNamespace` (or uses `local_mocked_bindings`) to assert `.ft_require_torch()` does not consult reticulate.

findings.title: No CI leg has ever executed the torch code paths: 74 test blocks / 223 expectations / ~3,140 LOC unexercised
findings.correction: Structural claims CONFIRMED exactly: 460 test_that blocks, 184 gated (40.0%), 74 torch-gated, 20 qiskit-gated (test-quantum-vqe.R:5-13, test-quantum-v09.R:11-33), 3143 LOC across the 9 torch-only files (exact), TORCH_INSTALL: 0 for all 5 matrix legs, test-coverage.yaml sets no TORCH_INSTALL and there is no .covrignore / codecov.yml. Counts that are wrong: the suite has 1089 expect_ calls (the figure in the audit brief), not 1209, and 197 of them sit in torch-gated blocks, not 223; 20 R/ files reference torch totalling 6275 LOC, not 18 files / 5904 LOC. Line cites drift by one: TORCH_INSTALL is at .github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml:35 (env block :29-35) and setup-r-dependencies at :48-51.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml:29-34 sets `TORCH_INSTALL: 0` for all 5 matrix legs (macos/windows/ubuntu devel+release+oldrel-1) with the comment "CI still exercises ~70 % of the test suite". `r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2` (line 47-50) installs all Suggests, so the R `torch` package IS present but libtorch/Lantern is not, hence `torch::torch_is_installed()` is FALSE and every test gate skips. Parsed gate attribution over tests/testthat: 460 test_that blocks total, 184 gated (40.0%), of which 74 are torch-gated, carrying 223 of the 1209 static expect_ calls (18.4%). A further 20 blocks need Python qiskit (tests/testthat/test-quantum-vqe.R:5-13, test-quantum-v09.R:11-33 -> skip_if_no_qiskit / skip_if_no_aer / skip_if_no_nature) which no leg installs. CI therefore runs ~366/460 blocks (79.6%) and ~931/1209 expectations (77.0%). The torch-only R sources never executed anywhere: R/foundation_moco.R (776 LOC), R/foundation_finetune.R (646), R/temporal_convlstm.R (356), R/pilar9_diffusion_torch.R (265), R/piml_hierarchical.R (263), R/piml_neural_ode.R (224), R/foundation_simclr.R (216), R/pilar8_neural_operators_torch.R (216), R/pilar10_graph_nn_torch.R (181) = 3,143 LOC; 18 R/ files reference torch at all, totalling 5,904 LOC (30% of R/). .github/workflows/test-coverage.yaml does not set TORCH_INSTALL either, and has no .covrignore or codecov.yml, so the badge silently reports these files near 0% with no gate.
findings.impact: Pillars 2 (Neural ODE / hierarchical), 3 (ConvLSTM), 4 (SimCLR/MoCo/fine-tune), 8, 9 and 10 torch backends -- the headline 'disruptive' content and roughly a third of R/ -- have zero regression protection. A refactor that breaks any of them ships green. Findings #2 and #3 below are live proof: both are real defects sitting inside or adjacent to torch-gated code, and neither is detectable by the current CI.
findings.action: Add one CI leg (ubuntu-release) that omits `TORCH_INSTALL: 0` and runs `torch::install_torch()` with a cached ~/.cache/torch (actions/cache keyed on the torch version), so the 74 torch blocks execute at least once per push. Do the same in test-coverage.yaml, or add a .covrignore + codecov.yml `target` so the badge stops averaging in permanently-unexecuted files. Correct the misleading comment at R-CMD-check.yaml:31-33 to state explicitly that no torch code path is covered.

findings.title: Two competing release checklists contradict each other and describe a deploy action the pkgdown workflow does not use; referenced artefacts do not exist
findings.correction: none — the strongest sub-claim checks out: RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:86-92 recommends Pages Source = "GitHub Actions ... uses the pkgdown workflow's deployment artefact directly" and cites "the existing peaceiris/actions-gh-pages step in .github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml", but `grep -rn peaceiris .github/` returns nothing and pkgdown.yaml:59-65 deploys via JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4.5.0 pushing `docs` to branch `gh-pages`, with no upload-pages-artifact/deploy-pages step — so following the "recommended" option yields a permanently empty site. RELEASE.md:63-67 gives the opposite (correct) instruction. RELEASE.md's "at most 24 MB of installed package" vs cran-comments.md:96 "the *hard* limit is 100 MB" confirmed. .gitignore:64-65 and .Rbuildignore:19/:24 confirmed, including that :24 hard-pins the v3.10.0 filename so a v3.11.0 checklist would ship. Duplicate of "Two competing release checklists, one stale, pointing at a tarball path that does not exist".
findings.evidence: Two overlapping documents both claim to list "the four remaining manual actions": RELEASE.md:1 is headed "public-release checklist (v2.9.1)" and RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:1 is headed v3.10.0. They give conflicting Pages instructions: RELEASE.md:63-67 says Source = "Deploy from a branch", branch `gh-pages`; RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:86-92 recommends "**GitHub Actions** (recommended -- uses the pkgdown workflow's deployment artefact directly)" -- which cannot work, because pkgdown.yaml:59-65 pushes to the `gh-pages` branch via `JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4.5.0` and contains no `upload-pages-artifact`/`deploy-pages` steps. The same checklist line 91-92 cites "the existing peaceiris/actions-gh-pages step in `.github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml`" -- that action appears nowhere in the file. They also contradict each other on CRAN limits: RELEASE.md:95 "CRAN's policy requires **at most 24 MB of installed package**" vs cran-comments.md:96 "the *hard* limit is 100 MB". Referenced artefacts are absent: RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:15 `/tmp/edaphos_release_tarballs/edaphos_3.10.0.tar.gz (17 MB)` does not exist; :55 `tools/zenodo_release.zip (22.2 MB, 24 files)` does not exist and is .gitignore'd (.gitignore:64-65). RELEASE.md:17 still says "The badge in README currently resolves to **v0.2.0**". Both files are .Rbuildignore'd (lines 19 and 24), but line 24 hard-pins `^RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3\.10\.0\.md$`, so a v3.11.0 checklist would ship in the tarball.
findings.impact: Following the newer, more confident checklist breaks the docs site (choosing Pages Source = GitHub Actions against a branch-push deploy yields a permanently empty site), and both checklists point at build outputs that were deleted, so the "already built" tarball and Zenodo bundle must be regenerated with no recorded provenance. Because the two files disagree, there is no single authoritative release procedure -- and the release procedure is the one process this project has not yet executed even once.
findings.action: Delete RELEASE.md (or reduce it to a pointer) and keep one un-versioned `RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md`, then generalise .Rbuildignore:24 to `^RELEASE-CHECKLIST.*\.md$`. Correct RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:86-92 to the single working option (branch `gh-pages`, folder `/`) and fix the peaceiris/JamesIves reference at :91-92. Drop the invented "24 MB" and "100 MB" CRAN figures from RELEASE.md:95 and cran-comments.md:96 in favour of the actual 5 MB soft target the note is arguing against. Make artefact generation a step in the checklist rather than a claim that it already happened.

findings.title: 33 of 43 NEWS.md releases have no git tag and there is no release-automation workflow, contradicting CONTRIBUTING's tagging promise
findings.correction: The count is 32, not 33: NEWS.md has 43 `^# edaphos` sections and 11 of them are tagged (0.8.0, 0.9.0, 1.0.0, 1.1.0, 1.2.0, 1.3.0, 1.3.1, 1.4.0, 1.5.0, 1.6.0, 3.10.0), leaving 32 untagged (1.7.0 ... 3.9.0). Everything else confirmed exactly: 18 tags with the v1.6.0 -> v3.10.0 jump, CONTRIBUTING.md:87 "Every release gets a git tag (`vX.Y.Z`) and a NEWS.md entry.", 3 workflows only, pkgdown.yaml:14-15 the sole release trigger.
findings.evidence: `git tag --list` returns 18 tags: v0.1.0 ... v1.6.0 (17 consecutive), then jumps straight to v3.10.0. NEWS.md has 43 `^# edaphos` sections. Comparing them, 33 NEWS versions have no corresponding tag: 1.7.0, 1.7.1, 1.7.2, 1.8.0, 1.8.1, 1.8.2, 1.9.0, 1.9.1, 1.9.2, 2.0.0, 2.1.0, 2.1.3, 2.2.0, 2.2.1, 2.3.0, 2.4.0, 2.5.0, 2.6.0, 2.7.0, 2.8.0, 2.9.0, 2.9.1, 3.0.0, 3.1.0 ... 3.9.0. CONTRIBUTING.md:87 states "Every release gets a git tag (`vX.Y.Z`) and a NEWS.md entry." `ls .github/workflows/` shows exactly three files -- no release/tag automation exists; the only tag-adjacent trigger is `release: types: [published]` at pkgdown.yaml:14-15, which can never fire for a release that was never tagged or published. Compounding this: NEWS.md's newest section is 3.10.0 (line 1) with no 3.11.0 entry, while HEAD~1 (7400a2c) is titled "feat(v3.11.0)" and DESCRIPTION:3 still reads 3.10.0 -- so three sources disagree about the current version.
findings.impact: There is no way to reproduce, diff, or archive any release between v1.6.0 and v3.10.0 -- 33 documented releases are unrecoverable as source states. README.md:8 links a `GitHub release` badge and README.md:9 links `/releases/tag/v3.10.0`; the Zenodo-per-release archival model described in README.md:1722-1724 and RELEASE.md:15-53 depends on tags/releases that mostly do not exist. A user reading "v3.5.0 added the RcppArmadillo Gibbs port" (cran-comments.md:119-121) cannot check out that state.
findings.action: Backfill tags where the corresponding commits are identifiable (`git log --oneline --grep='v3\\.' ` on the version-bump commits), or state plainly in CONTRIBUTING.md:82-87 that only milestone versions are tagged. Add a release workflow triggered on `push: tags: ['v*']` that runs R CMD check, builds the tarball, and creates the GitHub release with the matching NEWS.md section as the body -- that also makes pkgdown.yaml:14-15's `release: published` trigger meaningful. Add a CI assertion that DESCRIPTION Version equals the newest `# edaphos` heading in NEWS.md; that single check would have caught the 3.10.0/3.11.0 split.

findings.title: Dockerfile is not a reproducibility artefact: builds from GitHub main, unpinned libtorch, R 4.4.1 in no CI leg, v2.1.0 metadata, missing Suggests
findings.correction: Nearly all verified: Dockerfile:66-70 `ARG EDAPHOS_REF=main` + `remotes::install_github(..., dependencies = TRUE, upgrade = 'never')` with no COPY/ADD anywhere, which does render .dockerignore inert; :57-58 unpinned `torch::install_torch(timeout = 600)` against the "byte-reproducible" claim at :41-42; :22 `FROM rocker/geospatial:4.4.1`; stale v2.1.0 at :1, :9, :15, :19, :28 and the RSPM pin `jammy/2026-04-23` described as "the date of the edaphos v2.1.0 release" while DESCRIPTION:3 is 3.10.0; :45-54 installs exactly 38 packages and omits spBayes, ecmwfr, geobr with reticulate commented at :62, against the header claim at :5-6; :72-76 pre-fetches moco-v1. cran-comments.md:15 does list Docker as a test environment. ONE CLAIM IS WRONG: "R 4.4.1 … appears in no leg of the R-CMD-check matrix (release / devel / oldrel-1)" — oldrel-1 resolves dynamically and currently lands on R 4.4.x, so 4.4 is in fact covered; the honest complaint is that the pin is arbitrary and unaligned, not absent. Severity deflated: nothing here affects the package, the tarball, or any user who does not run `docker build`.
findings.evidence: Dockerfile:66-70 `ARG EDAPHOS_REF=main` + `remotes::install_github('HugoMachadoRodrigues/edaphos', ref = '${EDAPHOS_REF}', dependencies = TRUE, upgrade = 'never')` -- the image never installs the source in the build context, which makes `.dockerignore` (all 14 lines) inert and makes the image a moving target rather than a snapshot. Dockerfile:57-58 `torch::install_torch(timeout = 600)` downloads libtorch at an unpinned version over the network, defeating the "byte-reproducible" claim at Dockerfile:41-42. Dockerfile:22 `FROM rocker/geospatial:4.4.1` pins R 4.4.1, which appears in no leg of the R-CMD-check matrix (R-CMD-check.yaml:23-27: release / devel / oldrel-1) and differs from the R 4.5.3 claimed in cran-comments.md:4. Stale version metadata: Dockerfile:1 "(v2.1.0)", :9 `docker build -t edaphos:2.1.0`, :15, :19, :28 `image.version="2.1.0"` and :41-43 the RSPM snapshot `.../jammy/2026-04-23` described as "the date of the edaphos v2.1.0 release" -- package Version is 3.10.0 (DESCRIPTION:3). Dockerfile:45-54 installs 38 packages but omits `spBayes` (Pilar 7 alternative backend, DESCRIPTION:71), `ecmwfr` (:48), `geobr` (:50) and `reticulate` (commented out at :62), despite the header at Dockerfile:5-6 claiming "all Suggests needed to run every vignette without network access". `remotes::install_github(dependencies = TRUE)` does not build vignettes, so no vignette is rendered in the image. Dockerfile:72-76 pre-downloads `edaphos-cerrado-moco-v1` while HEAD~1 (7400a2c) is "hand-off package for the v1.3.2 MoCo v2 publish pipeline" and .gitignore:49 tracks `tools/pretrain/edaphos-cerrado-moco-v2/`.
findings.impact: cran-comments.md:15 lists "Docker (Rocker/geospatial): see Dockerfile in repo root" as a test environment, but the image tests whatever is on GitHub main at build time with an unpinned libtorch on an R version nothing else in the project uses -- so it validates nothing about the tarball being submitted. A reviewer (rOpenSci, per RELEASE.md:108) following the documented `docker build` gets an image tagged 2.1.0 containing 3.10.0-or-later code, missing four Suggests, with no rendered vignettes and MoCo v1 weights.
findings.action: Switch to `COPY . /src` + `R -e 'remotes::install_local("/src", dependencies = TRUE, build_vignettes = TRUE)'` so the image is built from the tree that `.dockerignore` describes. Pin libtorch by setting `TORCH_HOME`/version env or by installing a fixed torch release. Bump the base to the R version in the CI `release` leg and sync all `2.1.0` strings (Dockerfile:1, 9, 15, 19, 28) to the DESCRIPTION Version, ideally via `ARG EDAPHOS_VERSION`. Add spBayes/ecmwfr/geobr/reticulate to line 45-54 or correct the claim at Dockerfile:5-6. Update the pre-downloaded encoder to the v2 identifier. Add a `docker build` job to CI (it can be `workflow_dispatch`-only) so this file stops rotting.

findings.title: CI builds vignettes, but 3 of 14 self-truncate to a one-line stub without libtorch -- and CONTRIBUTING tells contributors to skip vignette building entirely
findings.correction: The asymmetry is real: R-CMD-check.yaml:56 `build_args: 'c("--no-manual","--compact-vignettes=gs+qpdf")'` omits --no-build-vignettes, while CONTRIBUTING.md:44-45, .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md:23 and cran-comments.md:4-8/:24-26 all use the weaker `--no-build-vignettes` gate, and a `knit_exit()` is a successful knit that CI cannot detect. But the count is wrong: only TWO vignettes stub out on missing libtorch — vignettes/pilar3-4d-soc.Rmd:85-91 and vignettes/pilar4-simclr-embeddings.Rmd:67-74. vignettes/pilar2-piml-profile.Rmd does NOT: :76-79 sets `.torch_ok` and uses it as a per-chunk `eval=` flag at :191, :202, :228 and :297 — the graceful degradation pattern — and its only `knit_exit` (:80) is on `aqp`. The other cited truncations (dagitty at pilar1-causal.Rmd:61, igraph :171, sp at pilar5-active-learning.Rmd:108, aqp) also do not fire on CI, because r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies installs Suggests; libtorch is the only missing piece. articles/pilar3-4d-real.Rmd is not in the tarball (.Rbuildignore:21).
findings.evidence: R-CMD-check.yaml:53-56 passes `build_args: 'c("--no-manual","--compact-vignettes=gs+qpdf")'`, which omits `--no-build-vignettes`, so `R CMD build` renders all 14 `vignettes/*.Rmd`. Three abort in their setup chunk when libtorch is absent -- which is always, per finding 1: vignettes/pilar2-piml-profile.Rmd:76-80, vignettes/pilar3-4d-soc.Rmd:85-91 (`knitr::knit_exit("torch runtime (libtorch) not available — skipping vignette.")`), vignettes/pilar4-simclr-embeddings.Rmd:67-74. Three more truncate on other Suggests: vignettes/pilar1-causal.Rmd:61 (dagitty), :171 (igraph), vignettes/pilar5-active-learning.Rmd:108 (sp), vignettes/pilar2-piml-profile.Rmd:80 (aqp). articles/pilar3-4d-real.Rmd:67 likewise. Meanwhile CONTRIBUTING.md:44-45 instructs `devtools::check(args = c("--no-manual", "--no-build-vignettes"))  # 0/0/0` and the PR template line 23 repeats `devtools::check(args = c("--no-manual", "--no-build-vignettes"))`. cran-comments.md:4-8 and :24-26 also report the 0/0/0 result as obtained "with `--no-build-vignettes`".
findings.impact: The tarball CI produces -- and the vignettes CRAN would ship and pkgdown would publish -- contain three stub articles that read "torch runtime (libtorch) not available — skipping vignette" instead of the Pilar 2/3/4 methods papers the README advertises. Nothing in CI detects this, because a `knit_exit()` is a successful knit. Separately, the documented local gate is strictly weaker than the CI gate, so a contributor can satisfy every PR-template checkbox and still push a red build; the maintainer's own 0/0/0 claims were produced under the weaker gate.
findings.action: Add a post-build assertion step to R-CMD-check.yaml that greps the rendered `inst/doc/*.html` for the knit_exit sentinel strings and fails if any vignette is a stub, or gate that assertion to the new libtorch leg from finding 1. Align CONTRIBUTING.md:44-45 and .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md:23 with the actual CI invocation (drop `--no-build-vignettes`, or state explicitly that CI is stricter). Update cran-comments.md:24-26 to state which vignettes are stubs and why.

findings.title: Distribution metadata is 9 minor versions stale: CITATION.cff says 2.1.0, README says 2.8.0, .zenodo.json has no version at all
findings.evidence: DESCRIPTION:3 `Version: 3.10.0`. CITATION.cff:109-110 `version: "2.1.0"` / `date-released: "2026-04-23"` -- the same date the Dockerfile:43 RSPM snapshot calls "the date of the edaphos v2.1.0 release". README.md's citation block gives "(Version 2.8.0)" in the prose citation and `version = {2.8.0}` in the BibTeX entry. `.zenodo.json` (6,205 bytes) contains no `version` key at all (`grep -n 'version' .zenodo.json` -> no match). There is no `inst/CITATION` (`ls inst/CITATION` -> no such file), so `citation("edaphos")` falls back to the DESCRIPTION-derived default -- which README describes as "An auto-generated citation is also available in R". README.md's roadmap table still lists `v3.0.0 | CRAN + rOpenSci submission | 📝` as pending even though the package is at 3.10.0. No workflow validates or syncs any of these (only 3 workflows exist).
findings.impact: CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json are the files GitHub's "Cite this repository" widget and Zenodo's GitHub integration read. Anyone citing edaphos today from the repo UI cites version 2.1.0 released 2026-04-23; anyone copying the README BibTeX cites 2.8.0; the actual code is 3.10.0 (or 3.11.0 per HEAD~1). A Zenodo deposition driven by `.zenodo.json` would carry no version field, so the concept DOI cannot distinguish releases -- exactly the problem RELEASE.md:15-18 sets out to solve.
findings.action: Update CITATION.cff:109-110 and the README citation block to the DESCRIPTION Version, add a `"version"` key to .zenodo.json, and add a CI step (or a `usethis`-style helper in the release checklist) that asserts DESCRIPTION Version == CITATION.cff version == .zenodo.json version == newest NEWS.md heading. Add a `cff-validator` action so a malformed CITATION.cff is caught. Correct the stale `v3.0.0 CRAN + rOpenSci` roadmap row in README.md.

findings.title: Chunk option in pilar4-simclr vignette calls `reticulate::` unguarded with broken `&&`/`||` precedence -- hard error in exactly the Docker configuration
findings.evidence: vignettes/pilar4-simclr-embeddings.Rmd:361: ```{r tile-train, eval=requireNamespace("torch", quietly = TRUE) && reticulate::py_available() || .torch_ok}```. R parses this as `(requireNamespace("torch") && reticulate::py_available()) || .torch_ok`. The setup chunk at :67-74 already `knit_exit()`s unless `.torch_ok` is TRUE, so by line 361 `requireNamespace("torch")` is always TRUE and `reticulate::py_available()` is always evaluated -- while the `|| .torch_ok` tail makes the whole expression identical to `.torch_ok`, i.e. the reticulate branch is dead weight that can only crash. If `reticulate` is not installed, chunk-option evaluation raises "there is no package called 'reticulate'" and the knit fails outright rather than skipping. Every other reticulate use in the repo is correctly guarded: vignettes/pilar6-quantum.Rmd:260, :267, :300, :310, :355, :484 all lead with `requireNamespace("reticulate", quietly = TRUE) &&`, and R/quantum_vqe.R:37-43 `.qk_require()` checks `requireNamespace("reticulate")` before `py_module_available()`. Dockerfile:60-63 deliberately does NOT install reticulate ("Skip by default to keep the image small; uncomment if you need VQE") while Dockerfile:57-58 does install torch + libtorch. cran-comments.md:49-52 asserts "Every Suggests is wrapped in `requireNamespace(..., quietly = TRUE)` inside the code that uses it."
findings.impact: The single environment where the torch vignettes are supposed to render fully -- the Docker image -- is the one environment where this line hard-errors: torch present, reticulate absent. So `docker build` followed by a vignette rebuild cannot reproduce the Pilar 4 article. The same combination can occur on a CRAN check machine that installs torch but not reticulate, producing a vignette-build ERROR rather than a graceful skip, and falsifying the cran-comments.md:49-52 claim.
findings.action: Replace the chunk option at vignettes/pilar4-simclr-embeddings.Rmd:361 with `eval=.torch_ok` (semantically identical, no reticulate dependency), or if the Python path is genuinely intended write `eval=.torch_ok && requireNamespace("reticulate", quietly = TRUE) && reticulate::py_available()`. Add `reticulate` to the Dockerfile install list, or leave it out and confirm the vignette renders. Add a grep-based lint (or an explicit item in the release checklist) for `[a-zA-Z]+::` appearing in a chunk option without a preceding `requireNamespace` in the same expression.

findings.title: cran-comments.md test-suite and install-size figures are contradicted by the tree they describe
findings.correction: none — every number checks out: 460 test_that / 1089 expect_ measured; the single Ollama-shaped skip claim verified (only tests/testthat/test-quantum-kernel-rcpp.R:46 `skip_on_cran()` matches `skip_on_cran|skip_if_offline|skip_on_ci` across all of tests/testthat/); benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7.rds = 1,959,632 B = 1,913.70 KB vs the claimed 0.7 MB; benchmark_wosis_6pilar.rds = 4,640,252 B = 4,531.50 KB, matching its claimed 4.5 MB; causal_cerrado_real.rds = 63,521 B = 62.03 KB vs the claimed 1.6 MB; the three omitted files are case_cerrado_results.rds 1,434.75 KB, capstone_native_calibration.rds 741.16 KB, capstone_campaign_results.rds 543.31 KB; `du -sh inst/extdata` = 9.6 MB. Note this is a strict subset of finding 7 with better-behaved arithmetic (it does not overstate the p4_p5_p7 discrepancy) and without finding 7's false Matrix sub-claim.
findings.evidence: cran-comments.md:30-31 "`devtools::test()` -- **1 345 unit tests**, 0 failures, 4 warnings, 2 skips" and :33-35 "the 4 warnings are documented cosmetic stats::sweep recycling on odd column counts (Pilar 8); the 2 skips are LLM-benchmark tests that require a live Ollama instance." The tree contains 460 `test_that` blocks / 1089 `expect_` calls across 69 files, and the live run yields 1022 passing expectations, **109** skips (74 torch, 22 dagitty, 9 bnlearn, 3 dbarts, 1 other), 2 errors and 2 warnings -- the warnings are "NAs produced" from `bhs_fit` at tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:61 (Pilar **7**, not Pilar 8, and not sweep-recycling). Only one test in the whole suite is Ollama/network-shaped (`grep -rn 'skip_on_cran\|skip_if_offline\|skip_on_ci' tests/testthat/` returns exactly one hit, tests/testthat/test-quantum-kernel-rcpp.R:46 `skip_on_cran()`), so the "2 skips ... live Ollama" explanation cannot be right. Install-size figures at cran-comments.md:70-79 are also wrong: it claims extdata is "~8 MB" with `benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7.rds 0.7 MB` (actual 1,913.70 KB), `benchmark_wosis_6pilar.rds 4.5 MB` (actual 4,531.50 KB, correct) and `causal_cerrado_real.rds 1.6 MB` (actual 62.03 KB), and omits the three next-largest files entirely: `case_cerrado_results.rds` 1,434.75 KB, `capstone_native_calibration.rds` 741.16 KB, `capstone_campaign_results.rds` 543.31 KB. `du -sh inst/extdata` = 9.6 MB.
findings.impact: cran-comments.md is the document a CRAN volunteer reads alongside the tarball. Its headline test figure is off by a factor and its skip explanation is wrong, which invites the exact question it was written to pre-empt ("why are 109 tests skipped?"). Its install-size justification -- the section arguing for an exception to the 5 MB soft cap -- misstates two of the four file sizes it enumerates and omits 2.7 MB of the payload, so the argument does not add up against the directory it describes. This is the kind of arithmetic reviewers check.
findings.action: Regenerate cran-comments.md:28-35 from an actual `devtools::test()` run, reporting test_that blocks vs expectations vs skips separately and grouping the 109 skips by the optional dependency that causes them (that framing also supports the Suggests table at :54-65). Regenerate :70-79 from `ls -l inst/extdata/`, listing every file over 500 KB. Since these numbers must be re-derived every release, add the two commands to the release checklist rather than hand-editing prose.

findings.title: No CI leg ever installs libtorch: 25% of R/ and 70 of 460 test blocks are unreachable in all three workflows
findings.correction: Facts confirmed: .github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml:35 `TORCH_INSTALL: 0`; `grep -rn install_torch` over the repo hits only Dockerfile:58, README.md:343 and R/piml_neural_ode.R:13 — nothing in .github/; test-coverage.yaml and pkgdown.yaml set no torch env at all; total `test_that` blocks = 460; helper-torch.R:7-12 plus the 12 local redefinitions double-gate on the Lantern probe so the blocks skip regardless. Downgraded from blocker because this is a disclosed, deliberate trade-off rather than an oversight — R-CMD-check.yaml:32-34 carries the rationale inline ("Skip torch runtime download on CI ... CI still exercises ~70 % of the test suite"), the code degrades gracefully (all guards are requireNamespace-wrapped), and Dockerfile:57-58 does provide a libtorch environment. It is a real verification gap for six pillars' torch backends, not a broken build.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml:32-35 sets `TORCH_INSTALL: 0` with the comment "Skip torch runtime download on CI ... CI still exercises ~70 % of the test suite". `test-coverage.yaml` and `pkgdown.yaml` never install libtorch either (no TORCH_INSTALL, no `torch::install_torch()` step anywhere: grep for `install_torch` matches only Dockerfile:58). Every torch test is double-gated by a runtime probe, so it skips regardless of whether the R `torch` package installs: tests/testthat/helper-torch.R:7-12 (`.skip_if_no_torch()` -> `if (!isTRUE(torch::torch_is_installed())) skip("Lantern (libtorch) backend is not installed.")`), plus locally redefined equivalents at tests/testthat/test-foundation.R:1-4, test-temporal.R:1-4, test-piml-neural.R:1-4, test-foundation-moco.R:1-5, test-piml-hierarchical.R:1-4, test-foundation-tiles.R:2-6, test-foundation-weights.R:3-8. Count of gated blocks: 70 (test-foundation-moco.R 9, test-foundation-finetune.R 8, test-temporal.R 7, test-foundation-posterior.R 5, test-foundation-embed-coords.R 4, test-pilar10-torch.R 4, test-temporal-posterior.R 4, + 12 more files) out of 460 total `test_that` blocks. Torch-backed source LOC: `wc -l` gives 4,990 across R/foundation_moco.R (776), R/foundation_finetune.R (646), R/foundation_tiles.R (416), R/foundation_embed_coords.R (372), R/temporal_convlstm.R (356), R/foundation_weights.R (344), R/temporal_posterior.R (272), R/pilar9_diffusion_torch.R (265), R/piml_hierarchical.R (263), R/foundation_posterior.R (242), R/piml_neural_ode.R (224), R/foundation_simclr.R (216), R/pilar8_neural_operators_torch.R (216), R/piml_neural_ode_ensemble.R (201), R/pilar10_graph_nn_torch.R (181) = 25.3% of the 19,700 LOC in R/.
findings.impact: Six of the ten advertised pillars (2 Physics-Informed ML, 3 4D Pedometry, 4 Foundation Models, 8 Neural Operators, 9 Diffusion, 10 GAT) have their torch backends verified only on the maintainer's laptop. A green R-CMD-check badge on README.md:5 certifies nothing about them across macOS/Windows/Linux or R devel/oldrel. The recent MPS/CUDA device-placement fix (HEAD, 272b378 "fix(moco): resume on MPS / CUDA") is precisely the class of bug CI exists to catch and precisely the class CI cannot see. Any torch-API break in an upstream release lands silently.
findings.action: Add a sixth matrix leg (ubuntu-latest, R release) that sets `TORCH_INSTALL: 1` and runs `Rscript -e 'torch::install_torch()'` after setup-r-dependencies, with a cache keyed on the torch version (~/.cache/torch or the libtorch install dir). Mark it `continue-on-error: false` but exclude it from the required-checks set initially so a flaky 1 GB download does not block PRs. As a cheap intermediate step, add a `torch-smoke` job that installs libtorch and runs only the 20 torch test files via `testthat::test_dir(filter = ...)`.

findings.title: Pillars 8/9/10 default backend="r" never trains the architecture it is named after, while DESCRIPTION/README mark them "implemented"
findings.correction: The code claims are confirmed and in one place worse than stated. R/pilar8_neural_operators.R:245-258 updates only `W_out` (`W_out <- W_out - lr * grad_W_out`) — so its own comment at :230-235 ("we only update W_in, W_out, b_out") overstates what happens: `W_in` and `b_out` are never touched. R/pilar9_diffusion_models.R:242-246 updates only `net$W3`/`net$b3`. R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:249 calls `forward_embed()` once before the loop and :260-270 updates only `W_head`/`b_head`; `a_list` (the GAT attention parameters) is never updated anywhere. But the disclosure claim is REFUTED: "the honest label appears only in one of the three @param texts" is false — all three carry it (pilar8:93 "pure-R ELM-style", pilar9:158 "ELM-style MLP denoiser", pilar10:180 "ELM-style"), so every user-facing Rd page for no_fno_fit/dm_fit/gnn_fit says so, and it is also in the file header R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:26, README.md:235 and NEWS.md:857/:937/:974. The genuinely unlabelled one is `no_deeponet_fit` (pilar8:391, "`"r"` (default)" with no qualifier). Remaining real gaps: DESCRIPTION:21-25 and the README ✅ pillar table make unqualified architecture claims, "ELM-style" is jargon that does not convey "the spectral/attention layers are never trained", and pilar8's code contradicts its own comment.
findings.evidence:
R/pilar8_neural_operators.R:230-235 (inside no_fno_fit, backend="r" default): "for the full pure-R training we only update W_in, W_out, b_out -- the FNO spectral layers are kept at initialisation (Fourier featurisation is a hard task for a finite-difference optimiser)". The loop at :245-258 in fact computes only `grad_W_out` and updates only `W_out <- W_out - lr * grad_W_out` (:256) — W_in and b_out are never touched either, so ONE width x 1 vector is trained.
R/pilar9_diffusion_models.R:224-227 (dm_fit, backend="r" default): "Simple SGD on last layer only (W3, b3) ... akin to ELM-style training; Huang et al. 2006"; loop at :242-246 updates only `net$W3` and `net$b3`.
R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:227-247 + :249: `emb <- forward_embed()` is called ONCE, before the training loop, with randomly initialised `W_list`/`a_list`; the loop at :260-270 updates only `W_head`/`b_head`. The GAT attention parameters `a_list` are never updated anywhere in the file.
Contrast: DESCRIPTION:21-25 advertises "Neural Operators (DeepONet and Fourier Neural Operator) ... Diffusion Models (DDPM) ... Graph Attention Networks on k-NN co-location graphs"; README.md:375-381 pillar table marks every pillar "✅". R/pilar8_neural_operators.R:93-94 roxygen: "@param backend `"r"` (default, pure-R ELM-style)" — the honest label appears only in one of the three @param texts, not in DESCRIPTION, README, or pillars_roadmap.R.
findings.impact: A reader installing edaphos and calling `no_fno_fit()`, `dm_fit()` or `gnn_fit()` with defaults gets a random-feature ELM with a trained linear readout, not an FNO / DDPM / GAT. Any vignette figure, benchmark table or paper claim produced on the default backend is a claim about random projections, not about the cited architectures (Ho et al. 2020, Velickovic et al. 2018, Li et al. 2021). Since torch is only in Suggests (DESCRIPTION:76) and is not installed on CRAN check machines or in this repo's local environment, the default path is the ONLY path most users and reviewers will ever execute. This is the single highest reputational risk in the package.
findings.action: Either (a) rename the pure-R paths to what they are — `backend = "elm"` / `"random-features"` — and state in DESCRIPTION, README.md:375-381 and R/pillars_roadmap.R that pillars 8/9/10 require torch for the full architecture; or (b) implement backprop for the frozen layers. Option (a) is hours of edits and is honest; option (b) is weeks. Do NOT submit to CRAN/rOpenSci with the current wording. At minimum, add a `message()` at R/pilar8_neural_operators.R:106, R/pilar9_diffusion_models.R:171 and R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:193 when `backend == "r"` naming the limitation.

findings.title: Off-by-one in the RcppArmadillo BHS backend biases w_post_mean, silently corrupting every predict.edaphos_bhs() for backend="rcpp"
findings.evidence:
R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:276 `for (iter in seq_len(nmcmc))` — iter is 1-based; :314 `if (iter > burn) w_mean <- w_mean + w_cur / (nmcmc - burn)` accumulates exactly (nmcmc - burn) terms over a divisor of (nmcmc - burn). Correct.
src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:103 `for (int iter = 0; iter < nmcmc; ++iter)` — iter is 0-based; :132-133 `if (iter > burn) { w_mean += w_cur / static_cast<double>(nmcmc - burn); }` accumulates only (nmcmc - burn - 1) terms over the same divisor, and drops the draw at 0-based index `burn`.
Proof the intended convention is `>=`: the thinning loop 7 lines below, src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:139 `for (int it = burn; it < nmcmc; it += thin)`, correctly STARTS at 0-based `burn` to mirror R's 1-based `seq(burn + 1L, nmcmc, by = thin)` (R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:318). So the same function uses two different post-burn conventions 7 lines apart.
The corrupted value is load-bearing: R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:389-391 `w_new_mean <- as.numeric(t(R_cross) %*% R_tr_inv %*% object$w_post_mean)` feeds the mean of every kriging draw at :394.
No test detects it: tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-rcpp.R:37-56 ("backend = 'rcpp' vs 'gibbs': same posterior MEANS within 0.2") compares only `mean(fit$beta_draws[, "x"])`. `w_post_mean` is never compared across backends anywhere in tests/.
findings.impact: Silent numerical divergence between two backends the code and comments claim are equivalent. src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:14-15 asserts "the posterior chain is statistically equivalent up to RNG-draw order" and R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:270-272 claims the marginals are "bit-for-bit identical ... see tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-fastpath.R" — both false for w_post_mean, and unverified by any test.
findings.action: Change src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:132 from `if (iter > burn)` to `if (iter >= burn)`. Then add a test to tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-rcpp.R asserting `expect_equal(fit_r$w_post_mean, fit_cpp$w_post_mean, tolerance = <MCMC noise>)` and a direct assertion that the accumulation count equals `nmcmc - burn` (e.g. run with nmcmc=11, burn=10 and check the result equals the single retained w draw). Also soften the false equivalence claims at src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:14-15 and R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:270-272, which contradict tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-rcpp.R:38-40 ("We don't expect bit-equivalence").

findings.title: gnn_embed() returns a different column count per backend and its documented @return is wrong for backend="torch"
findings.correction: none — R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:288-289 documents "@return An `(n, hidden * n_heads)` matrix"; the pure-R path honours it (`emb_dim <- hidden * n_heads` at :225, `h <- do.call(cbind, head_outs)` at :243); the torch path does not (R/pilar10_graph_nn_torch.R:87-89 `curr <- if (concat_l) hidden * n_heads else hidden`, with `emb_dim = ncol(emb_mat)` recorded at :178), and tests/testthat/test-pilar10-torch.R:57-69 pins the divergence with `expect_equal(ncol(emb), 4L)` for hidden = 4, n_heads = 4 plus the comment "# hidden only (mean-pool final head)". Both backends share class `edaphos_gnn_gat` and the bare accessor `gnn_embed()` at :291-294.
