Downgraded one notch: the main downstream consumer (`qf_krr_on_gat_embeddings`, R/bridges_structure_v3.R:196) reduces `emb` to `n_pcs` principal components and so tolerates either width — the concrete harm is a wrong Rd page, not a runtime break.
findings.evidence:
R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:289 roxygen: "@return An `(n, hidden * n_heads)` matrix -- one row per node." The pure-R path honours this: :225 `emb_dim <- hidden * n_heads`, and multi-head outputs are concatenated at :243 `h <- do.call(cbind, head_outs)`.
The torch path does not. tests/testthat/test-pilar10-torch.R:57-69 ("torch GAT handles multi-head concatenation correctly") fits with `hidden = 4L, n_heads = 4L` and asserts `expect_equal(ncol(emb), 4L)` with the comment "# hidden only (mean-pool final head)" — i.e. 4, not hidden * n_heads = 16.
Both paths return objects of the same S3 class `edaphos_gnn_gat` (R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:284, and the torch constructor in R/pilar10_graph_nn_torch.R:111+), and `gnn_embed()` (:291-294) is a bare `object$emb` accessor with no shape normalisation.
Downstream consumer: R/bridges_structure_v3.R:196 `qf_krr_on_gat_embeddings(gnn_fit, y, ...)` reduces `emb` to `n_pcs` principal components used as QUBITS, and R/bridges_structure_v3.R:226 prints `ncol(x$gnn_fit$emb)` as "GAT emb_dim".
findings.impact: Two backends share one S3 class, one accessor and one Rd page while returning incompatible shapes. The Rd page shipped to users is wrong for one of the two backends, and the divergence is documented only in a test comment. Everything downstream of gnn_embed() — two of the six advertised v3.0.0 cross-pillar bridges — is backend-sensitive in an undocumented way.
findings.action: Pick one contract. Simplest: make the torch path concatenate the final layer's heads so both return (n, hidden * n_heads), matching R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:289; otherwise change the roxygen @return to document the per-backend shape explicitly and record `emb_dim` in both fit objects. Either way add a test in tests/testthat/test-pilar10-gat.R that fits both backends with the same hidden/n_heads and asserts `ncol(gnn_embed(fit_r)) == ncol(gnn_embed(fit_t))`.

findings.title: Rank-deficient design matrix poisons the entire BHS Gibbs chain to NA on iteration 1, then hard-errors — and the test's own comment about it is wrong
findings.correction: none of substance — the whole propagation chain is verified line by line: R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:238 unguarded `beta <- as.numeric(stats::lm.fit(X, y)$coefficients)`; :283 `rhs_w`, :286 `mu_w`, :288 `w_cur`, :302 `rate_s`, :303 first `rgamma`, :306 `resid`, :309 second `rgamma` — matching the two live "NAs produced" warnings; `.chol_jitter` at :246-256 with the unguarded final fallback `chol(M + diag(1e-2 * mean(diag(M)), nrow(M)))` at :255 that throws once `sigma2` is NA at :280. The ordering critique is correct and is the finding's best point: the w-update at :277-288 consumes `beta` before the beta-update at :290-298, so the test's comment at tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:66-67 ("NA beta from lm.fit init is OK -- Gibbs will re-sample") is factually false, and the `tryCatch(..., error = function(e) NULL)` + `expect_true(is.null(fit) || inherits(fit, "edaphos_bhs"))` at :57-69 passes either way. Minor: the rcpp analogue is src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:91 (`arma::vec beta = arma::solve(X, y);`), not :93, and arma::solve on a rank-deficient X warns/throws rather than yielding NA, so that failure mode differs. Severity deflated: the outcome is two warnings plus a loud error, not silently wrong inference, on a degenerate input.
findings.evidence:
R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:238 `beta <- as.numeric(stats::lm.fit(X, y)$coefficients)` — `lm.fit` returns NA for aliased columns of a rank-deficient X and there is no `is.na()` guard.
Propagation, all in the same function: :283 `rhs_w <- (y - as.numeric(X %*% beta)) / tau2` → all-NA because `X %*% c(b0, NA)` is NA; :286 `mu_w` NA; :288 `w_cur` NA; :302 `rate_s <- prior_ig_b + 0.5 * as.numeric(crossprod(w_cur, Rinv %*% w_cur))` NA → :303 `stats::rgamma(1, shape = shape_s, rate = rate_s)` returns NA with warning "NAs produced"; :306 `resid` NA → :309 second `rgamma` → second "NAs produced". That is exactly the 2 warnings observed at tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:61.
Iteration 2 then has `sigma2 = NA`, so :280 `prec_w <- Rinv * (1 / sigma2)` is all-NA, `.chol_jitter` (:246-256) exhausts its 8 jitter retries and its unguarded final fallback `chol(M + diag(1e-2 * mean(diag(M)), nrow(M)))` at :255 throws.
The guarding test is tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:57-69, which wraps the call in `tryCatch(..., error = function(e) NULL)` and asserts `expect_true(is.null(fit) || inherits(fit, "edaphos_bhs"))` — it passes either way. Its comment at :66-67 states "NA beta from lm.fit init is OK -- Gibbs will re-sample", which is factually wrong: the w-update at :277-288 consumes beta BEFORE the beta-update at :290-298, so the chain is already NA by the time beta would be re-drawn.
The rcpp backend has the analogous unguarded init at src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:93 `arma::vec beta = arma::solve(X, y);`.
findings.impact: A common, benign data condition produces two stray warnings plus a cryptic linear-algebra error from three frames deep, with no indication that the cause was a collinear covariate. This is precisely the class of failure the v3.8.0 `.stopf()`/hint machinery was added to eliminate — and `bhs_fit` is the one function that already uses `.assert_type` (:91-100), so the omission is inconsistent within a single function body.
findings.action: At R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:238, detect rank deficiency and fail loudly: `qrX <- qr(X); if (qrX$rank < ncol(X)) .stopf("design matrix is rank-deficient (rank %d < %d columns).", qrX$rank, ncol(X), hint = "Drop collinear or zero-variance covariates from the formula.")`. As a belt-and-braces fix also add `beta[!is.finite(beta)] <- 0` and mirror the rank check before src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:93. Then rewrite tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:57-69 to assert the specific error with `expect_error(..., regexp = "rank-deficient")` instead of accepting both outcomes, and delete the incorrect comment at :66-67.

findings.title: Twelve copies of skip_if_no_torch() in three divergent flavours, orphaning the helper-torch.R that was added to replace them
findings.correction: none on the counts — I reproduced them exactly: helper-torch.R:7 defines `.skip_if_no_torch()` with the header rationale at :1-6, used at 18 call sites across 7 files; 12 test files define a local undotted `skip_if_no_torch()` (test-foundation.R:1, test-piml-neural.R:1, test-piml-hierarchical.R:1, test-temporal.R:1, test-foundation-moco.R:1, test-foundation-tiles.R:2, test-piml-posterior.R:3, test-temporal-posterior.R:3, test-foundation-posterior.R:3, test-piml-neural-ode-ensemble.R:3, test-foundation-weights.R:3, test-foundation-finetune.R:7), used at 52 sites. The link to live ERROR 2 is right: test-foundation-weights.R:29-36 sits two lines below its own unused local gate. TWO OVERSTATEMENTS: it is really 2 behaviours, not 3 — variants (a) and (c) are functionally identical, since `isTRUE()` is pure defensiveness around a function that returns a logical and the claimed "NA return would error rather than skip" is speculative; and the deeper fix for ERROR 2 is arguably to validate `n_channels` before `.moco_require_torch()` at R/foundation_weights.R:294, not to add a skip.
findings.evidence:
tests/testthat/helper-torch.R:7 defines the intended canonical gate `.skip_if_no_torch()` (dotted), and its header at :1-6 explains exactly why it exists: "CI environments routinely install the R package but skip the ~1 GB Lantern download, so a plain `skip_if_not_installed("torch")` is NOT enough". It is used at 18 call sites across 7 files.
But 12 test files still define their own UNdotted `skip_if_no_torch()` locally, used at 52 call sites: tests/testthat/test-foundation.R:1, test-piml-neural.R:1, test-piml-hierarchical.R:1, test-temporal.R:1, test-foundation-moco.R:1, test-foundation-tiles.R:2, test-piml-posterior.R:3, test-temporal-posterior.R:3, test-foundation-posterior.R:3, test-piml-neural-ode-ensemble.R:3, test-foundation-weights.R:3, test-foundation-finetune.R:7.
Three different semantics, verified by reading:
(a) helper-torch.R:7-13 — `skip_if_not_installed("torch")` + `if (!isTRUE(torch::torch_is_installed())) skip(...)`
(b) test-foundation.R:1-4 / test-piml-neural.R:1-4 — `tryCatch(torch::torch_tensor(1), error = function(e) skip("torch runtime unavailable"))`
(c) test-foundation-weights.R:3-8 / test-foundation-finetune.R:7-12 — `if (!torch::torch_is_installed()) skip("torch backend not installed")` (no isTRUE wrapper, so an NA return would error rather than skip)
findings.impact: 70 gate call sites, 13 definitions, 3 behaviours. Variant (b) actually allocates a tensor, which is the only one that reliably detects a broken-but-present Lantern; variant (c) trusts a flag. The centralisation effort that produced helper-torch.R stalled after 7 of 19 files, and the un-migrated files are precisely where the pillar-4 work lives. This is also the mechanism behind the live ERROR 2: tests/testthat/test-foundation-weights.R:28-37 sits two lines below a local gate definition it simply forgot to call.
findings.action: Delete all 12 local definitions and rename the 52 undotted call sites to `.skip_if_no_torch()`. Adopt variant (b)'s tensor allocation inside helper-torch.R:7 (it is the only sound check) while keeping the `isTRUE()` wrapper. Then grep-assert in CI that `skip_if_no_torch <- function` appears nowhere under tests/ so the duplication cannot come back.

findings.title: al_fit(num.trees=) has no lower bound against ranger's undocumented OOB-quantile minimum, and the test that breaks is unseeded — a ~25% flaky ERROR
findings.correction: Third restatement of the same defect, and its headline number is fabricated. Code facts verified (R/active_fit.R:1-10 hardcoding quantreg/keep.inbag; :52-53 and R/active_loop.R:73 accepting any num.trees; roxygen :29; the ranger 0.18.0 `minoob < 10` stop confirmed by deparse; tests/testthat/test-active-quantum-posterior.R:30-35 with bare `stats::rnorm(40L)` and 50L). But "~25% flaky" is asserted with no measurement anywhere in the evidence and is wrong on both counts: the unconditional across-seeds rate is 12.0% (I measured 24/200 at the exact shape), and within the suite the rate is 100% because line 7 of the same file calls set.seed(1L) — I reproduced the failure 3/3 by replaying that stream. "The suite is non-deterministically red" is therefore false; it is deterministically red on ranger 0.18.0. Duplicate of findings 12 and 20; findings 12 and 20 at least quote a measured number.
findings.evidence:
R/active_fit.R:1-10 `.fit_core()` hardcodes `quantreg = TRUE, keep.inbag = TRUE` in the `ranger::ranger()` call. R/active_fit.R:52-53 `al_fit(..., num.trees = 500L, ...)` and R/active_loop.R:73 `al_loop(..., num.trees = 500L, ...)` accept any value with no validation; the roxygen at R/active_fit.R:29 says only "Integer, number of trees (default 500)".
ranger 0.18.0's quantreg branch (verified by deparsing `ranger::ranger` in the installed 0.18.0) ends with: `minoob <- min(rowSums(inbag.counts == 0)); if (minoob < 10) { stop("Error: Too few trees for out-of-bag quantile regression.") }` — i.e. EVERY observation must be out-of-bag in at least 10 trees.
tests/testthat/test-active-quantum-posterior.R:30-35 has no `set.seed()` anywhere in the block; it builds `df` from bare `stats::rnorm(40L)` and calls `al_fit(df, target = "y", covariates = "x", num.trees = 50L)`.
findings.impact: The suite is non-deterministically red, which destroys the credibility of NEWS.md v3.10.0's "1 345 tests pass / 0 errors". Independently, any user who reduces `num.trees` for speed on a small pilot dataset — the exact use case active learning targets — gets a cryptic ranger error with no hint, from a function whose documented parameter contract has no lower bound. All other al_* tests use 100-200 (P(failure) negligible), so 50 is the single unlucky value in the suite.
findings.action: Two changes. (1) In R/active_fit.R, before the ranger call at :3, add `if (num.trees < 100L) .stopf("`num.trees` = %d is too small for out-of-bag quantile regression.", num.trees, hint = "ranger requires every observation to be out-of-bag in >= 10 trees; use num.trees >= 100.")` and document the floor at :29 and R/active_loop.R:36. (2) Add `set.seed(3L)` at the top of tests/testthat/test-active-quantum-posterior.R:30 and raise `num.trees` there to 100L — every other al_* test already uses >= 100.

findings.title: Same loop-invariant matrix product recomputed n_draws times, copy-pasted into two files
findings.evidence:
Site 1 — R/bridges_active_learning_v3.R:290-298. `R_tr_inv` is computed at :278 and `R_cross` at :283, both outside the loop. Inside `for (i in idx) {` at :290, line :295 reads `quadratic <- colSums((R_tr_inv %*% R_cross) * R_cross)` — the expression depends on neither `i` nor anything assigned in the loop body (:291-292 only read `sigma2_draws[i]` / `tau2_draws[i]`). Default `n_draws = 200L` (:261).
Site 2 — R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:384-396, the same copy-paste. `R_tr_inv` at :373 and `R_cross` at :379 are loop-invariant; inside `for (i in seq_along(idx)) {` at :385, lines :389-391 read `w_new_mean <- as.numeric(t(R_cross) %*% R_tr_inv %*% object$w_post_mean)` — no dependence on `i`. Default `n_draws = 500L` (:354).
findings.impact: Two of the package's headline v3.0.0 bridge/prediction entry points are two to three orders of magnitude slower than necessary on realistic problem sizes. This is the same defect duplicated by copy-paste, in the same idiom (build R_tr_inv and R_cross, then loop over posterior draws), which is a concrete measurement of how much of the cross-pillar bridge layer is duplicated rather than shared. Note the irony: this sits alongside a 156-line RcppArmadillo port (src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp) written to buy a 10-15x speedup on the sampler.
findings.action: Hoist line R/bridges_active_learning_v3.R:295 to just after :283, and hoist R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:389-391 to just after :379. Both are one-line moves with no behaviour change (verify with a before/after `expect_equal` on the returned object under a fixed seed). Then extract the shared "exponential-correlation kriging weights from coords" block — duplicated at R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:370-379 and R/bridges_active_learning_v3.R:275-283 — into one internal helper in R/core_utils.R.

findings.title: Naming schism: pilar/pillar, ordinal/domain module names, al_* vs active_*, and five undocumented cryptic export prefixes
findings.evidence:
**Portuguese vs English.** 7 files use the Portuguese "pilar": R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R, R/pilar8_neural_operators.R, R/pilar8_neural_operators_torch.R, R/pilar9_diffusion_models.R, R/pilar9_diffusion_torch.R, R/pilar10_graph_nn.R, R/pilar10_graph_nn_torch.R. One file uses English "pillar": R/pillars_roadmap.R. 17 test files use "pilar" (tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs*.R x4, test-pilar8-*.R x3, test-pilar9-*.R x4, test-pilar10-*.R x4, plus test-benchmark-6pilar.R and test-benchmark-6pilar-calibrate.R). DESCRIPTION and README use "Pillar" throughout. `man/` contains ZERO pilar/pillar-named pages, so the schism is invisible to users and hits only maintainers. Class strings leak it too: R/bridges_active_learning_v3.R:313 prints "(Pilar 7 x Pilar 5)", R/bridges_structure_v3.R:225 prints "(Pilar 6 x Pilar 10)" — Portuguese in USER-FACING print output, while README.md:1195 says "Pillar 5".
**Ordinal vs domain module names.** Pillars 1-6 use domain names (13 x causal_*, 7 x piml_*, 5 x temporal_*, 7 x foundation_*, 8 x active_*, 6 x quantum_*); pillars 7-10 use bare ordinals (pilar7_* .. pilar10_*). Nothing in R/ tells a newcomer that pilar7 == Bayesian hierarchical spatial.
**al_* vs active_*.** R/pillars_roadmap.R:14 and README.md:379 both declare Pillar 5's namespace is `al_*`, but all 8 implementation files are `active_*.R` (active_batchbald, active_fit, active_initial, active_loop, active_physics_gate, active_posterior, active_query, active_update) and tests are test-active.R / test-active-quantum-posterior.R / test-al-batchbald.R (mixed). NAMESPACE exports 14 `al_*` plus exactly one violator, `active_learning_posterior` (R/active_posterior.R).
**Undocumented cryptic prefixes.** Pillars 7-10 export `bhs_*` (1), `no_*` (2: no_fno_fit, no_deeponet_fit), `dm_*` (3), `gnn_*` (4), plus the cross-pillar `qf_*` (5). R/pillars_roadmap.R:8-15 is a namespace table with exactly SIX rows and stops at `quantum_*` — there is no documented convention for any of these five prefixes, and R/pillars_roadmap.R:1 still reads "Roadmap and status of the six pillars" while DESCRIPTION:9 says "ten research pillars". `no_` also collides with the English word "no", making `no_fno_fit` read as a negation.
**Parameter names shadow exported functions.** R/bridges_active_learning_v3.R:260 `al_query_bhs <- function(bhs_fit, pool_data, ...)` shadows the exported `bhs_fit()`; :174 `al_query_diffusion <- function(dm_fit, ...)` shadows the exported `dm_fit()`; R/bridges_structure_v3.R:50 `gnn_causal_discovery <- function(gnn_fit, ...)` and :196 `qf_krr_on_gat_embeddings <- function(gnn_fit, y, ...)` shadow the exported `gnn_fit()`. The generated Rd pages therefore read "@param bhs_fit" for a function also named bhs_fit.
findings.impact: A contributor cannot infer a file's contents or a function's prefix from any single source of truth: the roadmap covers 6 of 10 pillars, DESCRIPTION claims 10, README documents `al_*` for files named `active_*`, and print methods emit Portuguese while the docs emit English. The function-name shadowing is a live hazard: inside `al_query_bhs`, `al_query_diffusion`, `gnn_causal_discovery` and `qf_krr_on_gat_embeddings` the identifiers `bhs_fit`, `dm_fit` and `gnn_fit` resolve to data, so any future refactor that adds a refit call inside those bodies fails with "attempt to apply non-function".
findings.action: Three mechanical passes, none behaviour-changing. (1) `git mv` the 7 R/pilar*.R files and 17 test files to domain names matching pillars 1-6 (bhs_*.R, neural_operators*.R, diffusion*.R, graph_nn*.R) and fix the two user-facing print strings at R/bridges_active_learning_v3.R:313 and R/bridges_structure_v3.R:225 to "Pillar". (2) Extend R/pillars_roadmap.R:8-15 from six rows to ten, retitle :1 from "six pillars" to "ten pillars", and add the `bhs_*`/`no_*`/`dm_*`/`gnn_*`/`qf_*` namespace entries; either rename `active_learning_posterior` to `al_posterior` (with an alias for back-compat) or amend the `al_*` claim in R/pillars_roadmap.R:14 and README.md:379. (3) Rename the four shadowing parameters to `fit` or `object` (R/bridges_active_learning_v3.R:260, :174; R/bridges_structure_v3.R:50, :196) and re-roxygenise. Consider renaming the `no_*` prefix to `fno_*`/`don_*`.

findings.title: Twelve exported functions are never referenced anywhere in tests/, including the entire advertised tile-source pipeline
findings.evidence:
Cross-referencing the 169 `export()` entries in NAMESPACE against every file under tests/, these 12 exported functions appear in zero test file: `causal_ontology_agrovoc`, `causal_ontology_envo`, `edaphos_zenodo_release`, `foundation_build_cerrado_stack`, `foundation_tile_source_era5`, `foundation_tile_source_modis`, `foundation_tile_source_soilgrids`, `foundation_tile_source_srtm`, `foundation_tile_source_worldclim`, `llm_annotation_launch`, `piml_neural_ode_predict`, `temporal_convlstm_predict`.
All five `foundation_tile_source_*` are named explicitly in R/pillars_roadmap.R:13 as part of the "planetary-scale tile pipeline", and `foundation_build_cerrado_stack` is the deliverable of HEAD~2 ("feat(v1.9.3): close roadmap promise -- IV refit with real 31-channel SoilGrids+WorldClim+SRTM stack"). tests/testthat/test-foundation-tiles.R exists but exercises only `foundation_tile_align` / `foundation_tile_dataset`.
Counterpoint for calibration: 157 of 169 exports ARE referenced, and man/ has no orphan pages (182 Rd == 169 exports + 13 method/data/package pages), so this is a targeted gap, not systemic neglect.
findings.impact: The five tile sources plus the Cerrado stack builder are the exact functions a reviewer would run to reproduce the pretrained `edaphos-cerrado-moco-v1` encoder advertised in R/pillars_roadmap.R:13 and README, and none has a single assertion — not even a schema/argument-validation test that could run offline. `edaphos_zenodo_release` (R/edaphos_zenodo_release.R:38, 223 lines) performs authenticated HTTP publishing to Zenodo from inside a CRAN package with zero tests. `llm_annotation_launch` (R/llm_annotation.R:665) is likewise untested.
findings.action: Add offline tests for the cheap half first: argument validation and returned-descriptor schema for each `foundation_tile_source_*` (they should be pure constructors — assert the returned list's fields and that a bad CRS/bbox errors) and for `foundation_build_cerrado_stack` with a stubbed source. Gate the network-touching halves behind `skip_on_cran()` + `skip_if_offline()`. Separately, reconsider whether `edaphos_zenodo_release` belongs in R/ at all — it is release tooling, not a soil-mapping algorithm, and shipping it as a public export means CRAN users can POST to Zenodo; moving it to inst/scripts/ removes both the test debt and the API-surface cost.

findings.title: `Depends: R (>= 3.5)` is falsified by two features requiring R 4.0.0 and R 3.6.0
findings.evidence:
`DESCRIPTION:90-91` declares `Depends: R (>= 3.5)`.

Two hard violations:
1. `tools::R_user_dir()` was introduced in **R 4.0.0**. Used at `R/foundation_weights.R:111` (`root <- cache_dir %||% tools::R_user_dir("edaphos", which = "cache")`) and `R/foundation_embed_coords.R:226` (`cache_dir = tools::R_user_dir("edaphos", which = "cache")`). On R 3.5/3.6 the whole pretrained-weights cache path (`foundation_weights_download/load`, `foundation_embed_at_coords`) errors with `object 'R_user_dir' not found`.
2. `NAMESPACE:15` is `S3method(ggplot2::autoplot,edaphos_posterior)` — delayed S3 registration against a generic in a Suggests-only package. That `pkg::generic` form of `S3method()` was added in **R 3.6.0**; on R 3.5.x package load fails outright.

The CI matrix (`.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml:23-27`) is macos/windows/ubuntu at `release`, `devel`, `oldrel-1` — with R 4.6.1 current, `oldrel-1` is R 4.5.x, so the declared floor is never exercised anywhere.
findings.impact: CRAN builds against the declared minimum. A user (or a CRAN back-check machine) on R 3.5/3.6 gets a package that either fails to load or errors in all of Pillar 4's weight-loading API — reported to the maintainer as a broken package after acceptance.
findings.action: Change `DESCRIPTION:90-91` to `Depends: R (>= 4.0)`, and add an explicit `r: '4.0'` (or `'oldrel-3'`) leg to `.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml` so the declared floor is actually tested.

findings.title: 5 of 14 vignettes are written in Portuguese while DESCRIPTION declares `Language: en-US`
findings.correction: The language mismatch is real: DESCRIPTION:31 `Language: en-US`; PT-stopword counts reproduce as capstone-cerrado-campaign 193, pilar1-pilar4-iv 138, causal-discovery-trio 76, llm-annotation-workflow 64, pilar4-pilar6-quantum 44, everything else 0-1; capstone's title AND `%\VignetteIndexEntry{}` are Portuguese; DESCRIPTION:8 "organised" and :27 "synthesised" are en-GB; 22 man/*.Rd carry en-GB forms. Two claims are wrong. (1) "inst/WORDLIST ... nothing consumes it" — CONTRIBUTING.md:47 and .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md both mandate `devtools::spell_check()`, which is `spelling::spell_check_package()` and reads inst/WORDLIST as its ignore list; the 2032-line file is the documented dev-workflow artefact, not dead. (2) The stated check mechanism is wrong: `R CMD check --as-cran` does not run aspell over vignettes, and "checking for detritus in the temp directory" has nothing to do with spelling — CRAN's automated spell check covers DESCRIPTION/Rd only. The rOpenSci English-documentation concern stands on its own.
findings.evidence:
`DESCRIPTION:31` is `Language: en-US`. Portuguese-stopword density per vignette (`que|para|não|com|uma|dos|das|pelo|pela|como|mais|então|porque|também`):
- `vignettes/capstone-cerrado-campaign.Rmd` — 186 hits; title (`:2`) "Capstone — Uma decisão de amostragem sob incerteza no Cerrado"; `\VignetteIndexEntry` at `:13` is Portuguese.
- `vignettes/pilar1-pilar4-iv.Rmd` — 132 hits; subtitle `:3` "Pilar 1 × Pilar 4 — identificando efeitos causais com confundidores latentes".
- `vignettes/causal-discovery-trio.Rmd` — 71 hits; title `:2` "Causal discovery no Cerrado: expert vs. LLM vs. data-driven".
- `vignettes/llm-annotation-workflow.Rmd` — 58 hits; title `:2` "Escalando o gold-standard de 72 para 300+ claims".
- `vignettes/pilar4-pilar6-quantum.Rmd` — 44 hits.
The other 9 vignettes score 0-1.

DESCRIPTION itself is en-GB, not en-US: `:8` "organised", `:27` "synthesised". 22 `man/*.Rd` files carry en-GB forms (`organis|behaviour|colour|modelling|favour|harmonis|normalis|penalis`).

Supporting spell-check infrastructure is present but inert: `inst/WORDLIST` has **2032 lines** and is padded with Portuguese vocabulary (`Ação`, `aceitos`, `acelera`, `acima`, `aciona`, `acontece`, `acreditamos`, ...), yet `spelling` is not in Suggests and there is no `tests/spelling.R` — so nothing consumes it.
findings.impact: CRAN runs `aspell` against the declared `Language`; five Portuguese vignettes plus en-GB spellings in DESCRIPTION produce a large `checking for detritus`/spelling NOTE and a near-certain reviewer request ("the Language field must match the documentation language"). rOpenSci requires English-language documentation outright, so 5 of 14 vignettes are out of policy for the review the checklist is preparing to file.
findings.action: Decide one way: either translate the 5 Portuguese vignettes to English (and fix `organised`->`organized`, `synthesised`->`synthesized` in DESCRIPTION:8,27), or move them out of `vignettes/` into `articles/` and drop them from the tarball. Then add `spelling` to Suggests plus `tests/spelling.R` so `inst/WORDLIST` is actually enforced instead of being 20 KB of shipped dead weight.

findings.title: DESCRIPTION Title/Description violate CRAN style: marketing adjectives, unquoted software names, zero method references
findings.correction: none — DESCRIPTION:2 `Title: Disruptive Algorithms for Digital Soil Mapping`; :8 "Frontier algorithms…"; unquoted software names verified at :16 (SimCLR / MoCo), :19 (ZZFeatureMap), :21 (RcppArmadillo backend), :22 (DeepONet and Fourier Neural Operator), :23 (DDPM); `grep -l '\\doi{' man/*.Rd | wc -l` = 0 and `grep -c 'doi:' DESCRIPTION` = 0 while vignettes/references.bib is 31,291 bytes; Authors@R at :4-7 is `role = c("aut", "cre")` with no "cph" against `LICENSE:2 COPYRIGHT HOLDER: Hugo Rodrigues` and `License: MIT + file LICENSE` at :29; :25 "Six v3.0.0 cross-pillar bridges" and :26 unquoted `edaphos_posterior`. Note the version-stale prose at :25 is a second six-vs-ten instance inside the very file that says "ten" at :8.
findings.evidence:
`DESCRIPTION:2` — `Title: Disruptive Algorithms for Digital Soil Mapping`. `DESCRIPTION:8` — `Description: Frontier algorithms for Digital Soil Mapping organised around ten research pillars:`. CRAN's checklist explicitly asks maintainers to drop promotional language; "Disruptive" and "Frontier" are exactly that, and the same wording is repeated in `inst/rosc/submission.md:13` and `vignettes/case-cerrado-end-to-end.Rmd:28-30` (which itself calls the claim "falsifiable").

Software/package names are unquoted throughout the Description, where CRAN requires single quotes: `SimCLR / MoCo` (:16), `ZZFeatureMap` (:19), `RcppArmadillo backend` (:21), `DeepONet and Fourier Neural Operator` (:22), `DDPM` (:23).

**No references at all.** `grep '\\doi{'` over `man/*.Rd` returns **0 files**, and the Description contains no `<doi:...>` or `<https://...>` citation. Yet the Description names ten published method families (backdoor adjustment, Neural ODE, ConvLSTM, Ensemble Kalman Filter, SimCLR, MoCo, ZZFeatureMap, DeepONet, FNO, DDPM, GAT) whose papers *are* already catalogued in `vignettes/references.bib` (31 KB) and in `\references` blocks (e.g. `man/uncertainty_calibrate.Rd` cites Gneiting & Raftery 2007, `man/quantum_kernel.Rd` cites Havlicek 2019).

`Authors@R` (`:4-7`) gives Hugo Rodrigues roles `c("aut", "cre")` only — no `"cph"` — while `LICENSE:2` declares `COPYRIGHT HOLDER: Hugo Rodrigues` for the `MIT + file LICENSE` at `:29`.

The Description also embeds version-specific prose that goes stale immediately: `:25` "Six v3.0.0 cross-pillar bridges", and `:26` names an internal class (`edaphos_posterior`) unquoted.
findings.impact: "Please add references describing the methods in the Description field in the form authors (year) <doi:...>", "please put software names in single quotes", "please add the copyright holder (cph) role" and "please avoid marketing language" are four of the five most common CRAN first-round replies. Each costs a submission round-trip of days.
findings.action: Rewrite DESCRIPTION:2 to a neutral Title (e.g. `Advanced Algorithms for Digital Soil Mapping`); single-quote every software name in the Description; append 3-5 anchor references pulled from `vignettes/references.bib` as `Author (Year) <doi:10.xxxx/yyyy>`; add `"cph"` to the Authors@R role vector; drop the `v3.0.0`/`edaphos_posterior` internals from the Description.

findings.title: `src/Makevars.win` documents a Unix `src/Makevars` that does not exist
findings.evidence:
`src/` contains `Makevars.win`, `RcppExports.cpp`, `bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp`, `quantum_kernel_rcpp.cpp` — there is **no `src/Makevars`** (and `.gitignore:57-60` only ignores `src/*.o`, `*.so`, `*.dll`, `symbols.rds`, so it is genuinely absent rather than untracked).

`src/Makevars.win:1-6` reads:
```
# Windows-specific Makevars -- mirror the Unix Makevars, but
# explicit so rtools45 ld.exe can resolve the Armadillo BLAS/LAPACK
# symbols (ddot_, dgemv_, dgemm_, dsyrk_, ...).  Without this file
# the v3.5.0 RcppArmadillo Gibbs sampler fails to link on
# windows-latest CI with "undefined reference" errors.
PKG_LIBS = $(LAPACK_LIBS) $(BLAS_LIBS) $(FLIBS)
```
It asserts it mirrors a file that isn't there. `DESCRIPTION:86-88` declares `LinkingTo: Rcpp, RcppArmadillo`, and `src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp` is the RcppArmadillo Gibbs sampler the comment refers to.
findings.impact: On Linux/macOS the LAPACK/BLAS symbols currently resolve only by accident — because the already-loaded R process exports them and `.so` symbol resolution is lazy. On CRAN's Solaris/alternative-BLAS/`--disable-BLAS-shlib` build farms that assumption can break with the same `undefined reference to ddot_` the Windows file was written to fix, on a platform the CI matrix does not cover. The comment also misleads the next maintainer into believing a Unix counterpart exists.
findings.action: Add `src/Makevars` containing `PKG_LIBS = $(LAPACK_LIBS) $(BLAS_LIBS) $(FLIBS)` (the standard RcppArmadillo skeleton), which makes `Makevars.win`'s comment true and removes the platform-dependent link assumption.

findings.title: RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md instructs the maintainer to upload two artefacts that do not exist, and asserts a green state contradicted by the live test run
findings.correction: Confirmed: :13-15 names /tmp/edaphos_release_tarballs/edaphos_3.10.0.tar.gz (`ls` -> No such file or directory); :53-55 and :62 name tools/zenodo_release.zip, absent and .gitignore'd (line 65, plus tools/zenodo_release/ at 64); :3-4 headlines "code 100 % ready, CI green, all artefacts regenerated". One sub-point is a category error: :15's "17 MB" is the source *tarball* while cran-comments.md:69's "~13 MB" is the *installed* size — different quantities, not a contradiction. The version-scope point holds (DESCRIPTION:3 / NEWS.md:1 are 3.10.0 while HEAD~1 is the v3.11.0 hand-off commit and tools/pretrain/V1_3_2_HANDOFF.md exists).
findings.evidence:
`RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:13-15` — "The package source tarball is already built at: `/tmp/edaphos_release_tarballs/edaphos_3.10.0.tar.gz` (17 MB)". That directory does not exist.

`:53-55` — "The bundle is already built at: `tools/zenodo_release.zip` (22.2 MB, 24 files)", and `:62` — "Upload `tools/zenodo_release.zip` as the only file." The file does not exist, and `.gitignore:65` (`tools/zenodo_release.zip`) guarantees it never will be restorable from the repo. `tools/` currently holds 8 files, none of them a zip.

`:3-4` — "Status as of this commit: code 100 % ready, CI green, all artefacts regenerated." The live `devtools::test()` run has **2 errors** (`tests/testthat/test-active-quantum-posterior.R:34` and `tests/testthat/test-foundation-weights.R:33`).

`:15` also states the tarball is **17 MB** while `cran-comments.md:69` frames the problem as a "~13 MB" *installed* size — the two release documents disagree on the size being justified.

Compounding the version confusion: `DESCRIPTION:3` is `Version: 3.10.0`, `NEWS.md:1` is `# edaphos 3.10.0`, but `HEAD~1` is `feat(v3.11.0): hand-off package for the v1.3.2 MoCo v2 publish pipeline` and `tools/pretrain/V1_3_2_HANDOFF.md` exists — so the checklist is scoped to a version the repo has already moved past without a NEWS entry.
findings.impact: A maintainer following this checklist step-by-step reaches step 1 or 3 and finds nothing to submit or upload, with no recorded command to regenerate either artefact. The "CI green / 100 % ready" header actively suppresses the two real test failures that should gate the release.
findings.action: Replace the hard-coded artefact paths with the commands that produce them (`devtools::build()`, and whatever script built `zenodo_release.zip` — it is not in `tools/`). Rename/renumber the checklist for the actual next version, add a NEWS.md `# edaphos 3.11.0` section for the HEAD~1 work, and gate the header claim on a passing `devtools::test()`.

findings.title: Two overlapping release checklists disagree with each other and both claim to be the authoritative list of remaining steps
findings.evidence: RELEASE.md:1 "# edaphos — public-release checklist (v2.9.1)" and :3-4 "This file lists the **four remaining manual actions** a maintainer must execute", closing at :143-144 "These four manual steps are the **only** remaining blockers". RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:1 "# Release checklist for edaphos v3.10.0", :113-115 "The four steps above are the residual human-in-the-loop." Both enumerate CRAN / rOpenSci / Zenodo / GH-Pages but with different instructions and conflicting facts. Install-size limits contradict: RELEASE.md:95-96 "CRAN's policy requires **at most 24 MB of installed package**" vs cran-comments.md:69-70 "above the CRAN soft-cap of 5 MB" and :96 "the *hard* limit is 100 MB" -- three different numbers for the same policy. RELEASE.md:16-18 asserts "The badge in README currently resolves to **v0.2.0** because the concept DOI was minted early", a defect RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md never mentions. RELEASE.md:97-98 refers to "the 1.9 MB `benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7.rds`" while cran-comments.md:74 sizes the same file at 0.7 MB. Both files are excluded from the tarball (.Rbuildignore:19 and :24) so they exist only for the maintainer, and .Rbuildignore:24 hardcodes the version into the pattern `^RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3\.10\.0\.md$`, meaning the next release's checklist will silently ship inside the CRAN tarball.
findings.impact: There is no single answer to "what is left to do before release". A maintainer following RELEASE.md targets v2.9.1 and is told the DOI badge points at v0.2.0; following RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md they are told everything is "code 100 % ready, CI green" (RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:3-4), which finding #4 shows is false. The version-specific .Rbuildignore pattern guarantees a future R CMD check NOTE about a non-standard top-level file.
findings.action: Delete RELEASE.md (its v2.9.1 content is superseded), rename the survivor to a version-free `RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md`, and change .Rbuildignore:24 to `^RELEASE-CHECKLIST.*\.md$` so it stays excluded across releases. Reconcile the install-size numbers to one figure and fold RELEASE.md:16-18's concept-DOI-resolves-to-v0.2.0 warning into the surviving checklist.

findings.title: The "ten pillars" identity exists only in the unreleased HEAD; every other metadata artefact still says six
findings.correction: none — `git rev-list --oneline v3.10.0..HEAD` contains 797adc5 "chore(cran-prep): tighten DESCRIPTION (10 pillars instead of 6)", so DESCRIPTION:8-9 "organised around ten research pillars" is indeed post-tag. Every counter-citation verified: CITATION.cff:7 "six research pillars" and :33 "all six pillars"; .zenodo.json:3 six-item `<ol>`; _pkgdown.yml:44 and :66; R/pillars_roadmap.R:1 "Roadmap and status of the six pillars of edaphos" (and its table at :8-19 enumerates only pillars 1-6); README.md:371 "## The six pillars at a glance" plus 11 further "six pillars" hits (12 total). Against them: README.md:10 `pillars-10%2F10%20shipped`, INTRO.md:42 "## The ten research pillars", inst/rosc/submission.md:14 "ten research pillars", CONTRIBUTING.md:60 "Every \"pillar\" (1-10) lives in `R/pilarN_*.R`", and R/pilar7_*.R–R/pilar10_*.R on disk.
findings.evidence: Commit 797adc5 "chore(cran-prep): tighten DESCRIPTION (10 pillars instead of 6)" landed AFTER the v3.10.0 tag (it is in `git rev-list v3.10.0..HEAD`), so DESCRIPTION:8-9 "organised around ten research pillars" is the only ten-pillar statement in released metadata terms -- and it belongs to an unversioned commit. Everything else still says six: CITATION.cff:7 "organised across six research pillars"; .zenodo.json:3 "organised across six research pillars" with an `<ol>` of exactly six items; _pkgdown.yml:44 "Six research pillars"; _pkgdown.yml:66 "Capstone — six pillars integrated"; R/pillars_roadmap.R:1 "#' Roadmap and status of the six pillars of edaphos"; README.md:371 "## The six pillars at a glance" (a table with six pillar rows) plus 12 further "six pillars" occurrences in README.md. Meanwhile README.md:10 badges "pillars-10%2F10%20shipped", INTRO.md:42 says "## The ten research pillars", inst/rosc/submission.md:14 says "ten research pillars", CONTRIBUTING.md:60 says "Every \"pillar\" (1-10) lives in `R/pilarN_*.R`", and R/pilar7_*.R through R/pilar10_*.R exist on disk.
findings.impact: The package's most basic self-description is 6-vs-10 depending on which file you open, and the tie-breaking file (DESCRIPTION) only reached its current wording in a commit that carries no version number -- so there is no released version of edaphos that consistently claims ten pillars. Every downstream metadata consumer (Zenodo via .zenodo.json, GitHub citation widget via CITATION.cff, docs site via _pkgdown.yml, `?edaphos-roadmap` via R/pillars_roadmap.R) will keep publishing "six" after the DESCRIPTION change ships.
findings.action: In one commit, propagate the ten-pillar wording from DESCRIPTION:8-28 to CITATION.cff:4-107, .zenodo.json:3, _pkgdown.yml:43-48 and :66, and R/pillars_roadmap.R:1 (whose roxygen table also needs rows for Pilares 7-10, then re-roxygenise man/edaphos-roadmap.Rd). Update README.md:371 and its anchor consumers (README.md:10, :210). Tie the whole change to the version bump from finding #1 so "ten pillars" first appears in a numbered, tagged release.

findings.title: The 84 KB README documents nothing after v2.8.0; its only 3.x reference is the version badge
findings.evidence: `grep -nE 'v3\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+|3\.10\.0' README.md` returns exactly two hits: README.md:9 (the version badge) and README.md:1716 (the roadmap row marking v3.0.0 as 📝 not-done). The most recent "🆕" feature section is README.md:147 "## 🆕 v1.7.0 — capstone cross-pillar vignette", introduced as "The headline feature of the current release". README.md:230 is "## 🆕 v2.7.0 – v2.8.0" described as "Two new releases complete the v2.x arc". The table of contents (README.md:209-226) lists Pillars 1-6 and stops -- there are no entries for Pillars 7-10, while the badge at README.md:10 claims "pillars-10%2F10%20shipped" and links to `#the-six-pillars-at-a-glance` (the heading at README.md:371 is literally "## The six pillars at a glance"). Two further stale factual claims in the same file: README.md:1674-1675 "`R CMD check --as-cran` → **0 errors / 0 warnings / 0 notes** on v1.7.0", and README.md:364 "The package imports only **six** CRAN packages" while `read.dcf('DESCRIPTION')[,'Imports']` yields 7 (clhs, deSolve, httr2, jsonlite, ranger, Rcpp, stats -- Rcpp was added at v2.1.3).
findings.impact: The public front page of the project describes a 6-pillar package at v1.7.0/v2.8.0 while the badges beside it claim 3.10.0 and 10/10 pillars. Pillars 7-10 -- Bayesian hierarchical spatial, neural operators, diffusion models, GATs, i.e. R/pilar7_*.R through R/pilar10_*.R and roughly the whole v2.3.0-v3.6.0 arc -- are invisible to anyone reading the README, and the ten-vs-six contradiction is visible within a single screen (badge line 10 vs heading line 371).
findings.action: Either add Pillar 7-10 sections and TOC entries and retitle README.md:371 to "The ten pillars at a glance" (updating the anchor at README.md:10 and the TOC entry at README.md:210), or drop the "10/10 pillars" badge until the README backs it. Delete the stale "🆕" prefixes at README.md:147 and :230, correct README.md:1674-1675 to the real check status (see finding #4), and change "six" to "seven" at README.md:364.

findings.title: .zenodo.json carries no version field at all and its description is frozen at v1.8.0
findings.correction: none on the file facts — .zenodo.json is 47 lines total, has no `version`, no `publication_date`, no `doi`; .zenodo.json:3 says "organised across six research pillars", narrates to "v1.8.0 delivers the first quantitative validation…", closes with "nine mathematically-derived vignettes" (vignettes/ holds 14 .Rmd); .Rbuildignore:11 is `^\.zenodo\.json$`; CITATION.cff:109-110 do carry version/date-released. SEVERITY DEFLATED because the stated impact is conditional on an unproven premise: nothing in the repo shows the GitHub→Zenodo integration is enabled, and RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:57-68 has the maintainer use Zenodo's manual "New version" web form, which never reads .zenodo.json. So the "immutable DOI record with no version label" scenario is possible but not demonstrated; what is demonstrated is two-major-versions-stale checked-in metadata.
findings.evidence: .zenodo.json:1-47 is the complete file. It has no `"version"` key and no `"publication_date"` key (compare CITATION.cff:109-110 which at least attempts both). Its `"description"` (.zenodo.json:3) says "Contributions are organised across six research pillars", narrates up to "v1.8.0 delivers the first quantitative validation of the Pillar 1 LLM extractor", and closes with "nine mathematically-derived vignettes" -- the repo now has 14 in vignettes/ plus 4 in articles/ (README.md:11 badge says 14, inst/rosc/submission.md:79 says 14). `.zenodo.json` is .Rbuildignore'd (.Rbuildignore:11) so it exists purely to drive the GitHub->Zenodo archiving integration, which reads it verbatim on tag/release.
findings.impact: If the GitHub-Zenodo integration is enabled and any tag is pushed, the resulting DOI record is published with NO version label and a description two major versions out of date (six pillars, v1.8.0, nine vignettes). That record is immutable. RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:63-65 tries to compensate by asking the maintainer to hand-type the version and description into the Zenodo web form, which means the checked-in metadata file is knowingly wrong and the correct metadata exists only as manual instructions.
findings.action: Add `"version": "3.10.0"` (or 3.11.0 per finding #1) and `"publication_date"` to .zenodo.json, and replace the .zenodo.json:3 description with the current 10-pillar text from DESCRIPTION:8-28 plus the v1.9.x-v3.10.0 highlights already written in cran-comments.md:105-132. Then the manual steps at RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:63-65 become unnecessary.

findings.title: The only DOI badge is a concept DOI the repo itself says resolves to v0.2.0, and nothing after v1.5.0 was ever deposited
findings.correction: File facts confirmed: README.md:7 is the sole DOI badge; RELEASE.md:17-18 (not :16-18) says the badge resolves to v0.2.0; the same concept DOI recurs at README.md:1728/:1737, cran-comments.md:103, inst/rosc/submission.md:22, INTRO.md:141, R/edaphos_zenodo_release.R:140/:202; RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:51-71 still lists the deposit as pending; only 3 workflows exist. Two claims do not hold as stated: the badge row at README.md:4-13 holds 10 badges (plus 4 social badges at :15-18), not "nine badges at README.md:4-18"; and "nothing after v1.5.0 was ever deposited" is an inference from CITATION.cff, not something the repo states -- a v3.10.0 tag does exist and GitHub Releases cannot be checked offline.
findings.evidence: README.md:7 is the sole DOI badge: `[![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.19683708.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19683708)`. RELEASE.md:16-18 states outright: "The badge in README currently resolves to **v0.2.0** because the concept DOI was minted early." The same concept DOI is presented as the citation for the current release at README.md:1727-1728 and :1736-1737, cran-comments.md:102-103 ("archived on Zenodo at <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19683708>"), inst/rosc/submission.md:22, INTRO.md, and R/edaphos_zenodo_release.R. The only other resolvable version DOIs in the repo are CITATION.cff:121 (v1.5.0, 10.5281/zenodo.19709560) and the twelve-way duplicate 10.5281/zenodo.19710162 (finding #7). RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:51-71 confirms the v3.10.0 deposit is still an unperformed manual step. README.md:8's `img.shields.io/github/v/release/HugoMachadoRodrigues/edaphos` depends on GitHub Releases, which no workflow creates (.github/workflows/ = R-CMD-check.yaml, pkgdown.yaml, test-coverage.yaml only).
findings.impact: The badge row makes the package look archived and versioned when the newest archived artefact is v1.5.0/v1.6.0-era. A reader citing the badge DOI cites v0.2.0 content while reading 3.10.0 documentation. Combined with the version badge (README.md:9, 3.10.0), the release badge (likely rendering "no releases"), the tests badge (1345, unreproducible per finding #5) and the pillars badge (10/10, contradicted by the README's own six-pillar body per finding #10), four of the nine badges at README.md:4-18 misstate the project's state.
findings.action: Execute the Zenodo deposit (RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:51-71) so a version DOI exists, then add a version-DOI badge alongside the concept-DOI badge at README.md:7 and record the minted id in CITATION.cff. Add a release-publishing workflow so README.md:8 has Releases to report. Until the deposit exists, either remove RELEASE.md:16-18's known-stale badge or annotate it in the README as "concept DOI (all versions)" so readers do not mistake it for the current release.

findings.title: Two parallel version schemes collide inside a single README table: "v1.x roadmap lines" are interleaved with package 3.x versions, and v3.0.0 means two different things
findings.correction: none — README.md:1687-1717 verified verbatim, including the three v1.x rows placed below the v2.x block (:1714 v1.9.3 📝, :1715 v1.3.2 🚧, :1716 v1.8.3 📝) and :1717 `v3.0.0 | CRAN + rOpenSci submission | 📝`. NEWS.md:660 is `# edaphos 3.0.0` (shipped). NEWS.md:915 is `# edaphos 2.6.0` under the heading "Pilar 10 -- Graph Attention Networks", so README.md:1713's `v2.8.0 | Pilar 10` is the wrong version. `git log` confirms fd4ab0b (v1.8.3), 05cb516 (v1.9.3) and 7400a2c ("feat(v3.11.0): ... v1.3.2 ..."). NEWS has sections for 2.6.0/2.7.0/2.9.0/2.9.1/3.1.0-3.10.0, none of which appear as rows.
findings.evidence: The roadmap table at README.md:1688-1717 mixes both schemes with no marker distinguishing them. Rows v1.4.0 through v2.8.0 are package versions marked shipped; then three rows appear BELOW the v2.x rows, out of order, as unfinished: README.md:1714 `v1.9.3 | Real geodata download path (EDAPHOS_IV_REAL_STACK) + refit | 📝`, :1715 `v1.3.2 | Re-benchmark with MoCo v2 encoder (200 k steps) | 🚧`, :1716 `v1.8.3 | Expand gold-standard to 300 real claims (via v1.8.2 tool) | 📝`. All three were in fact closed or advanced by commits that carry those same v1.x numbers as their subject: fd4ab0b "data(v1.8.3): expand cerrado_claims_real_corpus.jsonl from 210 -> 301 claims (closes the v1.8 roadmap promise)", 05cb516 "feat(v1.9.3): close roadmap promise -- IV refit with real 31-channel stack", 7400a2c "feat(v3.11.0): hand-off package for the v1.3.2 MoCo v2 publish pipeline" -- and that last subject line contains BOTH schemes at once. The hardest collision is README.md:1717 `v3.0.0 | CRAN + rOpenSci submission | 📝` versus the actually-shipped v3.0.0 at NEWS.md:660 and commit e09633c "feat(v3.0.0): six new cross-pilar bridges": the same string v3.0.0 denotes an unstarted roadmap goal in the README and a delivered feature release in NEWS. A separate factual collision: README.md:1713 credits `v2.8.0 | Pilar 10 — Graph Attention Networks`, but NEWS.md:915 is `# edaphos 2.6.0` and commit 221fda2 is "feat(v2.6.0): Pilar 10 -- Graph Attention Networks". The table also has no row whatsoever for v2.6.0, v2.7.0, v2.9.0, v2.9.1, v3.1.0-v3.10.0.
findings.impact: A reader cannot tell whether "v1.3.2" is an older release than the current 3.10.0 (it looks like it) or an open work item (it is). The two schemes make the roadmap unreadable: three items shown as pending are done, one item shown as pending (v3.0.0 CRAN submission) shares its number with a release that shipped ten versions ago, and the pillar that defines the package's headline "10/10" badge is attributed to the wrong version. Anyone estimating project state from this table will be wrong in both directions simultaneously.
findings.action: Split the table in two: a "Released" table keyed strictly on DESCRIPTION versions (with every 2.6.0-3.10.0 row filled in, and Pilar 10 corrected from v2.8.0 to v2.6.0 at README.md:1713), and a separate "Open research promises" list that uses names rather than version numbers (e.g. "MoCo v2 200k-step re-benchmark", "CRAN + rOpenSci submission") so no roadmap item can ever collide with a release number again. Mark the three completed rows (README.md:1714-1716) as done and stop using v1.x strings in commit subjects for work landing in 3.x.

findings.title: Archival metadata (.zenodo.json, CITATION.cff) still describes a six-pillar package that stops at v1.8.0
findings.correction: none — .zenodo.json:3 verified (six-item `<ol>`, narrative ending at v1.8.0, "nine mathematically-derived vignettes" vs 14 .Rmd in vignettes/); CITATION.cff:7 "organised across six research pillars" and :33 "all six pillars"; RELEASE.md ~:53-55 does say "Copy the minted version DOI into `CITATION.cff` under `identifiers:` as a new entry, and also update `.zenodo.json` if it still points to an older DOI"; README's BibTeX at :1735 reads `version   = {2.8.0}` (the cited 1741-1752 range is ~6 lines low). This is the same defect as finding 3 with CITATION.cff added; severity is honest for stale citation metadata but it is not new information.
findings.evidence: `.zenodo.json:3` description enumerates six pillars in an `<ol>` and its narrative ends at "v1.8.0 delivers the first quantitative validation of the Pillar 1 LLM extractor" — no mention of pillars 7-10 (v2.3.0-v2.8.0), the v3.0.0 bridges, or anything in v3.1.0-v3.10.0. It also claims "nine mathematically-derived vignettes" while `vignettes/` holds 14 .Rmd files. `CITATION.cff:7` "organised across six research pillars" and :33 "integrates all six pillars". RELEASE.md:51-53 explicitly lists updating both as a post-Zenodo step ("Copy the minted version DOI into CITATION.cff ... and also update .zenodo.json if it still points to an older DOI") — never done. README.md:1741-1752 citation block still says `version = {2.8.0}`.
findings.impact: These two files are what Zenodo and citation tooling read. Publishing the v3.10.0 deposit (RELEASE-CHECKLIST step 3) would archive a description of a two-years-stale, six-pillar package under the current DOI, and `citation("edaphos")` / the README BibTeX would tell citing authors to reference v2.8.0. This is the metadata half of the ten-vs-six contradiction and is not fixable after the deposit is published.
findings.action: Rewrite `.zenodo.json` description to ten pillars + the v2.x/v3.x history and correct the vignette count to 14; update `CITATION.cff:7,33` to ten pillars and bump its version/date fields; update the README citation block and install pin. Do all of this BEFORE executing RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md step 3, since the deposit snapshots these files.

findings.title: Step 4 of the v1.3.2 hand-off (wire_up_v2_doi.R) matches nothing and silently writes the timestamp into the `url` field
findings.correction: none — I executed the script's logic against the real file and got precisely the predicted end state. `grep(pat, txt, fixed=TRUE)` returns 0 matches for the script's pattern at tools/pretrain/wire_up_v2_doi.R:50/:55 (`\\\'` in a single-quoted R literal yields backslash+apostrophe) and 2 matches for the correctly-escaped one; the dead `patches <- list(...)` block at :37-46 does use correct single-backslash escaping. Simulated result: R/foundation_weights.R:67 becomes `"2026-05-01T18:30:00Z"           # filled after the user's Zenodo upload` inside `url = c(...)`, :71 correctly gets the SHA256, and :75 (doi) and :80 (published_at) stay `NA_character_`; remaining NA lines were 67, 75, 80, 137 so `ix[1L]` = 67 as claimed. The guard at R/foundation_weights.R:185-191 (`if (is.na(entry$url) || !nzchar(entry$url))`) would then pass and httr2 would fetch the literal timestamp. HANDOFF text confirmed at tools/pretrain/V1_3_2_HANDOFF.md:130 ("Diff is tiny (4 single-line substitutions)"), one line off the cited :131. SEVERITY DEFLATED FROM BLOCKER: tools/ is .Rbuildignore'd (.Rbuildignore:12), the script is maintainer-only tooling for a not-yet-started v3.11.0 step, it corrupts no released artefact, and the script itself instructs `git diff`/`git add` review before commit — where a timestamp sitting in a `url` vector is obvious.
findings.evidence: `tools/pretrain/wire_up_v2_doi.R:50` and `:55` search for the URL/DOI placeholders with `sub('NA_character_           # filled after the user\\\'s Zenodo upload', ..., fixed = TRUE)`. In an R single-quoted literal `\\\'` yields the two characters backslash + apostrophe, so the search string is `user\'s Zenodo upload` while `R/foundation_weights.R:67` and `:75` contain `user's Zenodo upload`. Verified: `grep(pat, txt, fixed=TRUE)` returns 0 matches for the script's pattern and 2 matches for the correctly-escaped one. The dead `patches <- list(...)` block at `wire_up_v2_doi.R:37-46` uses the CORRECT single-backslash escaping but is never used. Because the URL sub fails, the published_at fallback at `:58-64` (`ix <- which(grepl('NA_character_', new)); new[ix[1L]] <- sub(...)`) picks `ix[1] = 67`, the `url` row. Simulated end state of R/foundation_weights.R after running the documented Step 4 command: line 67 becomes `"2026-05-01T18:30:00Z"           # filled after the user's Zenodo upload` inside `url = c(...)`, sha256 is correctly patched, and `doi` (line 75) and `published_at` (line 80) remain `NA_character_`.
findings.impact: The last documented step of tools/pretrain/V1_3_2_HANDOFF.md (Step 4, "~30 seconds") corrupts the pretrained-weights registry instead of wiring it up. `foundation_weights_download("edaphos-cerrado-moco-v2")` would then pass the NA-URL guard at R/foundation_weights.R:186-191 (url is non-NA) and attempt an HTTP fetch of the literal string `2026-05-01T18:30:00Z`, failing with an opaque error for every user. The DOI never lands in the catalog, so the v1.3.2 roadmap line cannot actually be closed by the tooling written to close it. HANDOFF.md:131 tells the maintainer the "diff is tiny (4 single-line substitutions)" — it is 2, in the wrong places.
findings.action: In tools/pretrain/wire_up_v2_doi.R replace `\\\'` with `\'` in the patterns at lines 50 and 55 (or switch to matching on the unambiguous anchors `url         = c(` / `doi         = c(` blocks). Delete the unused `patches` list at 37-46. Replace the positional `ix[1L]` published_at fallback with an explicit match inside the `published_at = c(` block, and add a post-write assertion that `.foundation_weights_registry()` has zero NA fields for the v2 row before the script exits 0.

findings.title: Four pkgdown navbar links point at articles pkgdown never builds, and man/edaphos-package.Rd tells users to open a vignette that is not in the package
findings.correction: none of substance — navbar hrefs verified at _pkgdown.yml:75 (pilar1-causal-real), :79 (llm-kg-benchmark), :91 (pilar3-4d-real), :101 (pilar5-soilgrids-br), i.e. 1-2 lines off the cited 74/78/88/99. The four sources are top-level (articles/llm-kg-benchmark.Rmd 16,575 B, pilar1-causal-real.Rmd 8,766 B, pilar3-4d-real.Rmd 12,739 B, pilar5-soilgrids-br.Rmd 5,399 B); `ls vignettes/articles` → No such file or directory; `.Rbuildignore:21` is `^articles$`; `git ls-files | grep -c '^docs/'` = 0 so no pre-rendered HTML is committed; pkgdown.yaml:56 runs `build_site_github_pages` with no copy step and its header at :3-4 does claim the site "builds from already-rendered vignettes (`articles` folder)"; the `articles:` index at :219-247 lists exactly the 14 vignettes/ files and none of the four. R/edaphos-package.R:153 → man/edaphos-package.Rd:162 does point at `vignette("pilar5-soilgrids-br", package = "edaphos")`, which cannot resolve in an installed package. One nuance: inst/rosc/submission.md:79 shows the articles/ exclusion from the tarball is deliberate ("4 additional articles in `articles/` (case studies; `.Rbuildignore`-d to keep the vignette build fast)"), so "dead content" overstates intent — but the four 404 menu entries and the unresolvable man-page pointer are genuine. Severity deflated from high because neither R CMD check nor CI inspects vignette() calls or navbar hrefs, so the blast radius is broken doc links, not broken code.
findings.evidence: `_pkgdown.yml` navbar references `articles/pilar1-causal-real.html` (:74), `articles/llm-kg-benchmark.html` (:78), `articles/pilar3-4d-real.html` (:88), `articles/pilar5-soilgrids-br.html` (:99). Those four sources live in the top-level `articles/` directory (`articles/pilar1-causal-real.Rmd`, `llm-kg-benchmark.Rmd`, `pilar3-4d-real.Rmd`, `pilar5-soilgrids-br.Rmd`), not in `vignettes/`; `vignettes/articles/` does not exist. pkgdown only renders `vignettes/` (and `vignettes/articles/`). `.github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml` runs `pkgdown::build_site_github_pages(new_process = FALSE, install = FALSE)` with no step copying `articles/` anywhere — its own header comment even claims the site "builds from already-rendered vignettes (`articles` folder)", which is not what pkgdown does. The `_pkgdown.yml` `articles:` index (:220-248) correspondingly lists only the 14 `vignettes/*.Rmd`, omitting all four. Separately, `R/edaphos-package.R:153` -> `man/edaphos-package.Rd:162` instructs `vignette("pilar5-soilgrids-br", package = "edaphos")`, but `.Rbuildignore` line `^articles$` keeps that file out of the tarball entirely.
findings.impact: Four authored articles (~44 KB of .Rmd, including the only real-data P1 and P3 walkthroughs and the LLM-KG benchmark) are dead content: they 404 on the published site and are absent from the installed package. An installed-package user following the package-level man page gets `Error: vignette 'pilar5-soilgrids-br' not found`. Because the pkgdown workflow's `fail_ci_if_error` is not set for missing hrefs, CI stays green while the site ships broken menu entries.
findings.action: Move the four files to `vignettes/articles/` (pkgdown's supported location for non-tarball articles) and add `^vignettes/articles$` to `.Rbuildignore` so they still stay out of the CRAN build; add them to the `_pkgdown.yml` `articles:` index. Then either drop the `vignette("pilar5-soilgrids-br")` reference from `R/edaphos-package.R:153` or change it to a pkgdown URL. Fix the misleading comment at the top of `.github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml`.

findings.title: Two competing release checklists, one stale, pointing at a tarball path that does not exist
findings.correction: none of substance — RELEASE.md:1 "public-release checklist (v2.9.1)" with "four remaining manual actions" vs RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:1 with a different four; the GH-Pages advice does conflict (RELEASE.md:57-72 "Deploy from a branch" / gh-pages vs RELEASE-CHECKLIST:86-92 "GitHub Actions (recommended)"); RELEASE.md:17 still says the badge "currently resolves to v0.2.0"; /tmp/edaphos_release_tarballs does not exist; tools/zenodo_release.zip does not exist and is .gitignore'd. One line-number slip: the .zip is .gitignore line 65, not 60. Both files are .Rbuildignore'd (:19 RELEASE.md, :24 the checklist). Duplicate of the later "Two competing release checklists contradict each other ..." finding, which is the better-evidenced version.
findings.evidence: `RELEASE.md:1` is headed "public-release checklist (v2.9.1)" and :3 claims "four remaining manual actions"; `RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:1` is a second checklist with a different four. They overlap and conflict: RELEASE.md:57-72 tells the maintainer to set GH Pages Source = "Deploy from a branch" / `gh-pages`, while RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:88-92 recommends "GitHub Actions (recommended)" instead. RELEASE.md:15-18 is about a "v2.9.0+" Zenodo DOI badge that "currently resolves to v0.2.0". RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:13-15 says the tarball "is already built at /tmp/edaphos_release_tarballs/edaphos_3.10.0.tar.gz (17 MB)" — that directory does not exist (`ls: No such file or directory`). Its Zenodo step (:51-56) says "The bundle is already built at tools/zenodo_release.zip (22.2 MB, 24 files)": that file is `.gitignore`d (line 60) and present only in the maintainer's local clone. Only `RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md` is Rbuildignored (`.Rbuildignore` line `^RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3\.10\.0\.md$`); `RELEASE.md` is too (`^RELEASE\.md$`).
findings.impact: There is no single authoritative "what is left to do" for the release. A maintainer resuming after a gap has to reconcile two documents with contradictory GH-Pages advice, and both reference artifacts (the /tmp tarball, tools/zenodo_release.zip) that are absent or machine-local, so neither checklist can be executed as written without re-running the build steps neither document specifies.
findings.action: Delete or archive `RELEASE.md` (superseded) and make `RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md` the single source; replace its two "already built at" claims with the commands that build them (`devtools::build()` and `edaphos_zenodo_release(...)` per RELEASE.md:22-31), since neither artifact survives a fresh clone. Pick one GH-Pages recommendation.

findings.title: Three exported functions with .Rd pages and pkgdown entries are permanent stop() stubs
findings.evidence: `R/foundation_tiles.R:183-191` `foundation_tile_source_modis <- function(...) stop("MODIS ingestion requires NASA EarthData credentials...")`; its roxygen at :168-172 says "the implementation will be filled in once the package takes a harder dependency on a MODIS client" and `@return Nothing; always stops`. `R/foundation_tiles.R:203-210` `foundation_tile_source_era5 <- function(...) stop("ERA5 ingestion requires a Copernicus CDS key...")`. Both are `@export`ed and both are swept into the pkgdown "Pilar 4 — Foundation Models" reference group by `_pkgdown.yml:143 starts_with("foundation_")`. `R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:355-357`: `if (object$backend == "spBayes") stop("predict() for spBayes backend is not yet implemented; use the pure-R gibbs backend for v2.3.0.")` — while `spBayes` is in DESCRIPTION Suggests:71 and `bhs_fit()` accepts that backend. Contrast `R/pillars_roadmap.R:13`, which lists the tile pipeline among Pillar 4's "implemented" deliverables without qualification.
findings.impact: Three documented, exported API surfaces are guaranteed failures. A user who follows the pkgdown Pillar 4 index and calls `foundation_tile_source_modis()` on the strength of the roadmap's "planetary-scale tile pipeline" claim gets an error, not data. Worse, `bhs_fit(..., backend = "spBayes")` succeeds and then `predict()` on the result dead-ends — an inconsistent contract inside one pillar, and the reason the DESCRIPTION-advertised spBayes path cannot be used end-to-end.
findings.action: For the two tile sources: either mark them `@keywords internal` / unexport until implemented, or add an explicit "not implemented" note to `R/pillars_roadmap.R:13` and the `_pkgdown.yml:142-148` group description so the roadmap stops describing them as delivered. For spBayes: implement `predict()` for that backend or have `bhs_fit()` reject `backend = "spBayes"` up front with the same message, so the failure happens at fit time rather than after the sampler has run.

findings.title: v1.3.2 (MoCo v2 200k-step encoder) is 43 % short of target and the checkpoint exists nowhere in the repository
findings.correction: In-repo facts confirmed: README.md:1714 marks v1.3.2 🚧; README.md:1579-1581 says "v2 is in training, v1.3.2 will re-benchmark"; .gitignore:49 excludes tools/pretrain/edaphos-cerrado-moco-v2/ and the directory does not exist here; the registry row has NA url/sha256/doi/published_at; V1_3_2_HANDOFF.md:20/:32 claim resume at epoch 110000; Step 5 (HANDOFF:141-159, "clay -> SOC stage-1 F currently 2.7 with v1") is untested. But the quantitative core is UNVERIFIABLE from this repository: `tools/pretrain/train_v2.log` does not exist (tools/pretrain/*.log is .gitignore'd at line 34; tools/pretrain holds only README.md, UPLOAD_INSTRUCTIONS.md, V1_3_2_HANDOFF.md, ZENODO_DEPOSIT_README.md, package_v2_for_zenodo.R, wire_up_v2_doi.R). The "last line is [ep 114440/200000]", the "43 % short / 85 560 steps remaining" figure, and the inventory of the maintainer's checkpoints/ directory are all claims about an out-of-tree working copy that no repository artefact corroborates.
findings.evidence: README.md:1714 `| v1.3.2  | Re-benchmark with MoCo v2 encoder (200 k steps)        | 🚧   |`. README.md:1173-1174 and :1579-1581 both state "v2 is in training, v1.3.2 will re-benchmark"; NEWS.md:1644-1646 repeats it. `tools/pretrain/edaphos-cerrado-moco-v2/` is listed in `.gitignore:34` and does not exist in this worktree (`ls: No such file or directory`). In the maintainer's parent clone the directory contains ONLY `checkpoints/{encoder_k.pt, encoder_q.pt, queue.pt, state.rds}` dated Apr 23 17:19 — no top-level `encoder_q.pt`, no `metadata.json`, no `loss_history.rds`, no `.sha256`. `tools/pretrain/train_v2.log` last line is `[ep 114440/200000] InfoNCE loss = 0.1616`. tools/pretrain/V1_3_2_HANDOFF.md:20,32 claim resume lands at "epoch 110000"; the real state is ~114 440, i.e. 85 560 steps (~1.9 h MPS) still to run.
findings.impact: Three independent published claims are unfulfillable until this compute finishes: (1) the R/foundation_weights.R registry row `edaphos-cerrado-moco-v2` has NA url/sha256/doi/published_at; (2) the README honest-benchmark table at :1567-1581 cannot be updated; (3) the optional Step 5 IV re-benchmark (HANDOFF.md:141-159, "clay -> SOC stage-1 F currently 2.7 with v1") — described as "the FAIR test the v1.3.0 NEWS asked for" — is still untested. Also, because the checkpoint is untracked and machine-local, nobody but the maintainer on that specific Mac can resume; a lost laptop loses 114k steps of training.
findings.action: Run `Rscript data-raw/pretrain_cerrado_train_v2.R` to completion (needs `tools/pretrain/cerrado_stack.tif`, 108 MB, also gitignored, plus `cerrado_dataset_meta.rds` — see data-raw/pretrain_cerrado_train_v2.R:23-33). Before that, fix the wire-up bug above. Consider archiving the intermediate `checkpoints/state.rds` to Zenodo or a release asset so the run is resumable off-machine, and correct the stale "epoch 110000" figures in V1_3_2_HANDOFF.md:20,32.

findings.title: Pretrained-weight DOI is real but the v2 registry row is all-NA while claiming a nonexistent version; CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json are many releases stale and assign one DOI to ten releases
findings.correction: none — every element verified. R/foundation_weights.R:66/:70/:74/:79 give the complete v1 row (url, 64-hex sha256, doi 10.5281/zenodo.19701276, published_at) with enforcement at :214-221; :67/:71/:75/:80 are all NA_character_ for v2 while :82 declares `edaphos_version = c("1.2.0", "3.11.0")` — and 3.11.0 exists nowhere (DESCRIPTION:3 is 3.10.0, NEWS.md's newest heading is 3.10.0, though `git rev-list v3.10.0..HEAD` does contain 7400a2c "feat(v3.11.0): hand-off package…"). CITATION.cff:109 version "2.1.0", :110 date-released "2026-04-23", :112 doi 10.5281/zenodo.19683708, :184 preferred-citation version "1.6.0" — three versions, none 3.10.0; the identifiers block assigns the identical 10.5281/zenodo.19710162 to v1.6.0, v1.7.0, v1.7.1, v1.7.2, v1.8.0, v1.8.1, v1.8.2, v1.9.0, v1.9.1, v1.9.2, v2.0.0 and v2.1.0 (12 entries, so "ten-plus" is if anything conservative), with nothing for v2.2.0–v3.10.0, and 19683708 is simultaneously labelled "Concept DOI (all versions)" and used as the release doi and README badge. .zenodo.json has neither version nor doi and its description is six-pillar/v1.8.0-era. The v2-supersedes promise is confirmed at data-raw/case_cerrado_run.R:86-103 and vignette:64-67 with README.md:1714 still 🚧. Overlaps findings 3 and 18 on the metadata half, but the registry analysis is its own contribution.
findings.evidence:
**Registry (`R/foundation_weights.R:48-84`).** The v1 row is complete and internally consistent: `url = "https://zenodo.org/records/19701276/files/encoder_q.pt"`, `sha256 = "44ace7f78c658b6028f1cf5ccfa624023295e5576f681d0135db64726c6738e8"` (64 hex chars), `doi = "10.5281/zenodo.19701276"`, `published_at = "2026-04-22T21:59:12Z"`, and it matches `README.md:1172`. Verification is enforced, not advisory (`:215-221` stops on mismatch). The v2 row is `NA_character_` for `url`, `sha256` and `doi` (`:67,:71,:75`) yet declares `edaphos_version = "3.11.0"` (`:82`) — a version that does not exist (DESCRIPTION says `3.10.0`, and `NEWS.md` has no 3.11.0 section despite `HEAD~1` being `7400a2c feat(v3.11.0): hand-off package for the v1.3.2 MoCo v2 publish pipeline`).

**CITATION.cff.** `:109 version: "2.1.0"`, `:110 date-released: "2026-04-23"`, `:112 doi: "10.5281/zenodo.19683708"`, and `:184-185 preferred-citation: version: "1.6.0"` — three different versions, none of them 3.10.0. The `identifiers:` block (`:115-156`) assigns the **identical** value `10.5281/zenodo.19710162` as the "Version DOI" for v1.6.0, v1.7.0, v1.7.1, v1.7.2, v1.8.0, v1.8.1, v1.8.2, v1.9.0, v1.9.1, v1.9.2, v2.0.0 and v2.1.0 — ten-plus releases sharing one version DOI, which Zenodo does not do (it mints one per deposit). No entries exist for v2.2.0–v3.10.0. `19683708` is simultaneously labelled "Concept DOI (all versions)" (`:117`) and used as the release `doi:` (`:112`) and in the README badge (`README.md:7`) and BibTeX (`README.md:1737`), conflating concept and version DOI.

**.zenodo.json.** No `version` and no `doi` field at all. Its `description` opens "organised across **six research pillars**" (DESCRIPTION:5 says ten) and its narrative ends at v1.8.0 — so a deposit minted from this file would be labelled as v1.8.0-era six-pillar software.
findings.impact: The one genuinely published artefact (the MoCo v1 encoder) is properly citable and hash-verified — that part is done right. Everything above it is not: a citing author following `CITATION.cff` cites v2.1.0 or v1.6.0 for behaviour that only exists in v3.10.0, and the duplicated version DOIs mean no specific release of v1.6.0–v2.1.0 can be uniquely cited. The registry advertises a v2 encoder that cannot be downloaded, and `data-raw/case_cerrado_run.R:86-103` plus `vignettes/case-cerrado-end-to-end.Rmd:64-67` promise it supersedes v1 "when the v2 deposit is live" — a promise open since v1.3.2 and still 🚧 at `README.md:1714`.
findings.action: 1. Bump `CITATION.cff:109` and `:184` to 3.10.0 with the correct `date-released`, and either supply the real per-release Zenodo version DOIs or delete the `identifiers:` block rather than repeating one DOI ten times. 2. Add `"version": "3.10.0"` to `.zenodo.json` and rewrite its `description` for ten pillars, or generate it from DESCRIPTION at release time. 3. Change `R/foundation_weights.R:82` from `"3.11.0"` to the version that will actually ship the v2 row, and have `foundation_weights_list()` omit or clearly flag rows with `is.na(doi)` so users are not offered an undownloadable encoder. 4. Add a release-checklist step in `RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md` asserting DESCRIPTION, NEWS.md, CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json agree on the version.

findings.title: cran-comments.md misstates both the check status and the extdata sizes it uses to justify the install-size NOTE
findings.evidence:
`cran-comments.md:5` and `:21` claim `R CMD check --as-cran` → "**0 errors / 0 warnings / 0 notes**". The package's own release notes disagree in three places: `NEWS.md:357`, `:442` and `:480` all read "R CMD check: 0 errors | **2 warnings** (pre-existing inst/doc) | 0 notes". A live `devtools::test()` additionally produced 2 ERRORS (`test-active-quantum-posterior.R:34` via `R/active_fit.R:56`; `test-foundation-weights.R:33` via `R/foundation_weights.R:294`), so the suite is not green either.

The "Installed size note" (`cran-comments.md:67-96`) itemises `inst/extdata/` to justify exceeding the 5 MB soft cap, and two of its three figures are wrong:
```
cran-comments says              actual (bytes)
benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7.rds  "0.7 MB"   →  1,959,632  (1.9 MB, understated 2.7x)
benchmark_wosis_6pilar.rds    "4.5 MB"   →  4,640,252  (4.4 MB ✓)
causal_cerrado_real.rds       "1.6 MB"   →     63,521  (62 KB, overstated 26x)
```
`du -sh inst/extdata` = 9.6 MB against the "extra ~8 MB" claimed at `:70-71`.
findings.impact: `cran-comments.md` is read verbatim by CRAN volunteers. A submission asserting 0/0/0 when the maintainer's own NEWS records 2 warnings, backed by an itemisation whose largest single line item is off by 26x, invites rejection and erodes reviewer trust. The same document is the evidence base for the size exemption request, so getting the sizes wrong undermines the argument it exists to make.
findings.action: Regenerate the `cran-comments.md:67-96` itemisation from `file.size(list.files("inst/extdata", full.names = TRUE))` rather than by hand. Reconcile `:5`/`:21` with the actual check output — report the 2 inst/doc warnings and explain them, or fix them. Resolve the two live test errors before submitting: pass `num.trees >= 100` (or a `quantreg`-compatible minimum) at the `al_fit()` call site in `test-active-quantum-posterior.R:34`, and reorder the argument validation in `foundation_moco_*()` so the `n_channels` check precedes `.moco_require_torch()` at `R/foundation_weights.R:294` — the current order makes `test-foundation-weights.R:33` unable to observe the error it asserts on any machine without torch.

findings.title: Four mutually incompatible definitions of the headline benchmark's target variable across README, vignette and runner
findings.correction: Two of the four "definitions" are misattributed, including the one presented as the ground truth. (1) README.md:1611 `soc | **Target** — SOC, **0–5 cm**` sits inside the section "### `br_cerrado` — 45 × 45 synthetic surrogate" (README.md:1596) — it documents a column of the SYNTHETIC bundled dataset, not the 1095-profile WoSIS target. (4) The claim that the code computes a 0–30 cm depth-weighted average is REFUTED: `.soc_mean_0_30` (data-raw/case_cerrado_prepare.R:219) and `.stock_0_30` (:233) are DEAD CODE — `grep -rn 'soc_mean_0_30|stock_0_30'` finds only their definitions, no call site. The live path that actually produces `soc_topsoil_gkg` is :312-338: `candidates <- sub[sub$upper_depth == 0 & sub$lower_depth >= 5 & sub$lower_depth <= 30 & ...]`, shortest-first, with positional uncertainty <= 2 km (:282) — which MATCHES vignettes/case-cerrado-end-to-end.Rmd:44-46 exactly. WHAT SURVIVES, and is real: (i) the same vignette contradicts itself at :142-143 ("`upper_depth == 0 AND lower_depth ≤ 10 cm` (genuine 0–10 cm topsoil), `positional_uncertainty ≤ 500 m`"), repeated at :165, :180 and :353 ("302-profile clean 0–10 cm Cerrado dataset"), against the code's 5–30 cm / 2 km; and (ii) the scale confusion is confirmed — data-raw/case_cerrado_run.R:30-32 and :22 and vignette:75 all say log1p, while `.resp_col <- "soc_topsoil_gkg"` (:82) is raw g/kg, `.back_transform` (:75) has zero call sites, :200 says "(linear scale)", :179-183 uses `type = "response"`, and vignette:51-53 states the opposite of :75. So the physical quantity IS determinable from the code (surface-anchored 5–30 cm horizon, raw g/kg); it is the prose that disagrees with itself.
findings.evidence:
Four different specifications of how the 1095 "topsoil" SOC values were selected:
1. `README.md:1611` — "`soc` | **Target** — SOC, **0–5 cm** (g kg⁻¹)"
2. `vignettes/case-cerrado-end-to-end.Rmd:43-46` — "v1.3.1 requires `upper_depth == 0` and the shallowest qualifying surface-anchored horizon (**lower_depth in 5–30 cm**) ... Positional uncertainty is capped at **2 km**"
3. `vignettes/case-cerrado-end-to-end.Rmd` §3 — "After the v1.3.1 quality gates — `upper_depth == 0 AND lower_depth ≤ 10 cm` (**genuine 0–10 cm topsoil**), `positional_uncertainty ≤ 500 m`"
4. The actual code, `data-raw/case_cerrado_prepare.R:220-221` and `:235-240` — `keep <- df_orgc_profile$upper_depth < 30 & df_orgc_profile$lower_depth > 0`, followed by depth-weighted averaging with `u <- pmax(h$upper_depth, 0); l <- pmin(h$lower_depth, 30)` — a **0–30 cm interval average** that does not require any horizon starting at 0 cm at all.

So a profile whose shallowest measurement is 20–30 cm qualifies under the code but is excluded under all three prose descriptions. Depth-comparability across profiles is precisely what the vignette claims v1.3.1 fixed (`:37-46`: "v1.3.0 treated any horizon with `lower_depth ≤ 30 cm` as 'topsoil', mixing 0–5 cm and 10–30 cm layers").

The scale of the metrics is equally contradictory. `data-raw/case_cerrado_run.R:30-32` header: "Target: **log1p(SOC, g/kg)**. Point estimate = back-transformed MEDIAN"; `:22`: B2 kriges "on the **log1p-scale** residuals"; `vignettes/case-cerrado-end-to-end.Rmd:71`: B1 "target = $\log(1 + \text{SOC})$". But the code sets `.resp_col <- "soc_topsoil_gkg"` (`:82`, raw g/kg), the helper `.back_transform <- function(z) expm1(pmax(z, 0))` (`:75`) is **defined and never called**, `:200` says "(linear scale)", and `:179-183` uses `type = "response"` (bagged mean) not the median the header promises. `vignettes/case-cerrado-end-to-end.Rmd:51-53` states the opposite of line 71: "Log-transformation of the target also hurts on this dataset (R² 0.17 log vs 0.22 linear on 5-fold CV) so we train on the raw g/kg scale."

Because `data-raw/case_cerrado_prepare.R` is unrunnable (see the .gitignore finding), a reader cannot resolve which specification produced the shipped numbers.
findings.impact: Neither the physical quantity being predicted nor the scale on which RMSE = 13.51 g/kg was computed can be determined from the repository.
