Comparison against the published Cerrado SOC literature that `README.md:1576-1578` invokes ("R² ≈ 0.22–0.23 is in line with published regional Brazilian / Cerrado SOC DSM") is meaningless if the target is a 0–30 cm depth-weighted average rather than 0–5 cm topsoil concentration — those are different variables with different achievable R².
findings.action: Read the actual filter out of `data-raw/case_cerrado_prepare.R:220-240`, write it down once in a single authoritative place, and make `README.md:1611`, `vignettes/case-cerrado-end-to-end.Rmd:43-46`, its §3 prose, and the `data-raw/case_cerrado_run.R:8-32` header all point at it. Delete the dead `.back_transform` at `:75` and the stale log1p claims at `:22,:30-32` and `vignettes/case-cerrado-end-to-end.Rmd:71`. Remove the duplicated near-identical filter blocks at `case_cerrado_prepare.R:220-225` / `:235-240` so there is one code path.

findings.title: README's headline benchmark tables are two to four release cycles stale, and the current 6-method result exists only in NEWS.md
findings.correction: I read every artefact's stamp directly and all eight cited values are exact (case_cerrado 1.3.1, causal_cerrado_real 1.3.1, causal_discovery_results 1.7.1, llm_benchmark_results 1.7.2 + mode=simulated, quantum_foundation_cerrado 1.9.2, benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7 2.7.0, benchmark_wosis_6pilar 3.3.0, temporal_cerrado_results no version field). `grep -in '6-pilar|six-pilar|6 pilar' README.md` returns ZERO matches while NEWS.md:421-428 holds the current v3.4.0 six-method table with P1 Causal+OLS best (RMSE 13.94, R^2 0.082) and P10 GAT last (15.18). case_cerrado_results.rds$covariate_cols has length 59 and contains lon, lat and year, against README.md:1568's "56 covariates". quantum_foundation_cerrado.rds has n_train = 250 in every fold and n_profiles_used = 1081 against README.md:1404's "1 095". causal_iv_cerrado_real.rds$extraction_seconds = 1.359 against README.md:841's "O(minutes)". The inst/extdata size table is off by up to ~31x (causal_cerrado_real.rds "~2 MB" vs 62 KB; cerrado_abstracts.jsonl "~40 KB" vs 4.9 KB; cerrado_claims_real_corpus.jsonl "~400 KB" vs 94 KB) and omits benchmark_wosis_6pilar.rds (4.6 MB), benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7.rds (2.0 MB) and llm_kg_smoke_claims.jsonl entirely. Two corrections: "No artefact's self-declared version matches the release the documentation attributes it to" is overbroad — causal_iv_cerrado_real.rds is stamped 3.10.0 — and a bundle computed at v2.7.0 and shipped in v2.8.0 is normal release hygiene, not staleness; the lon/lat/year addition IS documented, in data-raw/case_cerrado_run.R:54-63, just not in the README. Small numeric slips in the finding: 13.92/15.20 should be 13.94/15.18.
findings.evidence:
Artefact provenance stamps versus `DESCRIPTION: Version: 3.10.0`:
```
case_cerrado_results.rds        ver=1.3.1    (README §Benchmarks, lines 1566-1570)
causal_cerrado_real.rds        ver=1.3.1    (README lines 632-636)
causal_discovery_results.rds   ver=1.7.1    (README lines 649-654)
llm_benchmark_results.rds      ver=1.7.2  mode=simulated  (README lines 676-680)
quantum_foundation_cerrado.rds ver=1.9.2    (README lines 1406-1411, attributed to v2.0.0)
benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7.rds   ver=2.7.0    (README lines 246-250, attributed to v2.8.0)
benchmark_wosis_6pilar.rds     ver=3.3.0    (NEWS.md 421-428, attributed to v3.4.0)
temporal_cerrado_results.rds   ver=(absent)
```
No artefact's self-declared version matches the release the documentation attributes it to.

The README's flagship cross-pillar table (`README.md:243-255`) is the **three**-method v2.8.0 result, still captioned "First honest cross-pillar comparison" and "All three tie at ~14.1 g/kg RMSE". It has been superseded twice — by the six-method v3.1.0 table (`NEWS.md:601-608`) and again by the recalibrated v3.4.0 table (`NEWS.md:421-428`, matching the shipped `benchmark_wosis_6pilar.rds$cv_aggregate`) — and `grep -n "6-pilar|six-pilar"` over `README.md` returns **zero** matches. A reader of the README never learns that P1 Causal+OLS has the best RMSE (13.92) and R² (0.082) of all six methods, nor that P10 GAT sits last at 15.20.

Secondary numeric mismatches in the same area: `README.md:1568` says "56 covariates" but `case_cerrado_results.rds$covariate_cols` has **59** and includes `lon`, `lat` and `year` (added at `data-raw/case_cerrado_run.R:54-63`, never mentioned in the README). `README.md:1404` says the quantum benchmark is "5-fold spatial CV on **1 095** Cerrado profiles" but `quantum_foundation_cerrado.rds$cv_table$n_train` is **250** in every fold and `n_profiles_used` is 1081. `README.md:841` says embedding extraction is "O(minutes) for 1 095 WoSIS profiles on Apple M1 Max MPS" against `causal_iv_cerrado_real.rds$extraction_seconds = 1.36`. `inst/extdata` sizes at `README.md:1615-1632` are wrong by up to 32x (`causal_cerrado_real.rds` claimed "~2 MB", actual 62 KB; `cerrado_abstracts.jsonl` "~40 KB", actual 4.9 KB), and the two largest files (`benchmark_wosis_6pilar.rds` 4.6 MB, `benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7.rds` 2.0 MB) are absent from the table.
findings.impact: The README is the primary scientific document and it advertises a superseded three-method comparison as the state of the art while the shipped bundle contains a six-method result with a different winner. Readers cannot map any published number to the artefact or release that produced it. The "56 covariates" error conceals that coordinates and sampling year are model features — material information for interpreting a spatial-CV benchmark.
findings.action: Promote the v3.4.0 six-method table from `NEWS.md:421-428` into `README.md`, replacing or clearly superseding `README.md:243-255`, and stamp each README table with the artefact and version it came from (e.g. "computed at v3.4.0 from `inst/extdata/benchmark_wosis_6pilar.rds`"). Correct "56 covariates" → 59 and disclose `lon`/`lat`/`year`. Correct the quantum caption to state the 250-row per-fold training cap and n = 1081. Regenerate the `inst/extdata` size table with `file.size()` and add the two benchmark bundles. Fix `README.md:841`.

findings.title: The "LLM-augmented (Gemma 4)" DAG in the causal-discovery trio is six hand-typed edges, not an LLM output
findings.correction: Verified: data-raw/causal_discovery_benchmark.R:118-133 contains the literal `llm_extra_edges` data frame with the six from/to pairs and literal `confidence = c(0.90, 0.82, 0.78, 0.75, 0.72, 0.71)`, prefaced by the comment claiming these are "the same six high-confidence edges that a fresh Ollama + gemma4:latest run returns"; `grep -n 'causal_llm_extract|ollama|cerrado_claims'` over the script matches only comment lines (:8 and :120), so inst/extdata/cerrado_claims.jsonl is never read and no LLM is invoked; the shipped inst/extdata/causal_discovery_results.rds is stamped version 1.7.1. README.md:643-662 presents the SHD of 2 and the 6-vs-0 adjustment-set contrast as "The major scientific finding". Note in mitigation: the script comment is candid about hard-coding — the misrepresentation lives in the README, not the runner.
findings.evidence:
`README.md:643-662` presents "### 🆕 v1.7.2 — Causal-discovery trio: expert × LLM × data-driven", reports `| Expert ↔ LLM-augmented (Gemma 4) | **2** |` structural Hamming distance, and calls the result "The **major scientific finding** ... the choice of DAG changes the backdoor adjustment set for MAP → SOC from **6 covariates** (LLM-augmented) to **0 covariates** (bnlearn mmhc)".

No LLM is invoked. `data-raw/causal_discovery_benchmark.R:118-132`:
```r
# We cache a realistic set of Gemma-4-extracted edges for the canonical
# WoSIS column names.  In production this is `cerrado_claims.jsonl`;
# here we hard-code the same six high-confidence edges that a fresh
# Ollama + gemma4:latest run returns on the ten Cerrado-pedology abstracts
llm_extra_edges <- data.frame(
  from = c("wc_bio_12", "wc_bio_01", "wc_landcover_trees", "soilgrids_clay", "slope", "wc_bio_12"),
  to   = c("wc_landcover_trees", "wc_landcover_trees", "soilgrids_bdod", "soilgrids_bdod", "soilgrids_sand", "soilgrids_clay"),
  confidence = c(0.90, 0.82, 0.78, 0.75, 0.72, 0.71))
```
The "confidence" scores are literals. `grep -n "causal_llm_extract\|ollama"` over the script returns nothing. The shipped `inst/extdata/causal_discovery_results.rds` (`version = 1.7.1`) confirms: `edges_expert` 22 rows, `edges_llm_aug` 24 rows, `llm_extra_edges` 6 rows — so SHD(expert, LLM-aug) = 2 is the arithmetic consequence of typing 6 edges of which 2 are new, and the "6 covariates" adjustment set is the 6 hand-written edges.

The bnlearn arm additionally cannot be verified locally — `bnlearn` is not installed and 9 tests skip on it.
findings.impact: The "major scientific finding" that DAG-construction strategies disagree, and the recommendation to "use all three and report sensitivity", rest on a comparison between an expert DAG and the same expert DAG plus six edges the author added by hand. The claim that this is what "a fresh Ollama + gemma4:latest run returns" is asserted in a comment with no cached transcript, no seed, and no way to check — `inst/extdata/cerrado_claims.jsonl` (30 lines) exists but is not read by the script.
findings.action: Either call `causal_llm_extract()` (or read `inst/extdata/cerrado_claims.jsonl`, which the comment names as "production") and derive `llm_extra_edges` from it, committing the raw extraction alongside; or relabel the arm honestly as "expert + literature-derived edges" throughout `README.md:643-662`, `NEWS.md`, and `articles/…`, and drop "(Gemma 4)" and the fabricated per-edge confidence scores.

findings.title: DESCRIPTION's "every vignette runs offline" is false: four advertised vignettes are not vignettes, and the Pilar 4 × Pilar 6 vignette evaluates nothing
findings.evidence:
`DESCRIPTION:28` claims "A synthesised Cerrado dataset is bundled so every vignette runs offline."

(a) **Four of the vignettes listed in `README.md:1644-1662` do not exist as vignettes.** `pilar1-causal-real`, `pilar3-4d-real`, `pilar5-soilgrids-br` and `llm-kg-benchmark` live in `articles/`, and `.Rbuildignore` contains `^articles$` — so they are stripped from the built package. `README.md:1641` tells users to run `browseVignettes("edaphos")`, where they will never appear, and `README.md:702` says `📖 Vignette: vignette("llm-kg-benchmark")`, which errors. The `inst/extdata` table at `README.md:1615-1632` lists these four as the "Used by" consumer for `causal_cerrado_real.rds`, `temporal_cerrado_results.rds`, `cerrado_gold_standard_v1.jsonl` and `llm_benchmark_results.rds` — i.e. four shipped data files have no installed consumer.

(b) **`vignettes/pilar4-pilar6-quantum.Rmd` computes nothing.** It has exactly three chunks and the only two content chunks are both disabled: `:78 ```{r eval = FALSE}` and `:95 ```{r benchmark-table, eval = FALSE}`. The disabled `benchmark-table` chunk is what would render `inst/extdata/quantum_foundation_cerrado.rds`. So the table at `README.md:1406-1411`, which `README.md:1429` sources to `vignette("pilar4-pilar6-quantum")`, appears nowhere in the rendered vignette.

(c) `README.md:1638-1662` also omits `getting-started` entirely, though `NEWS.md:449-481` presents it as the intended entry point.

The offline claim itself does hold for the installed set — every `foundation_weights_load()` call in `vignettes/` is inside an `eval = FALSE` chunk or prose (`case-cerrado-end-to-end.Rmd:70`, `getting-started.Rmd:104`, `pilar1-pilar4-iv.Rmd:393`, `pilar4-simclr-embeddings.Rmd:494,510,524`), and the data-consuming chunks read `system.file("extdata", ...)`. The falsehood is about *which* vignettes exist.
findings.impact: A user following the README to reproduce the Pillar 1 real-data causal results, the Pillar 3 real-data 4D results, the SoilGrids AL loop, or the LLM-KG benchmark hits `vignette()` errors on all four. The single vignette dedicated to the v2.0.0 Pilar 4 × Pilar 6 fusion renders as prose with no numbers, so the README's 4-way head-to-head table has no reproducible presentation anywhere in the installed package.
findings.action: Decide per document: move the four `articles/*.Rmd` into `vignettes/` (they read only `inst/extdata`, so they should build offline), or remove them from the `README.md:1644-1662` table and from the "Used by" column at `:1615-1632`, replacing `vignette("llm-kg-benchmark")` at `:702` with a pkgdown URL. Enable the two chunks in `vignettes/pilar4-pilar6-quantum.Rmd` — the `benchmark-table` chunk only needs `readRDS(system.file(...))` and should evaluate offline. Add `getting-started` to the vignette table. Add a CI check that every `vignette("...")` string in `README.md` resolves in the built package.

findings.title: The flagship case-study benchmark cannot be re-run by anyone: its input is .gitignore'd and its output path is not the shipped artefact
findings.correction: Verified: data-raw/case_cerrado_run.R:43-45 hardcodes tools/case_cerrado/case_cerrado_bundle.rds and ...results.rds behind a `stopifnot(file.exists(bundle_path))`; both paths are .gitignore'd (lines 43-44, alongside the .gml/.tif inputs at 40-42); `ls tools/` shows only make-readme-figures.R, pretrain/ and readme-outputs.txt; no committed script writes inst/extdata/case_cerrado_results.rds, which is stamped `edaphos_ver = 1.3.1`, `created_at = 2026-04-23T00:16:28Z` against DESCRIPTION 3.10.0. One mitigation the auditor omitted: README.md:1594-1596 immediately offers "or read the pre-computed `.rds` shipped at inst/extdata/case_cerrado_results.rds and rebuild every plot via vignette(...)", so the *results* are consumable offline — what is broken is regeneration and provenance, not access.
findings.evidence:
`README.md:1584-1589` instructs:
```bash
Rscript data-raw/case_cerrado_prepare.R   # ~60 min, downloads ~2 GB
Rscript data-raw/case_cerrado_run.R       # ~3 min
```
The second step is unreachable. `data-raw/case_cerrado_run.R:43-45`:
```r
43: bundle_path <- "tools/case_cerrado/case_cerrado_bundle.rds"
44: out_path    <- "tools/case_cerrado/case_cerrado_results.rds"
45: stopifnot(file.exists(bundle_path))
```
`tools/case_cerrado/` **does not exist** in the repository (`ls tools/` → `make-readme-figures.R`, `pretrain`, `readme-outputs.txt`), and `.gitignore` excludes both files explicitly:
```
tools/case_cerrado/case_cerrado_bundle.rds
tools/case_cerrado/case_cerrado_results.rds
```
So `stopifnot` fails immediately on a fresh clone, and even on success the runner writes to a gitignored path — there is no scripted step producing the actually-shipped `inst/extdata/case_cerrado_results.rds`. That artefact is stamped `edaphos_ver = 1.3.1`, `created_at = 2026-04-23T00:16:28Z`, against a DESCRIPTION at `Version: 3.10.0` — roughly thirty releases stale, and the roadmap promise it depends on is still open (`README.md:1714`: `| v1.3.2 | Re-benchmark with MoCo v2 encoder (200 k steps) | 🚧 |`).

Step 1 is itself blocked for a third party: `data-raw/case_cerrado_prepare.R` requires the ISRIC WoSIS WFS endpoint (`:90-112, :171-174`), `geodata::landcover()` (`:403`), and per `README.md:1587` a ~2 GB download.
findings.impact: The benchmark the README nominates as the falsifiable test of its core claim (`vignettes/case-cerrado-end-to-end.Rmd:27-33`: "That is a falsifiable statement. Either it is true on real data, or the README needs to get more modest") is unreproducible by its own author on a clean checkout. There is no audit trail from any committed script to the shipped `.rds`, so the provenance of the headline 13.51 / 13.86 / 14.07 RMSE figures cannot be established.
findings.action: 1. Change `out_path` at `data-raw/case_cerrado_run.R:44` to `inst/extdata/case_cerrado_results.rds` so the committed artefact has a scripted origin. 2. Either commit `case_cerrado_bundle.rds` (the extracted 1095×59 profile frame is small — `causal_cerrado_real.rds` is only 62 KB for a comparable table) or publish it under the existing Zenodo deposit and have the runner fetch + SHA-256 verify it, matching the pattern already implemented in `R/foundation_weights.R:214-221`. 3. Re-run against v3.10.0 and refresh the stamp, or add a dated "computed at v1.3.1" banner to `README.md:1554-1582`.

findings.title: Residual kriging (B2) is fit to in-bag rather than OOB forest residuals, manufacturing the README's PICP conclusion
findings.correction: none — data-raw/case_cerrado_run.R:200-202 verified (`train_mid <- predict(rf_b1, data = train)$predictions` after rf_b1 was fit on `train` at :184-193, i.e. in-bag fitted values), the variogram at :210-219 seeded from `stats::var(train$residual) * 0.5` for both psill and nugget, and `b2_sd <- sqrt(pmax(kr$var1.var, 0))` with `b2_mid ± 1.96 * b2_sd` at :237-240. inst/extdata/case_cerrado_results.rds matches the quoted table and README.md:1576-1579 does read it as science ("much worse PICP (0.82 vs 0.94)", "plain QRF is the calibration champion"). The n = 1095/910/923 footnote at README.md:1569-1574 confirms the three-different-test-sets objection. One thing the finding UNDERSTATES: `b2_mid <- pred_b1[test_ix] + kr$var1.pred` but the B2 interval is built from the kriging variance ALONE, discarding B1's forest predictive uncertainty entirely — so the too-narrow interval is over-determined and the "one-line fix" (swap to `rf_b1$predictions`) would not by itself repair PICP. Severity deflated: this lives in .Rbuildignore'd data-raw/ and handicaps a baseline, not package functionality — though the README conclusion built on it is unsupported.
findings.evidence:
`data-raw/case_cerrado_run.R:200-202`:
```r
200:  # --- B2 B1 + residual kriging (linear scale) -------------------------------
201:  train_mid <- predict(rf_b1, data = train)$predictions
202:  train$residual <- train[[.resp_col]] - train_mid
```
`rf_b1` was fit on `train` at `:185-193`, so `predict(rf_b1, data = train)` returns **in-bag** fitted values. The resulting residuals are shrunk far below true error, so the variogram fitted at `:206-219` (`psill = var(train$residual) * 0.5`, `nugget = var(train$residual) * 0.5`) understates the semivariance, and the kriging variance at `:237` (`b2_sd <- sqrt(pmax(kr$var1.var, 0))`) produces intervals that are too narrow: `pred_b2_lo/hi <- b2_mid ± 1.96 * b2_sd`.

The consequence is the headline finding. `inst/extdata/case_cerrado_results.rds$results`:
```
B1 ranger            n=1095  rmse=13.51  r2=0.2189  picp=0.9443  interval_score=65.81
B2 ranger + kriging  n= 910  rmse=13.86  r2=0.2329  picp=0.8165  interval_score=99.52
```
`README.md:1576-1579` reads this as science: "Residual kriging gains +0.01 R² over B1 **at the cost of much worse PICP (0.82 vs 0.94)**. The **plain QRF is the calibration champion**."

ranger exposes the OOB predictions as `rf_b1$predictions`; the fix is one line. Note also that `B2` is scored on n = 910 and `E` on n = 923 against `B1`'s 1095 (`README.md:1569-1574` footnote), so the R² comparison the "Honest reading" makes is across three different test sets.
findings.impact: The README's central methodological claim about the classical DSM stack — that residual kriging trades calibration for accuracy — is an artifact of using in-bag residuals, not a property of kriging. This is the specific comparison the package uses to argue it is "beyond the regression-tree state of the art", so the baseline is handicapped by a one-line bug in exactly the metric where the package claims a win.
findings.action: Replace `predict(rf_b1, data = train)$predictions` at `:201` with `rf_b1$predictions` (ranger's OOB predictions), re-run, and update `inst/extdata/case_cerrado_results.rds` and `README.md:1566-1582`. Additionally, restrict all three methods to the common 910-row intersection so the RMSE/MAE/R²/PICP columns are comparable, and state the intersection size in the table rather than three different `n` values with a footnote.

findings.title: The spBayes backend is advertised as an equal peer in README/NEWS/man but predict(), as_edaphos_posterior() and al_query_bhs() all fail on it
findings.correction: none — all three gaps verified at the cited lines. R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:355-357 is the clean `stop("predict() for spBayes backend is not yet implemented; use the pure-R gibbs backend for v2.3.0.")` (stale v2.3.0 pointer shipped at v3.10.0); R/bridges_active_learning_v3.R:263-264 is `if (bhs_fit$backend != "gibbs") stop("al_query_bhs() currently supports backend = 'gibbs' only.")`; `as_edaphos_posterior.edaphos_bhs` at :411-419 has no backend guard and hits `sweep(fitted_mat, 2L, x$w_post_mean, "+")` at :418, and the spBayes `out <- list(...)` at :156-164 omits w_post_mean/phi_hat/nmcmc/burn/thin. I reproduced the failure exactly: `sweep(matrix(1:6,2,3), 2L, NULL, "+")` emits `no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf` then `Error: 'data' must be of a vector type, was 'NULL'`. Advertising verified at README.md:272, README.md:1709, NEWS.md:1054-1063, man/bhs_fit.Rd:32-34, and `grep 'spBayes|gibbs' man/predict.edaphos_bhs.Rd man/as_edaphos_posterior.Rd man/al_query_bhs.Rd` returns nothing. SEVERITY DEFLATED: reaching the crash requires installing a heavy Suggests-only package (DESCRIPTION:71) and opting into a backend the code itself labels "alternative"; two of the three paths already stop cleanly.
findings.evidence:
Three of the four documented methods on `edaphos_bhs` do not work for `backend = "spBayes"`:
1. R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:355-357 -- clean stop, but with a stale version pointer shipped at v3.10.0:
```r
if (object$backend == "spBayes")
  stop("predict() for spBayes backend is not yet implemented; ",
        "use the pure-R gibbs backend for v2.3.0.", call. = FALSE)
```
2. R/bridges_active_learning_v3.R:263-265 -- `if (bhs_fit$backend != "gibbs") stop("al_query_bhs() currently supports backend = 'gibbs' only.")`
3. `as_edaphos_posterior.edaphos_bhs` (R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:411-419) has NO backend guard and dereferences `x$w_post_mean` at line 418, which the spBayes branch (R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:155-165) never sets -- that `out <- list(...)` omits `w_post_mean`, `phi_hat`, `nmcmc`, `burn`, `thin` and the prior fields.
Advertised without any caveat in: README.md:272 ("optional `spBayes::spLM` backend"), README.md:1709 (v2.3.0 row marked ✅), NEWS.md:1054-1063 (lists both backends, then lists `predict.edaphos_bhs` and `as_edaphos_posterior.edaphos_bhs` as delivered features), man/bhs_fit.Rd:32-34. Verified: `grep spBayes|gibbs man/predict.edaphos_bhs.Rd man/as_edaphos_posterior.Rd man/al_query_bhs.Rd` returns nothing -- zero caveats in the reference manual.
findings.impact: A user who follows README.md:272 and installs the Suggests-only `spBayes` gets a fit object on which the only usable method is `print()`. `predict()` and `al_query_bhs()` at least stop cleanly; `as_edaphos_posterior()` crashes with a message that names none of the relevant concepts. Reproduced the exact failure: `sweep(matrix(1:6,2,3), 2L, NULL, "+")` -> `Error: 'data' must be of a vector type, was 'NULL'` plus a spurious `max()` warning. The spBayes path is effectively dead weight that costs a Suggests dependency (DESCRIPTION:71) and a documented promise.
findings.action: Minimum: add a `backend` guard to `as_edaphos_posterior.edaphos_bhs` at R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:412 mirroring the one at :355 so it fails with a readable message; fix the stale "for v2.3.0" text in the :356 message to name the current version; and add an explicit `\note{}` to man/bhs_fit.Rd, man/predict.edaphos_bhs.Rd and README.md:272 stating that only `gibbs`/`rcpp` support prediction, posterior extraction and active-learning queries. Better: have the spBayes branch populate `w_post_mean` from `fit_sp$p.w.recover.samples` and `phi_hat` from `median(theta_draws[,"phi"])`, which would make all three methods work.

findings.title: bhs_fit()'s rcpp backend is absent from its own @param documentation, and al_query_bhs() rejects it despite the fit being complete
findings.evidence:
The signature offers three backends -- R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:84:
```r
backend = c("gibbs", "rcpp", "spBayes"),
```
but the roxygen `@param backend` at R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:68-70 documents only two:
```
#' @param backend One of `"gibbs"` (pure-R Gibbs sampler, default,
#'   no external deps), `"spBayes"` (dispatches to `spBayes::spLM`
#'   when available).
```
This propagates verbatim to man/bhs_fit.Rd:32-34, whose `\usage{}` at :11 nonetheless shows `backend = c("gibbs", "rcpp", "spBayes")`. So the reference manual lists a valid value it never explains. The rcpp path itself is fully implemented and returns a complete object including `phi_hat` and `w_post_mean` (R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:207-229) -- yet R/bridges_active_learning_v3.R:263-265 excludes it anyway:
```r
if (bhs_fit$backend != "gibbs")
  stop("al_query_bhs() currently supports backend = 'gibbs' only.", call. = FALSE)
```
The guard uses `!= "gibbs"` where the actual requirement (`phi_hat`, `w_post_mean`, `coords`, `beta_draws`) is satisfied by rcpp too; only spBayes lacks them. tests/testthat/test-bridges-v3.R:197 pokes at this by assigning `fit$backend <- "spBayes"` to "simulate other backend for the guard", so the guard's rcpp exclusion is untested.
findings.impact: Users cannot discover the `rcpp` backend from `?bhs_fit` even though it is the documented v3.5.0 headline (a claimed 5-15x speedup, R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:203-205). Users who do find it and follow the Pillar 7 x Pillar 5 bridge advertised at R/bridges_active_learning_v3.R:238 are then blocked from `al_query_bhs()` by a guard that is stricter than its own precondition -- so choosing the fast backend silently costs them a documented cross-pillar feature, for no technical reason.
findings.action: Add `"rcpp"` to the `@param backend` block at R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:68-70 (describing the RcppArmadillo fast path) and re-roxygenise. Relax R/bridges_active_learning_v3.R:263 to `if (!bhs_fit$backend %in% c("gibbs", "rcpp"))` and add a test in tests/testthat/test-bridges-v3.R that `al_query_bhs()` succeeds on a `backend = "rcpp"` fit.

findings.title: al_fit() performs no validation of num.trees against nrow(labeled), producing an opaque ranger error; the guarding test is unseeded and fails ~12% of runs
findings.correction: Code facts and the 12% figure are right; the "per-run flake" framing is wrong. Verified: R/active_fit.R:1-10 hardcodes `quantreg = TRUE, keep.inbag = TRUE`; :52-56 validates covariates/coords but never num.trees; roxygen at :29 is only "Integer, number of trees (default 500)."; DESCRIPTION:83 is a bare `ranger,`; installed ranger is 0.18.0 with the `minoob < 10` stop. I independently measured 24/200 = 12.0% at the exact shape (n=40, 1 covariate, 50 trees, quantreg, keep.inbag) and 0/200 at 100 trees — matching the finding. BUT the conclusion "the test suite has a genuinely stochastic 12%-per-run failure" and "a green CI run is ~88% luck on this one test" is refuted: test-active-quantum-posterior.R:7 calls `set.seed(1L)`, so the RNG state at :34 is deterministic within any full-file/full-suite run, and I reproduced the failure 3/3 by replaying that stream. 12% is the across-seeds rate, not the across-runs rate. Part (a) — no lower-bound guidance for a function whose whole use case is small labelled sets — is the durable content. Duplicate of finding 12.
findings.evidence:
R/active_fit.R:1-13 forwards `num.trees` straight into ranger with `quantreg = TRUE` and no lower-bound check:
```r
.fit_core <- function(labeled, target, covariates, num.trees, ...) {
  form <- stats::reformulate(covariates, response = target)
  fit <- ranger::ranger(formula = form, data = labeled, num.trees = num.trees,
                        quantreg = TRUE, keep.inbag = TRUE, ...)
```
`al_fit` (R/active_fit.R:51-56) validates covariates and coords via `.assert_covariates` / `.assert_coords` but never `num.trees`. DESCRIPTION:82 imports `ranger` with no version bound; installed version is 0.18.0, whose OOB-quantreg guard raises "Too few trees for out-of-bag quantile regression" -- the live test ERROR 1.
The failing call site, tests/testthat/test-active-quantum-posterior.R:30-35, sets NO seed:
```r
test_that("as_edaphos_posterior.edaphos_al_model requires newdata", {
  skip_if_not_installed("ranger")
  df <- data.frame(x = stats::rnorm(40L), y = stats::rnorm(40L))
  fit <- al_fit(df, target = "y", covariates = "x", num.trees = 50L)
```
Measured the flake rate directly with ranger 0.18.0 over the exact shape (n=40, 1 covariate, 50 trees, quantreg=TRUE, keep.inbag=TRUE): **24 failures out of 200 seeds = 12%**. Same shape at 100 trees: 0 failures. Every other `al_fit` test uses >= 100 trees (tests/testthat/test-active.R:40,55,70,78,148,157; test-physics-gate.R:25,45,72), so :34 is the lone marginal call.
findings.impact: Two distinct defects. (a) `al_fit()` is the documented entry point of Pillar 5 (`@param num.trees Integer, number of trees (default 500).`, R/active_fit.R:29) and gives no guidance that small forests break quantile regression on small labelled sets -- exactly the regime active learning starts in. The user sees a third-party ranger message with no mention of `al_fit`, `num.trees`, or the fix. (b) The test suite has a genuinely stochastic 12%-per-run failure, which makes NEWS.md's "1 345 tests pass" and "R CMD check: 0 errors" claims unsound: a green CI run is ~88% luck on this one test, and it will intermittently red-flag PRs for reasons unrelated to the change.
findings.action: In R/active_fit.R:53, before `.fit_core`, validate and rethrow: check `num.trees >= 100L` (or better, wrap the `ranger::ranger` call at :3-9 in `tryCatch` and rethrow "Too few trees" as "`al_fit()` needs more trees for out-of-bag quantile regression on n = <nrow> labelled rows; raise `num.trees` (>= 100 recommended, default 500)."). Document the floor at R/active_fit.R:29. Separately, add `set.seed(...)` and raise `num.trees` to 100L at tests/testthat/test-active-quantum-posterior.R:31-34, and add a `ranger (>= 0.18.0)` bound to DESCRIPTION:82 so the guard's behaviour is pinned.

findings.title: foundation_weights_load() requires torch BEFORE resolving the registry, so the placeholder v2 entry reports the wrong reason for failing
findings.correction: none — the ordering is exactly as described: `.moco_require_torch()` is the first statement of `foundation_weights_load()`, the NA-URL guard lives one call deeper inside `foundation_weights_download()` (R/foundation_weights.R:185-190), and `foundation_weights_download("edaphos-cerrado-moco-v2")` called directly does report correctly since it has no torch gate — so the two entry points genuinely disagree. This is the same root cause as "test-foundation-weights.R:29-36 asserts an error message that is unreachable without torch" and duplicates it.
findings.evidence:
R/foundation_weights.R:294 is the FIRST statement in the function body:
```r
foundation_weights_load <- function(source, ...) {
  .moco_require_torch()            # line 294
  if (is.character(source) && length(source) == 1L && !file.exists(source)) {
    loc <- foundation_weights_download(source, ...)   # line 298
```
`.moco_require_torch()` is defined at R/foundation_moco.R:28-34 and stops with "Install the `torch` package to use foundation_moco_*()." The NA-URL guard it pre-empts lives one call deeper, at R/foundation_weights.R:185-190:
```r
if (is.na(entry$url) || !nzchar(entry$url)) {
  stop("Registered entry '", name, "' has no published URL yet ...")
```
Traced code path for `foundation_weights_load("edaphos-cerrado-moco-v2")`: line 294 fires first, unconditionally. So the NA-URL guard does NOT fire before anything else -- it fires only on a torch-equipped machine. This is the same ordering that produced live test ERROR 2 (tests/testthat/test-foundation-weights.R:33 expected `"requires.*n_channels"` -- the guard at R/foundation_weights.R:312-315 -- but received the torch message from line 294).
findings.impact: Today a user without torch calling `foundation_weights_load("edaphos-cerrado-moco-v2")` is told to install torch. torch is a multi-hundred-MB dependency with a separate libtorch runtime download; after paying that cost they hit the real error -- the weights were never published. Users with torch get the correct message. The registry-resolution and URL-availability checks are pure metadata operations that need no torch at all, so the cheap deterministic guard is gated behind the expensive one. Note `foundation_weights_download("edaphos-cerrado-moco-v2")` (no torch gate) already reports correctly, so the two entry points disagree.
findings.action: Move registry resolution ahead of the torch gate in R/foundation_weights.R:287-301: call `.foundation_weights_entry(source)` and the `is.na(entry$url)` check for the registry-name branch first, then `.moco_require_torch()` immediately before `.moco_build_encoder()` at line 325 (which is the first statement that actually needs torch). Add a test asserting `foundation_weights_load("edaphos-cerrado-moco-v2")` matches "no published URL yet" that runs WITHOUT torch installed.

findings.title: bhs_fit() returns an all-NaN posterior for a rank-deficient design matrix, and the edge-case test is written to accept it
findings.correction: none — reproduced the propagation: `lm.fit(cbind(1, rep(1,10)), y)$coefficients` -> `c(0.1322, NA)` and `X %*% beta` -> all NA, which poisons rhs_w -> mu_w -> w_cur -> `rate_s` -> `rgamma(1, shape, rate = NaN)` (source of the live "NAs produced" warning at test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:61), then beta itself on the next sweep. No rank check exists; the validation block checks types, coords and the MCMC schedule only, and `.chol_jitter` guards the Cholesky, not the right-hand side. The test at :57-69 asserts only `is.null(fit) || inherits(fit, "edaphos_bhs")`, and its comment's premise ("Gibbs will re-sample") is false. The contrast with :52-53, which does assert `all(fit$sigma2_draws > 0)` for duplicate coordinates, is accurate.
findings.evidence:
R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:238 initialises beta from an unchecked `lm.fit`:
```r
beta <- as.numeric(stats::lm.fit(X, y)$coefficients)
```
Verified the propagation directly: `X <- cbind(1, rep(1,10)); lm.fit(X, y)$coefficients` -> `c(0.1576, NA)`, and `X %*% beta` -> all NA. That NA flows through R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:288 (`rhs_w <- (y - as.numeric(X %*% beta)) / tau2`) into :302 (`rate_s <- prior_ig_b + 0.5 * crossprod(w_cur, Rinv %*% w_cur)`) and then `stats::rgamma(1, shape = shape_s, rate = NaN)` at :303, which is the source of the live warning "NAs produced (x2)". No rank check exists anywhere in `bhs_fit`; the validation block at :92-108 checks types, coords and the MCMC schedule only.
The test that covers this, tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:57-69, is written so that an all-NaN fit passes:
```r
d$x <- rep(1, nrow(d))  # zero variance
fit <- tryCatch(bhs_fit(d, y ~ x, ...), error = function(e) NULL)
# Either it fits (NA beta from lm.fit init is OK -- Gibbs will re-sample)
expect_true(is.null(fit) || inherits(fit, "edaphos_bhs"))
```
It asserts only the class. The comment's premise ("Gibbs will re-sample") is false -- once `rate_s` is NaN every subsequent draw is NaN. Contrast tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:52-53, which for duplicate coordinates DOES assert `all(fit$sigma2_draws > 0)`.
findings.impact: A constant or collinear covariate -- trivially common in real covariate stacks (a masked layer, a single-class categorical, two derived terrain indices) -- yields an `edaphos_bhs` object whose `beta_draws`, `sigma2_draws`, `tau2_draws` and `w_post_mean` are entirely NaN, signalled only by a generic "NAs produced" warning from rgamma that names nothing. `print.edaphos_bhs` (R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:433-454) will happily print `NaN` posterior means. Downstream `predict()` returns all-NaN quantiles. The test suite actively certifies this as acceptable, so the behaviour is locked in.
findings.action: After building `X` at R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:128, check rank and fail with a named message: `if (qr(X)$rank < ncol(X)) stop(sprintf("Design matrix is rank-deficient (rank %d < %d columns); drop constant or collinear covariates: %s", ...), call. = FALSE)`. Then tighten tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:57-69 to `expect_error(bhs_fit(...), "rank-deficient")` instead of accepting either outcome.

findings.title: causal_iv bootstrap silently discards failed 2SLS replicates and rewrites B to the survivor count
findings.evidence:
R/causal_iv.R:338-372. Both the clustered and iid loops swallow refit failures into NA, then the NAs are dropped and `B` is quietly redefined:
```r
fit <- tryCatch(
  causal_iv_fit_2sls(data[ix, , drop = FALSE], exposure, outcome,
                     instruments, covariates),
  error = function(e) NULL)
draws[b] <- if (!is.null(fit)) fit$effect else NA_real_
...
draws <- draws[!is.na(draws)]        # line 360

edaphos_posterior(
  samples    = matrix(draws, ncol = 1L),
  ...
  metadata   = list(..., estimator = "2SLS", B = length(draws), ...)  # line 369
)
```
There is no warning, no floor on the survivor count, and no record of how many replicates were requested. Bootstrap resampling routinely produces singular first stages when instruments are weak or a cluster is small, so failures are expected, not exotic.
findings.impact: If 900 of 1000 replicates fail, the caller receives a perfectly well-formed `edaphos_posterior` built from 100 draws, with `metadata$B = 100` and nothing indicating that 90% of the resampling failed -- the reported confidence interval is then both far too narrow and selected on convergence (surviving replicates are systematically the ones with stronger instruments, biasing the effect estimate). In the total-failure case `draws` is length 0 and `matrix(draws, ncol = 1L)` is a 0-row matrix handed to `edaphos_posterior()`, which will either error obscurely or produce a degenerate posterior. Because `B` is overwritten, the failure rate is unrecoverable after the call returns.
findings.action: In R/causal_iv.R:360-372, record both counts and warn: keep `B_requested`, compute `n_failed <- B - length(draws)`, add `if (n_failed > 0) warning(sprintf("%d of %d bootstrap replicates failed to fit 2SLS (weak or collinear instruments after resampling); the posterior uses %d draws.", n_failed, B, length(draws)))`, `stop()` when `length(draws) < 2`, and store both `B_requested` and `B_effective` in the metadata list at :369 instead of silently reassigning `B`.

findings.title: test-foundation-weights.R:29-36 asserts an error message that is unreachable without torch (live ERROR 2) -- green on CI, red on CRAN
findings.correction: Confirmed by reading both files: `.moco_require_torch()` is the first statement of `foundation_weights_load()`'s body, before any argument handling; the validation it pre-empts ("Loading from a local path requires `n_channels`, `feature_dim` and `proj_dim` ...") sits further down in the local-path branch; torch is not otherwise touched until `.moco_build_encoder()` / `torch::torch_load()`. tests/testthat/test-foundation-weights.R:29-37 has no skip gate (the file's own `skip_if_no_torch()` at :3-8 is only called in the *next* block, :40) and asserts `regexp = "requires.*n_channels"`. `.moco_require_torch()` (R/foundation_moco.R:28-34) tests only `requireNamespace("torch")`, and r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies installs Suggests, so CI is green. Scope narrowing: CRAN flavours generally do have torch installed too, so the exposure is `_R_CHECK_DEPENDS_ONLY_` / no-suggests runs plus any developer machine without torch — which is where the live ERROR came from.
findings.evidence: R/foundation_weights.R:287-294: `foundation_weights_load()` calls `.moco_require_torch()` as its FIRST statement (line 294), before any argument validation. The validation it is supposed to trigger is at lines 310-315: `stop("Loading from a local path requires `n_channels`, `feature_dim` and `proj_dim` to be supplied explicitly.")`. torch is not actually touched until line 325 (`EncCtor <- .moco_build_encoder()`) / line 327 (`torch::torch_load`). tests/testthat/test-foundation-weights.R:29-36 has no skip gate and asserts `expect_error(foundation_weights_load(f), regexp = "requires.*n_channels")`; on a torch-free machine it instead gets "Install the `torch` package to use foundation_moco_*()" from R/foundation_moco.R:28-33. Crucially this is invisible on CI: `.moco_require_torch()` tests only `requireNamespace("torch")`, and CI installs the torch R package, so the guard passes, execution reaches line 312 and the test goes GREEN. It fails only where the torch package is entirely absent -- e.g. CRAN flavours without torch and `_R_CHECK_DEPENDS_ONLY_` runs.
findings.impact: A CRAN-only failure that the project's own CI is structurally incapable of reproducing, on the very release being prepared for submission (RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md step 1). It also means argument validation for a public function is dead code for every user who lacks the optional dependency.
findings.action: Move `.moco_require_torch()` in R/foundation_weights.R from line 294 down to immediately before line 325 (`EncCtor <- .moco_build_encoder()`), so the source/shape validation at 300-315 runs torch-free. Leave tests/testthat/test-foundation-weights.R:29-36 ungated -- it then becomes a real torch-free test. Do NOT 'fix' this by adding skip_if_no_torch() to the test; that would delete the only coverage of the validation branch. Audit the other four guards (.foundation_require_torch R/foundation_simclr.R:18, .piml_require_torch R/piml_neural_ode.R:11, .temporal_require_torch R/temporal_convlstm.R:12, .ft_require_torch R/foundation_finetune.R:40) for the same validate-after-guard ordering.

findings.title: al_fit is ~14.5%-flaky by construction: test-active-quantum-posterior.R:30-35 has no set.seed and passes num.trees=50 for OOB quantile regression (live ERROR 1)
findings.correction: The defect is real; the FLAKINESS THESIS IS REFUTED. Verified: tests/testthat/test-active-quantum-posterior.R:30-35 has no `set.seed` and calls `al_fit(df, target = "y", covariates = "x", num.trees = 50L)` at :34 on a 40-row frame; neighbours at :7 and :39 do seed; ranger 0.18.0 contains `minoob <- min(rowSums(inbag.counts == 0))` with the "Too few trees for out-of-bag quantile regression" stop; every other al_fit call uses >= 100 trees; R/active_fit.R:51-56 validates only `.assert_covariates`/`.assert_coords` and forwards `num.trees` straight to ranger at :1-10. BUT the block is NOT seed-free in practice: the file's FIRST test calls `set.seed(1L)` at line 7, so the RNG state entering line 34 is fully determined by lines 7-28 of the same file. Emulating that stream with ranger 0.18.0 reproduced the failure 3/3 runs. The 14.5% is the unconditional rate over independent seeds — I measured 12.0% (24/200) at n=40/B=50 and 0.0% at B=100 — which is NOT the rate the suite experiences. Consequences: "~1 run in 7 of the full suite fails with an error the maintainer cannot reproduce on demand" and "NEWS.md:71 can honestly claim '0 errors' from one lucky run" are both wrong; the failure is deterministic on ranger 0.18.0 and reproduces every run. Fix is 2 lines (add set.seed, raise to 100L).
findings.evidence: tests/testthat/test-active-quantum-posterior.R:30-35 -- `test_that("as_edaphos_posterior.edaphos_al_model requires newdata", ...)` builds a 40-row frame and calls `al_fit(df, target = "y", covariates = "x", num.trees = 50L)` at line 34. Unlike its neighbours at :7 (`set.seed(1L)`) and :39 (`set.seed(2L)`), this block sets NO seed, so it inherits whatever RNG state the preceding tests left. ranger's guard (verified by `deparse(ranger::ranger)`): `minoob <- min(rowSums(inbag.counts == 0)); if (minoob < 10) stop("Error: Too few trees for out-of-bag quantile regression.")`. With P(obs OOB in a tree) = (1-1/n)^n ~= 0.368, at n=40 / B=50: P(one obs OOB in <10 trees) = 0.00391 -> P(any of the 40 fails) = 0.1450. At B=100 the same probability is 0.0000. Every other al_fit call in the suite already uses num.trees >= 100 (test-active.R:40,55,70,78,148,157; test-physics-gate.R:25,45,72; test-data-regional.R:57,70; the sibling blocks at test-active-quantum-posterior.R:16 and :50 use 100L and 150L). R/active_fit.R:52-56 validates only covariates and coords (`.assert_covariates`, `.assert_coords`); `num.trees` is passed straight through to ranger at R/active_fit.R:3-6.
findings.impact: ~1 run in 7 of the full suite fails with an error the maintainer cannot reproduce on demand -- which is why NEWS.md:71 can honestly claim '0 errors' from one lucky run. It also means users hitting ranger's OOB-quantreg floor get a raw ranger error with no hint that `num.trees` is the knob.
findings.action: Primary fix is the TEST: tests/testthat/test-active-quantum-posterior.R:30-35 -- add `set.seed(...)` at the top of the block and raise `num.trees` to 100L or higher (this block does not exercise forest size at all; it only checks that `as_edaphos_posterior()` demands `newdata`). Secondary, in R/active_fit.R after line 55, add a guard so the failure is actionable rather than a ranger internal: e.g. `if (num.trees < 100L) .stopf("num.trees = %d is too small for ranger's out-of-bag quantile regression (needs every observation OOB in >= 10 trees).", num.trees, hint = "Use num.trees >= 100.")`. Note test-error-messages.R covers input validation for only 4 of 169 exports (bhs_fit, gnn_build_graph, dm_fit, no_deeponet_fit) -- al_fit is not among them.

findings.title: R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:270-272 cites a test that does not perform the verification it claims
findings.evidence: R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:270-272: "# Correctness: the beta and sigma2 / tau2 marginals are bit-for-bit / # identical (up to RNG-draw order) to the v2.3.0 path; see / # tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-fastpath.R." That file contains four blocks and none compares anything to the v2.3.0 dense-inverse path: :6-29 checks `abs(mean(beta_draws[,"x"]) - 3) < 5*sd`, :31-43 checks variance components are positive, :45-66 checks predict() is finite, and :68-88 is a timing guard whose own comment at :69-70 admits "We can't easily run the v2.3.0 dense path in-line here". Total assertions in the file: 7 across 4 blocks.
findings.impact: A source-level correctness claim about a performance rewrite points at evidence that does not exist. A future reader (or reviewer at rOpenSci / CRAN) auditing the v3.2.0 fast path will find nothing behind the citation, and there is no way to detect if the triangular-solve rewrite silently changed the posterior.
findings.action: Either implement the claimed check -- keep a `.bhs_gibbs_dense()` reference implementation as an internal (not exported) function and assert `expect_equal(draws_fast, draws_dense, tolerance = 1e-10)` under a fixed seed in test-pilar7-bhs-fastpath.R -- or delete the unsupported sentence at R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:270-272 and replace it with what the test actually contracts.

findings.title: The RcppArmadillo BHS Gibbs backend has no real numerical-agreement test: one scalar mean at 0.2 tolerance, w_post_mean never compared, no edge cases
findings.correction: Core claims verified: the only R-vs-C++ comparison is test-pilar7-bhs-rcpp.R:38-54, `expect_lt(abs(m_r - m_cpp), 0.2)` on `mean(beta_draws[,"x"])`; `grep -rn w_post_mean tests/` returns zero hits (the predict() test at :56-70 asserts shape only, so an all-NaN `w_post_mean` passes); `grep -n backend tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R` is empty and `bhs_fit`'s `backend = c("gibbs", "rcpp", "spBayes")` makes "gibbs" the default, so the C++ sweep has zero edge-case coverage; the init divergence is real (`arma::solve(X, y)` vs `stats::lm.fit(X, y)$coefficients`); and the draw order IS identical (n rnorm in sample_mvn_from_prec for w, p rnorm for beta, R::rgamma, R::rgamma), so the test comment "the C++ RNG ordering differs" is factually wrong. Two corrections: (a) `sigma2_draws`/`tau2_draws` positivity IS asserted, at :34-35 (just not cross-backend); (b) the proposed "seed-equivalence" test is not actually attainable — R's chol/backsolve and Armadillo's chol/trimatu differ in floating-point rounding, and a Gibbs chain amplifies that over hundreds of iterations, so bit-equivalence would be a flaky test even with matching RNG order. The gap is real; the suggested remedy is not.
findings.evidence: tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-rcpp.R:37-56 is the entire R-vs-C++ agreement check: it compares `mean(fit_r$beta_draws[,"x"])` to `mean(fit_cpp$beta_draws[,"x"])` with `expect_lt(abs(m_r - m_cpp), 0.2)`. Not compared anywhere: the intercept column, the posterior SDs, `sigma2_draws`, `tau2_draws`, and `w_post_mean` -- even though `w_post_mean` is the quantity `predict.edaphos_bhs` kriges with (R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:391 `t(R_cross) %*% R_tr_inv %*% object$w_post_mean`) and `fitted` adds (:419); `grep -rn w_post_mean tests/` returns zero hits. A far stronger test is available and is what the C++ header itself promises: src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:24-25 states "RNG is drawn from R's `R::rnorm` / `R::rgamma` so seed-equivalence with R is preserved", and the draw ORDER is in fact identical between R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:286-310 (n normals for w, p normals for beta, rgamma sigma2, rgamma tau2) and src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:106-126 -- yet tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-rcpp.R:38-40 asserts the opposite in a comment ("We don't expect bit-equivalence -- the C++ RNG ordering differs"). Divergence risk is concrete: src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:91 initialises with `arma::solve(X, y)` while R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:238 uses `stats::lm.fit(X, y)$coefficients` -- different rank-deficiency semantics (see finding on the constant covariate). And `grep -n backend tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R` returns nothing: all 10 edge blocks (NA rows, duplicate coords, constant covariate, too-few-rows, extreme phi_range) run the pure-R path only, so the C++ sweep has zero edge-case coverage. For contrast, tests/testthat/test-quantum-kernel-rcpp.R:6-20 is a genuine check: element-wise `expect_equal(K_r, K_cpp, tolerance = 1e-10)` swept over n_qubits 2..5 x reps 1..2, plus an asymmetric (X,Y) case at :22-32 and symmetry/unit-diagonal/PSD invariants at :34-43.
findings.impact: A wrong sign, a swapped shape/rate, or a mis-ordered triangular solve in the C++ sweep would move the posterior mean of one coefficient by well under 0.2 and pass. The kriging path (w_post_mean) could be entirely wrong in the rcpp backend and nothing would notice. Since backend='rcpp' is the advertised v3.5.0 performance path, users are the first line of defence.
findings.action: Replace the scalar check in tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-rcpp.R:37-56 with a draw-by-draw comparison: run both backends with the same `seed` and assert `expect_equal(fit_r$beta_draws, fit_cpp$beta_draws, tolerance = 1e-8)` plus the same for sigma2_draws, tau2_draws and w_post_mean. If that fails, the C++ header comment at src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:24-25 is wrong and should be corrected -- either way the ambiguity must be resolved. Add `backend = "rcpp"` variants of the 10 blocks in test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R (parameterise the file over both backends), and reconcile `arma::solve` at src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:91 with `lm.fit` at R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:238.

findings.title: NEWS.md v3.10.0 test and check claims are not reproducible in any environment the project automates
findings.correction: NEWS.md:71-72 ("R CMD check: 0 errors / 0 notes." / "1 345 tests pass (+17 vs v3.9.0).") and the comparable unqualified claims at NEWS.md:194, :241, :298 are all verified verbatim, and the live 1022/109/2/2 result stands. But two of the finding's own numbers are wrong and contradict its sibling finding: it states "the suite contains 1209 `expect_` calls" — I measured 1089 (the same number finding 2 reports) — and its breakdown ("223 behind torch, 22+21+12 behind the Python qiskit stack, 64 dagitty, 20 bnlearn, 10 dbarts") is unsourced and does not reconcile with the 109-skip breakdown. Its claim that the al_fit error "fires ~14.5% of runs" is also refuted (see finding 12: deterministic, because the file seeds at line 7). Substantively this is finding 2 restated with a different arithmetic error; the qualifier-free "0 errors" claims are the real content.
findings.evidence: NEWS.md:71-72 states "R CMD check: 0 errors / 0 notes." and "1 345 tests pass (+17 vs v3.9.0)." The live devtools::test() on the maintainer's own machine (R 4.6.1 aarch64-darwin) gives 1022 PASS / 109 SKIP / 2 FAIL / 2 WARN. Static analysis shows the suite contains 1209 `expect_` calls, of which 223 (18.4%) are behind torch, 22+21+12 behind the Python qiskit/nature/Aer stack, 64 behind dagitty, 20 behind bnlearn, 10 behind dbarts -- so 1345 runtime expectations is only attainable on a machine with libtorch AND a qiskit+PySCF virtualenv AND dagitty AND bnlearn AND dbarts, i.e. never on CI (TORCH_INSTALL=0, no Python stack) and never on CRAN. Both live errors are deterministic-or-frequent, not environmental noise: the foundation-weights one fires on every torch-package-free machine (finding #3) and the al_fit one fires ~14.5% of runs (finding #5). Comparable unqualified '0 errors' claims appear at NEWS.md:194, :241, :298.
findings.impact: The release notes assert a green state that no reproducible pipeline can confirm, and the number is not comparable release-to-release because it depends on which optional packages happened to be installed. Anyone verifying the claims (rOpenSci reviewer, CRAN maintainer, a collaborator) will get a different number and two errors.
findings.action: Restate NEWS.md:71-72 as the CI-reproducible figure with the environment named, e.g. "1 022 expectations pass, 109 skipped (74 torch, 22 dagitty, 9 bnlearn, 3 dbarts, 1 other) on R 4.6.1 without libtorch", and add the full-stack figure separately if desired. Fix the two errors before re-asserting '0 errors'. Consider having the test-coverage workflow emit the PASS/SKIP counts as a job summary so future NEWS entries quote a machine-generated number.

findings.title: 12 exported functions are never called by any test, including the entire tile-download layer and a function that recursively deletes a directory
findings.correction: none — I recomputed independently and got byte-identical results: NAMESPACE has 169 `export()` + 73 `S3method()`; 68 `test-*.R` files; 11 exports never mentioned and exactly the 12 named exports never called (causal_ontology_agrovoc, causal_ontology_envo, edaphos_zenodo_release, foundation_build_cerrado_stack, foundation_tile_source_{era5,modis,soilgrids,srtm,worldclim}, llm_annotation_launch, piml_neural_ode_predict, temporal_convlstm_predict). R/edaphos_zenodo_release.R:49 is `if (dir.exists(output_dir)) unlink(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)` in a 223-line file with one export and no test. SEVERITY DEFLATED: 12/169 = 7.1% untested exports is ordinary-to-good for an R package of this size, and most of the 12 are structurally hard to test offline (tile sources download rasters via terra/geodata, causal_ontology_agrovoc issues a live SPARQL query, llm_annotation_launch starts a Shiny app, the two *_predict functions need libtorch). The `unlink` is also documented behaviour — R/edaphos_zenodo_release.R:36 says `@return Invisibly, the path of the created directory` for a build-a-fresh-output-dir helper — not an undisclosed hazard.
findings.evidence: NAMESPACE has 169 `export()` lines plus 73 `S3method()` lines. Matching each export against the concatenation of all tests/testthat/*.R: 11 are never mentioned at all and 12 are never CALLED (`name(`). The 12: `foundation_tile_source_soilgrids` (R/foundation_tiles.R:55), `foundation_tile_source_worldclim` (:111), `foundation_tile_source_srtm` (:148), `foundation_tile_source_modis` (:183), `foundation_tile_source_era5` (:202), `foundation_build_cerrado_stack` (R/foundation_embed_coords.R:224), `foundation_weights`-adjacent `edaphos_zenodo_release` (R/edaphos_zenodo_release.R:39), `causal_ontology_agrovoc` (R/causal_ontology.R:104), `causal_ontology_envo` (R/causal_ontology.R:153), `llm_annotation_launch` (R/llm_annotation.R:665), `piml_neural_ode_predict` (R/piml_neural_ode.R:198), `temporal_convlstm_predict` (R/temporal_convlstm.R:283). Notable specifics: tests/testthat/test-foundation-tiles.R exercises only `foundation_tile_dataset` and `foundation_tile_align` against a hand-built terra raster (`make_toy_stack`, lines 8-24), so the whole AOI/variable/download layer that the roadmap calls the 'planetary-scale tile pipeline' is untested; `causal_ontology_agrovoc()` (the live SPARQL query builder) is never called -- only the downstream `causal_ontology_agrovoc_align()` is, with a mocked response (test-causal-scale.R:163-210); `edaphos_zenodo_release()` begins with `if (dir.exists(output_dir)) unlink(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)` (R/edaphos_zenodo_release.R:49) and is the only export in a 223-LOC file that no test file touches at all.
findings.impact: 7.1% of the public API has never been executed by a test. The destructive `unlink(..., recursive = TRUE)` in edaphos_zenodo_release is the sharpest: an untested, exported function that irreversibly deletes a user-supplied path, and it is on the release checklist path (Zenodo deposit). The tile sources are the documented on-ramp to Pillar 4 and would fail silently on any upstream URL/API change.
findings.action: Add a tests/testthat/test-zenodo-release.R that runs `edaphos_zenodo_release(tempfile(), include_tarball = FALSE, zip = FALSE)` and asserts the manifest/metadata.json/checksums, plus an explicit test that it refuses a non-empty non-edaphos directory (i.e. gate the `unlink` behind a confirmation or an `overwrite = FALSE` default). Add offline tests for `foundation_tile_source_soilgrids/worldclim/srtm` that assert the request objects they build (httr2 is already an Import and 14 blocks already use httr2 mocking), and simple `expect_error(..., "EarthData|Copernicus")` tests for the two documented stubs at R/foundation_tiles.R:183 and :202. Add a direct call test for `causal_ontology_agrovoc()` query construction.

findings.title: The v3.8.0 friendly-error work covers 4 of 169 exports; .assert_type/.stopf adopted in 6 of 70 R/ files
findings.evidence: tests/testthat/test-error-messages.R (16 blocks, all ungated -- the largest unconditional file) states its contract at :1-7 and tests exactly four public entry points: bhs_fit (:43-81), gnn_build_graph (:83-110), dm_fit (:112-144), no_deeponet_fit (:146-163), plus 4 unit tests of the helpers themselves (:13-36). `grep -c '.assert_type(|.stopf(' R/*.R` returns non-zero for only 6 of 70 files: R/core_utils.R (2, the definitions), R/pilar10_graph_nn.R (4), R/pilar9_diffusion_models.R (3), R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R (4), R/llm_kg_pipeline.R (3), R/pilar8_neural_operators.R (5). Everything else still uses bare `stop()` or `stopifnot()` -- e.g. R/foundation_weights.R:310-315 uses `stop()` and :318 uses `stopifnot(is.numeric(n_channels), ...)`, which produces a raw deparsed-expression message. Pillars 1-6 (causal_*, piml_*, temporal_*, foundation_*, al_*, quantum_*) have no `.stopf`/`.assert_type` adoption and no entries in test-error-messages.R at all -- which is directly why al_fit has no num.trees guard (finding #5).
findings.impact: The advertised v3.8.0 improvement is real for pillars 7-10 and absent for pillars 1-6, so error quality is inconsistent across the API in a way users will experience as arbitrary. Untested validation paths are also where finding #3's dead-code branch hid.
findings.action: Extend .stopf/.assert_type to the public entry points of pillars 1-6, starting with the ones the suite already stresses: al_fit (R/active_fit.R:52), al_loop (R/active_loop.R:73), quantum_krr_fit, piml_profile_fit, temporal_convlstm_fit, causal_estimate_effect, foundation_weights_load (replace the bare stop at R/foundation_weights.R:312 and the stopifnot at :318). Grow tests/testthat/test-error-messages.R in lockstep -- it is the highest-value file in the suite because it is the only large one that is 100% ungated and therefore runs everywhere including CRAN.

findings.title: Three of four wall-clock assertions run on CRAN: only 1 skip_on_cran() exists in the whole 460-block suite
findings.evidence: Timing assertions found by grep across tests/testthat: (1) tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-rcpp.R:85-99 -- `system.time(bhs_fit(..., backend="gibbs", nmcmc=300L))` vs the rcpp equivalent, `expect_lt(as.numeric(t_c), as.numeric(t_r))`, NO skip_on_cran; (2) tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-fastpath.R:81-87 -- `expect_lt(as.numeric(t1), 10)` for 500 Gibbs iterations at n=150, NO skip_on_cran; (3) tests/testthat/test-pilar10-gat-sparse.R:113-123 -- `expect_lt(as.numeric(t_sparse), as.numeric(t_ref))`, NO skip_on_cran; (4) tests/testthat/test-quantum-kernel-rcpp.R:46 -- the ONLY `skip_on_cran()` in the suite, with the correct rationale in-line: "timing tests are noisy on CRAN builders". `grep -c skip_on_cran tests/testthat/*.R` totals 1 across 69 files.
findings.impact: CRAN builders are shared, single-core on some flavours, and run under valgrind/rchk on others; a 10-second absolute ceiling and two strict A<B comparisons will flip non-deterministically. Combined with the flaky al_fit test, submission (RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md step 1) has several independent ways to bounce for reasons unrelated to the science.
findings.action: Add `skip_on_cran()` as the first line of the three blocks: tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-rcpp.R:84, tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-fastpath.R:80, tests/testthat/test-pilar10-gat-sparse.R:112 -- matching the pattern already used correctly at test-quantum-kernel-rcpp.R:46. Consider also gating them on `Sys.getenv("NOT_CRAN")` in the coverage job so they still run somewhere.

findings.title: test-coverage has no threshold gate, no codecov.yml, and diverges from R-CMD-check on TORCH_INSTALL; reported coverage has an invisible ~75% ceiling
findings.correction: All mechanical claims verified: no codecov.yml / .codecov.yml / .github/codecov.yml anywhere; test-coverage.yaml:35-52 runs covr and uploads via codecov-action@v4 with `fail_ci_if_error` (an upload-error flag, not a coverage gate); :18-19 sets only GITHUB_PAT with no TORCH_INSTALL, unlike R-CMD-check.yaml:35; README.md:12 is a hardcoded `tests-1345%20pass-brightgreen` badge and :13 a live Codecov badge; README.md:1672 says "109+ unit and integration tests" against 460 test_that blocks / 1022 passing expectations. Downgraded: an unenforced coverage number is a missing nice-to-have rather than a defect, and the badge staleness overlaps the README-staleness finding.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/test-coverage.yaml:35-52 runs `covr::package_coverage()` and uploads `cobertura.xml` via `codecov/codecov-action@v4` with `token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}` (line 52) and `fail_ci_if_error: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' && true || false }}` (line 48) -- that flag only fails on *upload* errors, not on a coverage drop. No `codecov.yml`, `.codecov.yml`, or `.github/codecov.yml` exists anywhere in the repo, so there is no project/patch target, no informational-vs-blocking configuration, and no `ignore:` list. Crucially, test-coverage.yaml:18-19 sets only `GITHUB_PAT` -- it does **not** set `TORCH_INSTALL: 0` the way R-CMD-check.yaml:35 does, so the two workflows do not agree on the torch environment even though covr re-runs the same 460 test blocks. Given finding 1, the 4,990 torch LOC (25.3% of R/) are unexecutable, capping coverage near 75% with no annotation. README.md:13 carries a live Codecov badge and README.md:12 a hardcoded `tests-1345%20pass-brightgreen` badge; README.md:1672 additionally says "109+ unit and integration tests" (the actual figure is 460 `test_that` blocks / 1022 passing expectations -- 109 is coincidentally the *skip* count).
findings.impact: Coverage is reported but never enforced: a PR that deletes tests shows a lower number and still merges. Because TORCH_INSTALL is pinned in one workflow and unpinned in another, the coverage figure is not reproducible against the check figure, and a future torch-version change could shift it without any code change. The ~25% structurally-uncoverable share is invisible to anyone reading the badge, so the badge overstates verification of exactly the pillars that are least verified.
findings.action: Add a `codecov.yml` with `coverage.status.project: {target: auto, threshold: 1%}` and `patch: {target: 80%}`, and an `ignore:` block listing the 15 torch-backed files with a comment pointing at the missing libtorch leg -- so the reported number describes what CI can actually reach. Set `TORCH_INSTALL: 0` in test-coverage.yaml:18-19 to match R-CMD-check.yaml:35 (or install libtorch in both). Replace the hardcoded `tests-1345 pass` badge at README.md:12 and the "109+ tests" line at README.md:1672 with the Codecov badge alone, or regenerate them from a real run.

findings.title: pkgdown site loads mermaid from a third-party CDN with no integrity attribute, on a surface SECURITY.md declares in scope
findings.evidence: _pkgdown.yml:9-30 injects into every page's `<head>`: `<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11/dist/mermaid.min.js"></script>` (line 11) with no `integrity` or `crossorigin` attribute, followed by an inline script that rewrites `pre > code.language-mermaid` nodes and calls `mermaid.run()`. The `@11` specifier floats across all minor and patch releases. SECURITY.md:36-37 explicitly places "The pkgdown site (<https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/edaphos/>)" in scope for vulnerability reports, and SECURITY.md:40-45 places dependency vulnerabilities out of scope -- so this script is in scope by the project's own policy while being unpinned and unverified.
findings.impact: Every visitor to the documentation site executes whatever jsdelivr serves for `mermaid@11` at that moment, with no subresource-integrity check. This is a modest risk for a docs site with no authentication, but the project has written a security policy that claims responsibility for exactly this surface, so the gap is a stated-commitment failure rather than merely a default.
findings.action: Pin the exact version and add an SRI hash (`mermaid@11.4.1` + `integrity="sha384-..." crossorigin="anonymous"`), or vendor the minified file into `pkgdown/extra.js` and drop the remote fetch entirely -- pkgdown copies `pkgdown/` assets into the built site, and the inline rewriting script at _pkgdown.yml:12-29 works unchanged.

findings.title: Documented quality gates (spell check, URL check, lint) exist in prose and templates but in no workflow; `_R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_` is never relaxed across 40 Suggests
findings.correction: Inventory verified: .github/workflows/ holds exactly R-CMD-check.yaml, pkgdown.yaml, test-coverage.yaml; .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md:25 requires spell_check; CONTRIBUTING.md:46-47 requires `devtools::spell_check()` and `urlchecker::url_check()`; CONTRIBUTING.md:31 specifies style with no .lintr; inst/WORDLIST is 17,811 bytes; `grep -rn '_R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_'` is empty repo-wide; R-CMD-check.yaml:29-35 sets only GITHUB_PAT/R_KEEP_PKG_SOURCE/TORCH_INSTALL and :48-51 passes no `dependencies:` input against 40 Suggests at DESCRIPTION:36-76; renv.lock, renv/, codemeta.json and .github/dependabot.yml are all absent. TWO CORRECTIONS. (1) "No URL check exists anywhere for the 84,288-byte README.md and 182 man topics" is wrong: `r-lib/actions/check-r-package@v2` defaults to `args: c("--no-manual", "--as-cran")`, and `--as-cran` runs the `checking URLs` step over DESCRIPTION, Rd and README.md on every push — so URLs are in fact checked in CI, just not by urlchecker. (2) The FORCE_SUGGESTS risk is real but hypothetical here; no red leg from a Suggests build failure is in evidence. The concrete, actionable residue is the missing codemeta.json against the rOpenSci target at RELEASE.md:108-127.
findings.evidence: `ls .github/workflows/` -> exactly R-CMD-check.yaml, pkgdown.yaml, test-coverage.yaml. Yet .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md:25 requires "No new warnings in `devtools::spell_check()` (or added to `inst/WORDLIST`)" and CONTRIBUTING.md:46-47 requires `devtools::spell_check()` and `urlchecker::url_check()`; `inst/WORDLIST` exists at 17,811 bytes, proving spell_check is run manually. CONTRIBUTING.md:31 specifies "2-space indent, no tabs, ~80 char lines" with no lintr/styler workflow or `.lintr` file to enforce it. No URL check exists anywhere for the 84,288-byte README.md and 182 man topics. `grep -rn '_R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_'` returns nothing repo-wide; R-CMD-check.yaml:29-35 sets only `GITHUB_PAT`, `R_KEEP_PKG_SOURCE` and `TORCH_INSTALL`, and no `dependencies:` input is given to setup-r-dependencies (R-CMD-check.yaml:48-51), so all 40 Suggests in DESCRIPTION:36-76 are resolved by the action default -- including dagitty (V8), spBayes, bnlearn, dbarts, geobr, ecmwfr, gstat, aqp, ontologyIndex -- on windows-latest and macos-latest as well as Linux. Also absent: renv.lock, renv/, codemeta.json, .github/dependabot.yml, any CITATION.cff validation, any revdep job.
findings.impact: Every gate the project documents for contributors is unenforced, so drift is guaranteed -- and the maintainer's own workflow depends on remembering four manual commands (CONTRIBUTING.md:42-48). More acutely, with 40 unrestricted Suggests and no `_R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_=false`, a single upstream build failure (dagitty needs V8; spBayes needs Fortran/BLAS) makes R CMD check error with "Packages required but not available" on a leg, producing a red build unrelated to the package -- the classic reason maintainers stop trusting CI. Absent codemeta.json is a concrete gap against the rOpenSci submission RELEASE.md:108-127 targets.
findings.action: Add three cheap workflows from the r-lib examples: `lint.yaml` (lintr with a `.lintr` encoding the CONTRIBUTING.md:31 rules), `spell-check` (`spelling::spell_check_package()` against inst/WORDLIST), and a scheduled `urlchecker` job. Set `_R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_: false` in R-CMD-check.yaml:29-35 so a Suggests install failure degrades to skips instead of a red build. Add `.github/dependabot.yml` with the `github-actions` ecosystem (weekly) since actions/checkout@v4, codecov-action@v4 and JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4.5.0 are all floating tags. Generate `codemeta.json` via `codemetar::write_codemeta()` and add a `cffconvert`/`cff-validator` step before the rOpenSci submission. Revdep tooling is not yet needed (cran-comments.md:100 correctly notes zero reverse dependencies).

findings.title: `needs: website` and `needs: coverage` are no-ops: DESCRIPTION declares no Config/Needs/* fields
findings.evidence: pkgdown.yaml:53 passes `needs: website` and test-coverage.yaml:33 passes `needs: coverage` to `r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2`; that input resolves `Config/Needs/<field>` entries in DESCRIPTION. `grep -n 'Config' DESCRIPTION` returns exactly one line -- DESCRIPTION:77 `Config/testthat/edition: 3`. There is no `Config/Needs/website` and no `Config/Needs/coverage`, so both inputs contribute nothing and the website dependencies are instead hard-coded in YAML at pkgdown.yaml:41-52 (pkgdown, DiagrammeR, ggdag, ggridges, ggnewscale, patchwork, RColorBrewer, scales, tidyr, dplyr, local::.) and covr/xml2 at test-coverage.yaml:29-32.
findings.impact: The DESCRIPTION does not record what the site needs, so a maintainer running `pkgdown::build_site()` locally gets missing-package errors with no manifest to consult, and the YAML list can silently diverge from what the vignettes actually import. It also hides a real gap: `igraph` is needed by four gated chunks in vignettes/pilar1-causal.Rmd (:269, :466, :491, :513, :530) and is not in the pkgdown extra-packages list -- it is only pulled in because the action's default Suggests resolution happens to include it, which is incidental rather than declared.
findings.action: Add `Config/Needs/website: pkgdown, DiagrammeR, ggdag, ggridges, ggnewscale, patchwork, RColorBrewer, scales, tidyr, dplyr, igraph` and `Config/Needs/coverage: covr, xml2` to DESCRIPTION, then reduce pkgdown.yaml:41-52 to `extra-packages: local::.` and test-coverage.yaml:29-32 to `local::.` so the manifest lives in one place and works locally too.

findings.title: .Rbuildignore hygiene: version-pinned checklist pattern, duplicated entry, dead README.Rmd rule
findings.evidence: .Rbuildignore:24 `^RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3\.10\.0\.md$` is hard-pinned to a single version, so the next release's checklist file will not be excluded and will ship in the tarball as a top-level non-standard file. Line 2 `^\.claude$` and line 18 `^\.claude$` are exact duplicates. Line 6 `^README\.Rmd$` matches nothing -- the root contains only README.md (84,288 bytes), no README.Rmd, so the README is hand-maintained rather than knitted despite the rule implying otherwise. Line 21 `^articles$` excludes the four root `articles/*.Rmd` from the tarball; combined with finding 2 those four documents are reachable from no distribution channel at all -- not the tarball, not the (never-built) pkgdown site.
findings.impact: Each item is individually trivial, but together they mean the ignore file has not been reviewed in several releases: the version-pinned rule is a latent `R CMD check --as-cran` NOTE ("Non-standard file/directory found at top level") on the very next release, and the dead README.Rmd rule misleads a contributor into editing a file that does not exist instead of the 84 KB README.md.
findings.action: Generalise line 24 to `^RELEASE-CHECKLIST.*\.md$` (or `^RELEASE.*\.md$`, which also covers RELEASE.md at line 19), delete the duplicate `^\.claude$` at line 18, and remove the dead `^README\.Rmd$` at line 6 -- or introduce a real README.Rmd so the badges and the 1,345/109 test figures noted in finding 7 can be generated rather than hand-typed. Resolve the `^articles$` question together with finding 2.

findings.title: No dependency pinning outside the Dockerfile; floating action tags in a job granted `contents: write`
findings.evidence: No renv.lock, no renv/ directory, no `.github/dependabot.yml` (all verified absent). All GitHub Actions use floating tags rather than commit SHAs: actions/checkout@v4 (R-CMD-check.yaml:38, pkgdown.yaml:31, test-coverage.yaml:21), r-lib/actions/*@v2 (six call sites), codecov/codecov-action@v4 (test-coverage.yaml:46), and the third-party JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4.5.0 (pkgdown.yaml:61). pkgdown.yaml:20-21 grants that job `permissions: contents: write`, whereas R-CMD-check.yaml:11 correctly uses `permissions: read-all` and test-coverage.yaml:12-13 `contents: read`. DESCRIPTION:83 declares `ranger` with no version floor even though the live test failure in finding 3 is ranger-version-sensitive (0.18.0 locally); only `deSolve (>= 1.40)` and `Rcpp (>= 1.0.0)` carry floors among the seven Imports (DESCRIPTION:78-85). The only version pinning anywhere in the project is the RSPM snapshot at Dockerfile:43.
findings.impact: The R environment CI resolves is whatever RSPM serves that day, so a check that was green last month can go red with no repo change and no record of which upstream moved -- a maintainer with no CI history (finding 8) cannot bisect that. The `contents: write` job runs a third-party action at a mutable tag, so a compromised or force-moved `v4.5.0` tag can push arbitrary content to the repo's gh-pages branch.
findings.action: Add `.github/dependabot.yml` with the `github-actions` ecosystem so tags are bumped deliberately, and SHA-pin at minimum the third-party JamesIves action at pkgdown.yaml:61. Add a version floor to `ranger` in DESCRIPTION:83 once finding 3 is diagnosed. A full renv.lock is overkill for a package (it would conflict with CRAN's resolution model), but recording the RSPM snapshot date used for the release check -- in cran-comments.md's test-environments section -- gives the same audit value cheaply.

findings.title: %||% is copy-pasted into 7 files; the definition that actually wins is decided by alphabetical collation, not by design
findings.correction: none on the facts — `grep -rn '`%||%` <- function' R/` returns exactly the seven cited sites (core_utils.R:4, bridges_active_learning_v3.R:322, bridges_structure_v3.R:266, llm_annotation.R:97, piml_quantum_bridge.R:228, quantum_foundation.R:221, uncertainty.R:522), `grep -n 'Collate' DESCRIPTION` returns nothing, uncertainty.R does sort last of the seven, and the dotted-helper dedup check confirms `%||%` is the sole duplicated name. SEVERITY IS INFLATED TO THE POINT OF IRRELEVANCE: all seven definitions are byte-identical (`function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a`), so which one "wins" has exactly zero observable consequence — there is no action-at-a-distance, only redundant source. R has also shipped `%||%` in base since 4.4.0, making all seven redundant rather than dangerous. Cosmetic cleanup, no behavioural risk.
findings.evidence:
Seven identical definitions of `` `%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a ``:
R/core_utils.R:4 (the canonical home — the file's own header at :1-2 reads "Internal utilities shared across pillars. Not exported.")
R/bridges_active_learning_v3.R:322 (last line of the file)
R/bridges_structure_v3.R:266 (last line)
R/llm_annotation.R:97
R/piml_quantum_bridge.R:228 (last line)
R/quantum_foundation.R:221 (last line)
R/uncertainty.R:522
DESCRIPTION has no `Collate:` field (`grep -n 'Collate' DESCRIPTION` → no match), so R/ is sourced in locale collation order and the LAST definition wins in the built namespace. Of the seven files, `uncertainty.R` sorts last, so R/uncertainty.R:522 — not the documented canonical R/core_utils.R:4 — is the operative definition.
By contrast there are zero other duplicated dotted-helper names across R/ (`grep -h '^\.[a-zA-Z0-9_.]* <- function' R/*.R | sed 's/ <- function.*//' | sort | uniq -d` → empty), so `%||%` is the sole offender, which makes it easy to fix.
findings.impact: Action-at-a-distance: the one function every pillar depends on for null-coalescing has seven sources of truth and its winner is chosen by filename sort order. R does not warn about the redefinitions, so nothing in R CMD check will ever surface this.
findings.action: Delete the six redundant definitions (R/bridges_active_learning_v3.R:322, R/bridges_structure_v3.R:266, R/llm_annotation.R:97, R/piml_quantum_bridge.R:228, R/quantum_foundation.R:221, R/uncertainty.R:522), keeping only R/core_utils.R:4. Note that R >= 4.4 provides `%||%` in base, so the cleanest end state is to drop the definition entirely and bump `Depends: R (>= 4.4)`. Either way, add a one-line unit test asserting `NULL %||% 1 == 1` so a future accidental redefinition is caught.

findings.title: quantum_kernel_rcpp allocates nX * 2^n complex states but its only guard is a warning keyed on n alone
findings.correction: Verified: src/quantum_kernel_rcpp.cpp:128-130 is `Rcpp::warning` (not stop) keyed on `n > 20` with no reference to nX; :131 `const size_t dim = (size_t) 1 << n`; :135 allocates `states_X(nX, std::vector<cplx>(dim))`; :146 allocates a second `states_Y_storage` of nY x dim for the two-argument form. R/quantum_kernel.R:180-183 warns only when `n > 12L && backend == "r"`, and the rcpp branch at :186-191 forwards with no size check. Two notes: the shift itself is safe (`(size_t)1` binds before `<<`, so no UB), and reaching a dangerous allocation requires ~18+ covariates as qubits, well outside the n_pcs = 6-8 the package's own benchmarks use — so the practical exposure is narrow.
findings.evidence:
