src/quantum_kernel_rcpp.cpp:135 `std::vector<std::vector<cplx>> states_X(nX, std::vector<cplx>(dim));` with `dim = (size_t) 1 << n` at :131 — memory is nX * 2^n * 16 bytes, and for the two-argument form :146 allocates a second `states_Y_storage` of nY * 2^n * 16.
The only guard is :128-130 `if (n > 20) { Rcpp::warning("quantum_kernel_rcpp with n_qubits > 20 may exhaust RAM."); }` — a WARNING, not a stop, and keyed on `n` with no reference to `nX`.
The R wrapper does not compensate: R/quantum_kernel.R:180-183 warns only about the pure-R path (`if (n > 12L && backend == "r")`) and the rcpp branch at :186-191 forwards straight through with no size check. `quantum_krr_fit` (:262) and `predict.edaphos_quantum_krr` (:293) both call it with user-sized matrices.
findings.impact: The advertised 10-50x-faster default backend for Pillar 6 can take down an R session on a covariate count the guard considers safe, and cries wolf on one that is safe. Because the allocation happens up front rather than streaming, there is no partial-progress or graceful-degradation path, and a std::bad_alloc surfaces as an opaque Rcpp error rather than an actionable message.
findings.action: Replace src/quantum_kernel_rcpp.cpp:128-130 with a size-aware check computed from the actual request: `const double gb = (double)(nX + (same ? 0 : nY)) * (double) dim * 16.0 / 1073741824.0; if (gb > 2.0) Rcpp::stop("quantum_kernel needs %.1f GB for %d samples x 2^%d amplitudes; reduce n_qubits (ncol(X)) or batch the samples.", gb, nX, n);` with a warning tier at ~0.5 GB. Better still, stop materialising all states: compute states in blocks and accumulate the Gram matrix block-wise, capping memory at O(block * 2^n). Mirror the check in R/quantum_kernel.R:186 so the error arrives before entering C++.

findings.title: Dead code, an undocumented non-dotted internal, and three comment/code contradictions in the pillar 7-10 modules
findings.evidence:
**Dead code.** R/pilar8_neural_operators.R:226-231 assigns `param_refs <- list("W_in" = quote(W_in), "W_out" = quote(W_out), "b_out" = quote(b_out))` — a vestige of an intended generic finite-difference loop. `grep -rn 'param_refs' R/*.R` returns exactly one hit, the assignment itself. Never read.
**Non-dotted internal with no @noRd.** R/bridges_structure_v3.R:218-221 `unclass_to_qf <- function(x) { class(x) <- setdiff(class(x), "edaphos_qf_krr_gat"); x }` — a top-level helper with no leading dot, no roxygen block, and no `@noRd`. It is correctly absent from NAMESPACE and from man/, but it is the only such helper in R/ and it sits between two roxygenised `#' @export` blocks (:208 and :224), so a stray `#' @export` during a future edit would publish it. Package-wide there are 0 `@noRd` tags and only 2 `@keywords internal`, so no convention protects it.
**Comment contradicts code.** R/pilar8_neural_operators.R:202-204: the comment reads `# Nonlinearity (GELU approximation)` and the code immediately below is `v <- pmax(v_new + v_lin, 0) + 0.1 * pmin(v_new + v_lin, 0)  # leaky ReLU (cheap & stable)` — two contradictory labels on adjacent lines. A real GELU IS implemented 250 lines later at :456 for the DeepONet path, so the two operators in the same file use different activations under the same "GELU" comment.
**Equivalence claims contradicted by the tests that supposedly prove them.** R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:270-272 claims "The beta and sigma2 / tau2 marginals are bit-for-bit identical (up to RNG-draw order) to the v2.3.0 path; see tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-fastpath.R" and src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:14-15 claims "statistically equivalent up to RNG-draw order" — while tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-rcpp.R:38-40 states "We don't expect bit-equivalence -- the C++ RNG ordering differs" and asserts only `abs(m_r - m_cpp) < 0.2`. src/quantum_kernel_rcpp.cpp:22-24 makes the same style of claim ("numerical output is identical to the R implementation up to machine precision").
findings.impact: None of these is a live defect, but together they are the residue of four rounds of copy-paste-and-tune (v2.7.0 torch, v3.2.0 fast path, v3.5.0 rcpp, v3.8.0 errors) landing in the same four files without a cleanup pass. The equivalence comments are the most costly because they actively discourage the tests that would catch backend divergence.
findings.action: Delete R/pilar8_neural_operators.R:226-231. Rename `unclass_to_qf` to `.unclass_to_qf` (3 call sites, all in R/bridges_structure_v3.R:211/:215/:224) and add `@noRd` as the house convention. Fix the R/pilar8_neural_operators.R:202 comment to say "leaky ReLU" and note in the roxygen that the pure-R FNO uses leaky ReLU while the DeepONet path uses GELU. Downgrade the three equivalence claims to what the tests actually assert, and cite the specific tolerance.

findings.title: The v3.8.0 friendly-error system covers ~5% of failure sites and exactly the 6 files that got a test; 136 raw stop() and 13 divergent torch gates bypass it
findings.correction: Counts reproduce exactly: 14 `.stopf(`, 7 `.assert_type(`, 136 raw `stop(`, 154 `stopifnot(`, zero rlang/cli; helpers defined once in R/core_utils.R (.stopf at :39-45, .assert_type at :49-54, .assert_covariates :6-13, .assert_coords :15-27) with the "Use sparingly at user-facing entry points" note at :33; 13 torch-gate sites with 9 wordings. But "The adopted set is EXACTLY the set covered by tests/testthat/test-error-messages.R" is wrong: R/llm_kg_pipeline.R has 3 `.stopf` calls and is outside that file's declared scope (:4-7 names bhs_fit, gnn_build_graph, dm_fit, no_deeponet_fit). The "165 exports get a bare stop()" framing also ignores the 12 `.assert_covariates` and 3 `.assert_coords` call sites, which do produce named, readable messages across more files. This is style/consistency debt, not a defect — no failure mode is described.
findings.evidence:
Helpers are defined once, in R/core_utils.R: `.stopf` (:39-45, adds "[caller] ... \n Hint:") and `.assert_type` (:49-54), plus the older `.assert_covariates` (:6-13) and `.assert_coords` (:15-27).
Adoption counts across all 70 files in R/: 14 `.stopf(` calls in 6 files only — R/core_utils.R (2, one of which is the definition), R/pilar10_graph_nn.R (3), R/pilar9_diffusion_models.R (3), R/llm_kg_pipeline.R (3), R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R (1), R/pilar8_neural_operators.R (2). 7 `.assert_type(` calls in 4 files: R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:52, R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:91/:94/:97, R/pilar8_neural_operators.R:411/:413/:421.
Against that: 136 raw `stop(`, 154 `stopifnot(`, 6 `warning(`, and zero `rlang::abort` / `cli::` usage anywhere in R/.
The adopted set is EXACTLY the set covered by tests/testthat/test-error-messages.R, whose header at :4-7 names its scope as "`bhs_fit()`, `gnn_build_graph()`, `dm_fit()`, and `no_deeponet_fit()`" — the initiative went precisely as far as its own test file and stopped. The 13-file, 45-export `causal_*` family (~4 700 LOC) has zero `.stopf`/`.assert_type` uses, as do all 7 `foundation_*` files, all 6 `quantum_*` files and all 8 `active_*` files. Worst single offender: R/foundation_tiles.R with 10 raw `stop()`.
The torch dependency gate is the clearest symptom: 13 sites, 3 named helpers (`.moco_require_torch` R/foundation_moco.R:28, `.ft_require_torch` R/foundation_finetune.R:40, `.qk_require` R/quantum_vqe.R:36) and 9 distinct message wordings — "Install `torch` to run the encoder." (foundation_embed_coords.R:78), "Install the `torch` package to use foundation_simclr_*()." (foundation_simclr.R:20), "Install the `torch` package (and its MPS / CUDA backend) to use ..." (foundation_finetune.R:43), "torch is required for foundation_mcdropout_predict()." (foundation_posterior.R:158), "Install `torch` to use backend = 'torch'." (pilar8:109, pilar8:406, pilar9:174, pilar10:196), "Install the `torch` package (and run torch::install_torch() ..." (piml_neural_ode.R:13), "Install the `torch` package to use temporal_convlstm_*()." (temporal_convlstm.R:14), "torch is required for temporal_convlstm_mcdropout_predict()." (temporal_posterior.R:186). None uses `.stopf`, and only piml_neural_ode.R:13 mentions `torch::install_torch()`.
findings.impact: 14 friendly errors against ~290 raw failure sites means the documented user-experience improvement is real for 4 functions and cosmetic for the other 165 exports. A user who mistypes an argument to any `causal_*`, `foundation_*` or `quantum_*` function gets a bare stop() or an unreadable `stopifnot` deparse, and gets one of 9 different answers to "how do I install torch". The `.stopf` docstring at R/core_utils.R:33 says "Use sparingly at user-facing entry points" — but 165 exported functions ARE user-facing entry points, so the guidance itself is what capped adoption.
findings.action: Add `.require_ns <- function(pkg, what, hint = NULL)` to R/core_utils.R and collapse all 13 torch gates plus the `.moco_require_torch`/`.ft_require_torch`/`.qk_require` trio onto it with one message and one hint (`torch::install_torch()`). Then convert `stop()` to `.stopf()` in the highest-traffic exported entry points first — R/foundation_tiles.R (10), R/active_query.R (8), R/foundation_embed_coords.R (7), R/uncertainty.R (6) — and extend tests/testthat/test-error-messages.R to cover one entry point per pillar so the pattern is enforced rather than aspirational. Also amend the "Use sparingly" guidance at R/core_utils.R:33.

findings.title: history[history > 0] injects NA into fit$history; the fix exists in all four torch files and none of the three pure-R files
findings.correction: none — `grep -rn 'history\[history > 0' R/` returns exactly the seven sites claimed, split exactly as claimed: bare filter at pilar8_neural_operators.R:269 and :527 and pilar10_graph_nn.R:283; NA-aware `| is.na(history)` at pilar8_neural_operators_torch.R:128/:214, pilar9_diffusion_torch.R:212 and pilar10_graph_nn_torch.R:179; pilar9_diffusion_models.R:254 has no filter at all. NA-insertion semantics reproduce (`c(1,NaN,3,0,0)[x>0]` -> `1 NA 3`), and the `if (!is.finite(history[ep])) next` at pilar8:255/:511 makes the non-finite path reachable by design. User-visible effect is a mis-aligned loss-trajectory vector only.
findings.evidence:
Broken (bare filter): R/pilar8_neural_operators.R:269 `history = history[history > 0]`, R/pilar8_neural_operators.R:527 (same), R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:283 `history  = history[history > 0]`.
Fixed (NA-aware): R/pilar8_neural_operators_torch.R:128 and :214, R/pilar9_diffusion_torch.R:212, R/pilar10_graph_nn_torch.R:179 — all four read `history[history > 0 | is.na(history)]`.
Third variant: R/pilar9_diffusion_models.R:257 `history = history,` with no filter at all.
The NA leak is real, verified: `Rscript -e 'x <- c(1, NaN, 3, 0, 0); print(x[x > 0])'` prints `1 NA 3` — logical subsetting with an NA index INSERTS an NA element rather than dropping it.
The non-finite path is reachable and deliberate: R/pilar8_neural_operators.R:255 and :511 both read `if (!is.finite(history[ep])) next`, which is only meaningful if `history[ep]` can be NaN/Inf — and `next` leaves the poisoned value in the vector.
findings.impact: Four different conventions for the same three-token idiom across seven sites in six files, with the correct one applied only to the torch variants. Someone found and fixed this bug in the torch files and never backported it, which is a strong signal that the pure-R/torch pairs are maintained as copies rather than as one implementation with two backends. The user-visible effect is a silently mis-aligned loss trajectory.
findings.action: Add one internal helper to R/core_utils.R, e.g. `.trim_history <- function(h) h[seq_len(max(which(h != 0 | is.na(h)), 0L))]` (truncate at the last recorded epoch rather than filtering, which also preserves index-to-epoch alignment), and replace all seven sites: R/pilar8_neural_operators.R:269 and :527, R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:283, R/pilar8_neural_operators_torch.R:128 and :214, R/pilar9_diffusion_torch.R:212, R/pilar10_graph_nn_torch.R:179, plus R/pilar9_diffusion_models.R:257. Then add `expect_true(all(is.finite(fit$history)))` to the pure-R tests in tests/testthat/test-pilar8-neural-operators.R and test-pilar10-gat.R to match tests/testthat/test-pilar8-torch.R:21.

findings.title: 169 exports + 73 S3 methods is an exceptionally wide public API for 19.7k LOC, with several internal-looking primitives promoted to the surface
findings.evidence:
NAMESPACE: 169 `export()`, 73 `S3method()`, 1 `importFrom()`, 1 `useDynLib()` — 242 entries against 19 700 LOC in R/, i.e. one public name per ~81 lines. Export distribution by prefix: causal 45, foundation 22, quantum 19, al 14, piml 13, llm 13, temporal 11, edaphos 10, qf 5, gnn 4, dm 3, benchmark 3, uncertainty 2, no 2, bhs 1, active 1, as 1.
The S3 surface is 73 methods over 4 generics — 42 `print`, 16 `predict`, 12 `as_edaphos_posterior`, 4 `summary`, 1 `autoplot` — i.e. 42 distinct printable classes.
No accidental exports were found: 242 roxygen `@export` tags exactly equal the 242 NAMESPACE entries, all 182 man pages resolve (169 exports + 6 predict/summary/autoplot method pages + 3 data pages + edaphos-package + edaphos-roadmap), and no dotted internal appears in NAMESPACE. That part is clean.
Candidates that read as internal primitives promoted to public: `temporal_convlstm_cell` (a single LSTM cell), `dm_cosine_schedule` (a noise-schedule table), `quantum_scale`, `qf_embed_reduce` (a PCA wrapper), and the three `benchmark_fit_p*` functions (R/benchmark_wosis.R:79/:156/:217, which are benchmark harnesses rather than user algorithms). `edaphos_zenodo_release` is release tooling exported as a public API.
File sizes are NOT the problem: 70 files, mean 281 lines, max 776 (R/foundation_moco.R), and the largest files decompose into 8-16 named functions each — cohesive, not dumping grounds. The mild exception is R/foundation_moco.R, which carries four separable concerns in one file: 7 augmentation primitives (:117-206), encoder/projection builders (:38-115), the InfoNCE loss (:223), and 3 exported entry points plus the tile-pipeline variant (:291, :428, :480, :688).
findings.impact: The wide surface is the main reason a single-author CRAN/rOpenSci submission of this package will be slow to review: a reviewer cannot form an opinion on 169 functions. Every export is also a permanent deprecation obligation.
findings.action: Before submission, demote the clear primitives to internal (`temporal_convlstm_cell`, `qf_embed_reduce`, `quantum_scale`) or document them under `@keywords internal`, and move `edaphos_zenodo_release` and the three `benchmark_fit_p*` harnesses out of the public API (inst/ or a companion package). Target a first-release surface of ~100 exports and add the rest on demand. Separately, split R/foundation_moco.R into foundation_moco_augment.R (:117-206) and foundation_moco.R, and consider a shared `.print_edaphos_fit(x, fields)` helper in R/core_utils.R to collapse the 42 print methods.

findings.title: pkgdown reference index selects on `has_concept("pilar1")` but no Rd file has a `\concept{}` tag
findings.correction: The premise checks out (\_pkgdown.yml:123 `- has_concept("pilar1")`; 0 of 182 man/*.Rd contain `\concept{`; 0 `@concept`/`@family` in R/) but the conclusion is false. I read the installed pkgdown: `section_topics()` calls `select_topics(match_strings, topics, error_pkg=, error_path=, error_call=)` WITHOUT `check = TRUE`, and `select_topics` only aborts when `check` is TRUE; it aborts on an all-empty section (`purrr::every(indexes, is_empty)`) and otherwise runs `indexes <- purrr::discard(indexes, is_empty)`. The Pilar-1 section also has `starts_with("causal_")` etc., which match, so the zero-match selector is silently dropped. No abort. Sub-claim 2 is also refuted: man/edaphos-package.Rd carries `\keyword{internal}` at line 189, and `check_missing_topics()` computes `missing <- !in_index & !pkg$topics$internal`, so it is exempt from the index requirement (edaphos-roadmap.Rd is internal too). I simulated the full reference index against all 182 topics: ZERO non-internal topics are unmatched, so `check_missing_topics()` will not fire either. What survives is minor: a dead selector, `news: releases:` stale at v2.0.0 (cosmetic navbar list), and articles/ being unrendered — which inst/rosc/submission.md:82-84 itself discloses as "`.Rbuildignore`-d to keep the vignette build fast". `pkgdown::build_site_github_pages()` is not blocked.
findings.evidence:
`_pkgdown.yml:123` is `- has_concept("pilar1")`. Checking the corpus: **0 of 182 `man/*.Rd` files contain `\concept{`**, and `grep -o '@(concept|family) ...' R/*.R` returns **0 matches** — no roxygen `@concept` or `@family` tag exists anywhere in the package, so the selector matches nothing. pkgdown aborts on a topic selector that resolves to zero topics.

Second gap: `man/edaphos-package.Rd` is not reachable from any selector. The index uses `starts_with("edaphos_")` (`_pkgdown.yml:197`) which does not match the hyphenated `edaphos-package`; only `edaphos-roadmap` is listed explicitly (`:217`).

Third: the four documents in `articles/` (`pilar1-causal-real.Rmd`, `pilar3-4d-real.Rmd`, `pilar5-soilgrids-br.Rmd`, `llm-kg-benchmark.Rmd`) render nowhere — they are excluded from the tarball by `.Rbuildignore:21` (`^articles$`) and pkgdown only picks up `vignettes/`, and the `_pkgdown.yml` `articles:` block (`:220-249`) lists only the 14 files in `vignettes/`. `inst/rosc/submission.md:82-84` presents them to the rOpenSci editor as "4 additional articles in `articles/` (case studies)".

Fourth: `_pkgdown.yml:252-257` `news: releases:` stops at `v2.0.0` — 10 minor versions stale.

`inst/rosc/submission.md:114-117` claims "pkgdown builds cleanly locally", and `RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:75-98` treats the documentation site as blocked only on a GitHub Pages settings toggle.
findings.impact: `pkgdown::build_site_github_pages()` in `.github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml:56` fails on the zero-match selector, so flipping the GH Pages source (release step 4) cannot produce a site. rOpenSci requires a working pkgdown site, and the submission document asserts one exists. Four vignette-quality case studies are dead weight in the repo, visible to no reader.
findings.action: Delete `_pkgdown.yml:123` (`has_concept("pilar1")`) — the `starts_with("causal_")` selectors below it already cover Pillar 1 — or add `@concept pilar1` roxygen tags and re-document. Add `edaphos-package` to the index. Decide whether `articles/*.Rmd` become real `vignettes/articles/` entries (pkgdown-rendered, not shipped) or are deleted. Refresh the `news:` release list. Verify with a local `pkgdown::build_site()` before claiming it builds.

findings.title: Maintainer-only files install into the user's library; CITATION metadata is stale and there is no inst/CITATION
findings.evidence:
No `.Rinstignore` exists, so everything under `inst/` lands in the installed library:
- `inst/rosc/submission.md` (8 KB) — a draft rOpenSci pre-submission issue body, including "Questions for the rOpenSci editor" (`:140-152`) and the author's email/ORCID (`:154-158`). It ships to every user of the package.
- `inst/WORDLIST` (20 KB, 2032 lines) — dead: `spelling` is not in `DESCRIPTION` Suggests and there is no `tests/spelling.R`.

Citation metadata is inconsistent and unreachable from R:
- `CITATION.cff:109-110` — `version: "2.1.0"` / `date-released: "2026-04-23"` while `DESCRIPTION:3` is `3.10.0`.
- `CITATION.cff:184` — the `preferred-citation` block says `version: "1.6.0"`.
- `.zenodo.json` (6.2 KB) contains **no** `version` field at all.
- `CITATION.cff` is excluded from the tarball by `.Rbuildignore:10`, and there is no `inst/CITATION`, so `citation("edaphos")` falls back to the auto-generated DESCRIPTION stub — losing the Zenodo DOI `10.5281/zenodo.19683708` that `README.md:7` and `cran-comments.md:103` advertise.

Housekeeping: `.Rbuildignore` lists `^\.claude$` twice (lines 2 and 18), and has no catch-all for stray root files — a `GATEOUT.rds` (2,082 B) is currently untracked at the repo root (`git status --porcelain` shows `?? GATEOUT.rds`) and a simulated build confirms it would ship in the tarball. (This particular file is an audit scratch artefact, not committed code — the point is that nothing stops such a file from shipping.)
findings.impact: Shipping a rOpenSci submission draft inside the installed package is the kind of detail reviewers notice and comment on. Three different version numbers across `DESCRIPTION`/`CITATION.cff`/`preferred-citation` undermine the Zenodo-archival reproducibility story, and `citation("edaphos")` silently omits the DOI the README leads with.
findings.action: Move `inst/rosc/submission.md` to a non-installed location (e.g. `.github/` or the repo root with an `.Rbuildignore` entry). Either wire up `spelling` (add to Suggests + `tests/spelling.R`) or delete `inst/WORDLIST`. Add `inst/CITATION` carrying the Zenodo DOI, and regenerate `CITATION.cff` / `.zenodo.json` from DESCRIPTION with `cffr::cff_write()` so the version can never drift again. Drop the duplicate `.Rbuildignore` line and add `^[^/]+\.rds$`-style protection against root scratch files.

findings.title: 6 of 40 Suggests are never used anywhere in the package
findings.correction: Only 5 of the 6 hold. `gstat` IS called: data-raw/case_cerrado_run.R:207 `gstat::variogram`, :211 `gstat::fit.variogram`, :213 `gstat::vgm`, :226 `gstat::krige` -- the claim "never called" is false. `abind` and `fmsb` are not "0 hits repo-wide": both appear in the Dockerfile install list (Dockerfile:51 and :52); they are unused in package code. RColorBrewer (only .github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml:48), geobr (only data-raw/case_cerrado_prepare.R:56 + prose; bib entry starts at references.bib:597) and ecmwfr (no `ecmwfr::` call; string/comment only at R/foundation_tiles.R:17, :195, :205-206) are confirmed. The stated impact is also wrong: R CMD check does not NOTE unused *Suggests* (only unused Imports), so no check NOTE follows.
findings.evidence:
40 `Suggests` (DESCRIPTION:36-76) against 7 `Imports`. Searching `R/ tests/ vignettes/ man/ inst/ articles/ cheatsheets/ data-raw/` for `pkg::`, `requireNamespace("pkg"`, `library(pkg)`, `loadNamespace("pkg")`:
- `abind` (DESCRIPTION:37) — **0 hits repo-wide**.
- `fmsb` (:49) — **0 hits repo-wide**.
- `RColorBrewer` (:63) — 0 code hits; sole occurrence is `.github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml:48` (`any::RColorBrewer`).
- `geobr` (:51) — only `data-raw/case_cerrado_prepare.R:56` (Rbuildignored) plus prose in `vignettes/case-cerrado-end-to-end.Rmd:95,181` and `vignettes/references.bib:597`.
- `gstat` (:56) — only prose/bibliography (`R/pillars_roadmap.R:13`, `vignettes/case-cerrado-end-to-end.Rmd:78-79`, `references.bib:579`); never called.
- `ecmwfr` (:48) — no `ecmwfr::` call exists. It appears only inside a string literal at `R/foundation_tiles.R:205-206` ("Install `ecmwfr`, authenticate with `ecmwfr::wf_set_key()`") — i.e. inside an error message.

Also `devtools` (:43): the only reach is `R/edaphos_zenodo_release.R:103-107`, `if (!requireNamespace("devtools", quietly = TRUE)) ... build_fn <- tryCatch(getExportedValue("devtools", "build"), ...)` — an exported user-facing function (`edaphos_zenodo_release()`) that builds a tarball of the package itself.
findings.impact: `R CMD check` NOTEs unused declared dependencies, and each phantom Suggests inflates the dependency graph CRAN/rOpenSci reviewers must vet. `devtools` in the dependency closure of a released package, reached from an exported maintainer-only release helper, is a specific rOpenSci review flag.
findings.action: Delete `abind`, `fmsb`, `RColorBrewer`, `geobr`, `gstat`, `ecmwfr` from DESCRIPTION:36-76 (move `RColorBrewer` reliance into the pkgdown workflow only, where it already is). Separately, un-export `edaphos_zenodo_release()` — move it to `data-raw/` or `tools/` as maintainer tooling — and drop `devtools` from Suggests.

findings.title: `MASS::ginv()` called unguarded at 5 sites while MASS is Suggests-only
findings.correction: none on the facts — `grep -rn 'MASS::' R/` returns exactly the five cited sites (R/causal_active_learning.R:90; R/causal_iv.R:113, :117, :285, :289), `grep -rn 'requireNamespace("MASS"' R/` returns nothing, the 17 guarded namespaces are Matrix bnlearn dagitty dbarts devtools digest geodata ggplot2 igraph ontologyIndex ranger reticulate sp spBayes stringdist terra torch (no MASS), DESCRIPTION:59 has MASS under Suggests, and cran-comments.md:49-50 does make the blanket claim. SEVERITY IS BADLY INFLATED: MASS is an R *Recommended* package — it ships with every standard R distribution and is present on every CRAN check machine and every CI leg here. The described failure ("there is no package called 'MASS'") is therefore near-unreachable in practice; the real content is a one-line hygiene fix (move MASS to Imports, or add a guard) plus the false blanket sentence in cran-comments, which finding 7 already covers.
findings.evidence:
`MASS` is declared at `DESCRIPTION:59` under `Suggests`, but there is **no `requireNamespace("MASS")` anywhere in R/** (the 17 distinct `requireNamespace("pkg")` guards cover torch, reticulate, dagitty, terra, geodata, stringdist, sp, ggplot2, ranger, igraph, digest, dbarts, spBayes, ontologyIndex, devtools, bnlearn, Matrix — not MASS).

The five unguarded call sites are all singular-matrix fallbacks reached from the Pillar 1 public API:
- `R/causal_active_learning.R:90`  `XtX_inv <- tryCatch(solve(XtX), error = function(e) MASS::ginv(XtX))`
- `R/causal_iv.R:113`  `ZZ_inv <- tryCatch(solve(crossprod(Z_all)), error = function(e) MASS::ginv(crossprod(Z_all)))`
- `R/causal_iv.R:117`  `XPX_inv <- tryCatch(solve(XPX), error = function(e) MASS::ginv(XPX))`
- `R/causal_iv.R:285`  same pattern in the second 2SLS path
- `R/causal_iv.R:289`  same

`cran-comments.md:49-50` asserts "Every Suggests is wrapped in `requireNamespace(..., quietly = TRUE)` inside the code that used it."
findings.impact: On any install without MASS, a rank-deficient design in `causal_iv_fit_2sls()` / `al_query_causal()` turns a recoverable numerical fallback into `there is no package called 'MASS'` — the opposite of the graceful degradation the code is trying to provide. Violates CRAN's "packages in Suggests must be used conditionally", and the blanket claim in cran-comments is false.
findings.action: Either promote `MASS` from Suggests to Imports (it is a recommended package, so no real install cost), or wrap the fallback: `error = function(e) { if (!requireNamespace("MASS", quietly = TRUE)) stop("Singular design; install 'MASS' for the pseudo-inverse fallback.", call. = FALSE); MASS::ginv(XtX) }`. Then correct `cran-comments.md:49-50`.

findings.title: Two network entry points call `httr2::req_perform()` with no error handling, against CRAN's graceful-failure policy
findings.evidence:
CRAN policy: "Packages which use Internet resources should fail gracefully with an informative message if the resource is not available or has changed (and not give a check warning nor error)."

`R/causal_corpus.R:114` — `resp <- httr2::req_perform(req)` inside `causal_corpus_scielo()` (defined at `:95`), no `tryCatch`. Contrast `R/causal_corpus.R:215` in `causal_corpus_openalex()`, which *does* wrap the same call: `resp <- tryCatch(httr2::req_perform(req), ...)`.

`R/causal_ontology.R:128` — `resp <- httr2::req_perform(req)` in the AGROVOC SPARQL path, no `tryCatch` (again inconsistent with `:330`, which checks `httr2::resp_status(resp) != 200L`).

The test suite does not expose this — `tests/testthat/test-causal-corpus.R:1-2` documents that "Corpus clients never actually hit the network in tests -- every live call is intercepted with `httr2::with_mocked_responses()`", and both corpus functions are mocked at `:43-46` and `:71-74`. But the discipline is thin overall: across 69 test files there is exactly **1** `skip_on_cran()` (`tests/testthat/test-quantum-kernel-rcpp.R:46`, for timing noise) and **0** `skip_if_offline()`; `tests/testthat/test-llm-kg-pipeline.R:49` opens a real socket to `http://127.0.0.1:1`.
findings.impact: A user (or any future non-mocked test/example) behind a proxy or on a CRAN check machine with no outbound access gets a raw httr2 curl error rather than an informative message. The absence of `skip_if_offline()` means a single future un-mocked network test would produce an ERROR on CRAN's daily checks after acceptance.
findings.action: Wrap `R/causal_corpus.R:114` and `R/causal_ontology.R:128` in the same `tryCatch` + `resp_status` pattern already used at `R/causal_corpus.R:215` and `R/causal_ontology.R:330`, returning an empty typed data.frame with a `message()` on failure. Add `skip_if_offline()` alongside `skip_on_cran()` to any test that touches a socket.

findings.title: Two exported functions are unconditional `stop()` stubs, documented and counted as shipped features
findings.correction: The stubs are real: R/foundation_tiles.R:183-191 (`foundation_tile_source_modis`) and :202-210 (`foundation_tile_source_era5`), both `@export`, both `@param ... Ignored.`, both with generated man pages; and the \value gap is real (R/foundation_tiles.R:181 gives modis `@return Nothing; always stops with an install-hint message.` while era5 at :193-201 has none). BUT THE ROADMAP CLAIM IS FALSE. R/pillars_roadmap.R:13 (the Pillar 4 row) names only `[foundation_tile_source_soilgrids()]`, `[foundation_tile_align()]`, `[foundation_tile_dataset()]`, `[foundation_moco_pretrain_tiles()]`, `[foundation_moco_embed_raster()]` — it does NOT list srtm, worldclim, modis or era5. So "a user reading the roadmap … sees five tile sources; two of them can only ever throw" does not happen, and neither stub is presented anywhere as implemented; each one's own help page says it returns an install hint. Exported install-hint stubs with honest documentation are a routine, accepted R pattern.
findings.evidence:
`R/foundation_tiles.R:183-191`:
```r
foundation_tile_source_modis <- function(...) {
  stop("MODIS ingestion requires NASA EarthData credentials and a MODIS client. Install `MODIStsp` or use `rgee` via `reticulate`, ...", call. = FALSE)
}
```
`R/foundation_tiles.R:202-210`:
```r
foundation_tile_source_era5 <- function(...) {
  stop("ERA5 ingestion requires a Copernicus Climate Data Store API key. Install `ecmwfr`, ...", call. = FALSE)
}
```
Both are `@export`ed (present in `NAMESPACE`), both have generated `man/` pages, and both take only `@param ... Ignored.`

`R/pillars_roadmap.R:13` (rendered into `man/edaphos-roadmap.Rd:18`) lists `foundation_tile_source_soilgrids()`, `foundation_tile_source_srtm()`, `foundation_tile_source_worldclim()` alongside them under a Pillar 4 row marked **`implemented`** with a "**planetary-scale tile pipeline**" label.

Related Rd gap: of the 182 Rd files, the only two documenting an *exported function* with no `\value` section are `man/foundation_tile_source_era5.Rd` and `man/no_deeponet_fit.Rd` (the other five without `\value` are the three datasets, `edaphos-package`, and `edaphos-roadmap`, which legitimately use `\format`/no return).
findings.impact: A user reading the roadmap or the reference index sees five tile sources; two of them can only ever throw. rOpenSci reviewers treat exported-but-unimplemented API as a scope/honesty issue, and `no_deeponet_fit` missing `\value` draws CRAN's standard "please add \value to all exported functions" request.
findings.action: Un-export `foundation_tile_source_modis` and `foundation_tile_source_era5` (keep them as internal `.tile_source_*` helpers or delete them), and amend the Pillar 4 row in `R/pillars_roadmap.R:13` to say three sources are implemented and MODIS/ERA5 are not. Add `\value` (via `@return`) to `no_deeponet_fit`.

findings.title: Placeholder and NA DOIs are committed: the exported weights registry advertises an encoder with no URL, DOI or checksum
findings.correction: The NA row is real (R/foundation_weights.R:51 name, url/sha256/doi/published_at all `NA_character_`, `edaphos_version = "3.11.0"` — a version with no NEWS section). But this is a documented, guarded design the auditor did not read: R/foundation_weights.R:145-152 states "The `url`, `doi` and `published_at` fields remain NA until the Zenodo deposit is created; the package consumer sees a clear 'no published URL yet' error until the next maintenance release wires them up", and R/foundation_weights.R:185-190 (in `foundation_weights_download`) implements exactly that error. The "fake DOIs" sub-claim is refuted: every occurrence is an explicitly labelled placeholder — V1_3_2_HANDOFF.md:97-98 "Zenodo mints a fresh DOI like `10.5281/zenodo.20000001`", :102-103 prefixed "e.g.", :123 "Replace the three string values with the ones from Step 3", UPLOAD_INSTRUCTIONS.md:63/65 both "(e.g. ...)". Nothing presents them as real deposits. Residual real defect: the "3.11.0" string, and roxygen at :87-98 calling the registry a catalogue of what is "published".
findings.evidence: R/foundation_weights.R:48-84 registers two encoders. The second, `edaphos-cerrado-moco-v2` (:51), has `url` = `NA_character_` (:67 "# filled after the user's Zenodo upload"), `sha256` = `NA_character_` (:71), `doi` = `NA_character_` (:75), `published_at` = `NA_character_` (:80), and `edaphos_version` = "3.11.0" (:82, a version that does not exist -- see finding #1). This data frame is the return value of the exported `foundation_weights_list()` (documented at R/foundation_weights.R:87-98 "Returns a data frame describing every pretrained encoder published by the `edaphos` project: its name, the Zenodo DOI, ..."), so the public catalogue lists an encoder that is by construction undownloadable. Fake DOIs also sit in tracked files: tools/pretrain/V1_3_2_HANDOFF.md:98,102,103,117,118 and tools/pretrain/wire_up_v2_doi.R:13-14 use `10.5281/zenodo.20000001`; tools/pretrain/UPLOAD_INSTRUCTIONS.md:63,65 uses `10.5281/zenodo.1234567`. tools/ is .Rbuildignore'd (.Rbuildignore:12) so these do not reach CRAN, but they are public on GitHub.
findings.impact: `foundation_weights_list()` presents a published-looking row for an encoder that was never deposited; a user who calls `foundation_weights_load("edaphos-cerrado-moco-v2")` hits the NA-URL guard instead of getting weights. The description at R/foundation_weights.R:55 compounds this by stating results in the future tense ("Final InfoNCE loss expected ~0.4 at step 200000") inside a registry documented as a catalogue of *published* artefacts. The 20000001/1234567 strings read as real DOIs to anyone skimming the hand-off docs.
findings.action: Either gate the moco-v2 row out of `foundation_weights_list()`'s public output until the Zenodo deposit lands (filter rows with `is.na(url)`, or add an explicit `status = c("published", "pending")` column so the NA state is self-describing), or drop the row from R/foundation_weights.R:48-84 and re-add it in the same commit that wires the real DOI via tools/pretrain/wire_up_v2_doi.R. Mark the placeholder DOIs unmistakably (e.g. `10.5281/zenodo.XXXXXXX`) in tools/pretrain/V1_3_2_HANDOFF.md and tools/pretrain/UPLOAD_INSTRUCTIONS.md.

findings.title: _pkgdown.yml's release list stops at v2.0.0 and its site description still says six pillars
findings.correction: File facts all hold: _pkgdown.yml:249-254 `news: releases:` has exactly four entries, newest "v2.0.0 — Quantum kernel × Foundation", none with `href`; :44-48 "Six research pillars…"; :66 "Capstone — six pillars integrated"; :161/:167/:172/:177 present Pilares 7-10 as v2.3.0+/v2.4.0+/v2.5.0+/v2.6.0+; :204 is the only v3.10.0 title; :1 is the site url. BUT THE IMPACT IS WRONG: pkgdown's `news.releases` field only populates a *highlighted-releases dropdown*; the generated changelog page still renders the whole of NEWS.md. It does not "silently hide 24 releases", and no visitor "concludes development stopped at v2.0.0" from the changelog — at most from the dropdown. That guts the severity: what remains is stale nav/description copy.
findings.evidence: _pkgdown.yml:248-253: `news: releases:` contains only four entries -- "v2.0.0 — Quantum kernel × Foundation", "v1.9.x", "v1.8.x", "v1.7.x" -- and none has an `href`. Twenty-four NEWS releases (v2.1.0 through v3.10.0) are absent. _pkgdown.yml:43-48 home description: "Six research pillars confronting specific methodological gaps in DSM: Causal AI ..., Physics-Informed ML, 4D Pedometry, Foundation Models, Autonomous Active Learning, and Quantum ML" -- enumerating six while DESCRIPTION:8-9 says ten. Reference section titles present v2.x as the frontier (_pkgdown.yml:161 "Pilar 7 — Bayesian Hierarchical Spatial (v2.3.0+)", :167 Pilar 8 v2.4.0+, :172 Pilar 9 v2.5.0+, :177 Pilar 10 v2.6.0+); only :204 "LLM-KG production pipeline (v3.10.0)" acknowledges 3.x. The navbar articles menu opens with _pkgdown.yml:66 `- text: "Capstone — six pillars integrated"`.
findings.impact: The generated pkgdown site -- the documentation URL declared at _pkgdown.yml:1 and the one rOpenSci reviewers browse -- presents the package as a six-pillar project whose latest release is v2.0.0. The changelog sidebar silently hides 24 releases, so a visitor concludes development stopped at v2.0.0.
findings.action: Delete the hand-maintained `news: releases:` block at _pkgdown.yml:248-253 and let pkgdown render NEWS.md in full (or regenerate it per release), rewrite the home description at _pkgdown.yml:43-48 to the ten-pillar text, and drop the "(v2.x+)" suffixes from the Pilar 7-10 section titles at :161,167,172,177 since they now read as version ceilings rather than introduction points.

findings.title: RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md instructs the maintainer to upload artefacts that do not exist and names the wrong deploy action
findings.correction: Three of three file facts verified: :13-15 points at `/tmp/edaphos_release_tarballs/edaphos_3.10.0.tar.gz`; :53-55 claims `tools/zenodo_release.zip` is "already built" while `ls tools/` shows only make-readme-figures.R, readme-outputs.txt, pretrain/, and .gitignore:64-65 excludes `tools/zenodo_release/` and `tools/zenodo_release.zip`; :91-92 names peaceiris/actions-gh-pages while .github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml:61 uses `JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4.5.0`. BUT "Steps 1 and 3 cannot be executed as written" is half wrong: the checklist's own :25 says `devtools::submit_cran()` will "Re-build the source tarball (or re-use the existing one)", so step 1 is self-healing and the /tmp path is cosmetic. Only step 3's missing zip is a real dead end, and RELEASE.md:20-32 does carry the `edaphos_zenodo_release(output_dir = "tools/zenodo_release", …)` call that regenerates it (the auditor concedes this). Net: two stale strings and one wrong action name — minutes of friction, not a broken release.
findings.evidence: RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:13-15 "The package source tarball is already built at: /tmp/edaphos_release_tarballs/edaphos_3.10.0.tar.gz   (17 MB)" -- an ephemeral /tmp path, absent on any fresh machine or after reboot. :53-55 "The bundle is already built at: tools/zenodo_release.zip   (22.2 MB, 24 files)"; `ls tools/` shows only make-readme-figures.R, readme-outputs.txt and pretrain/ -- the zip is absent, and .gitignore:64-65 excludes both `tools/zenodo_release/` and `tools/zenodo_release.zip`, so it can never be committed and the claim "already built" can never be true for anyone but the original author's working copy. :91-92 states the GH-Pages branch option "works with the existing peaceiris/actions-gh-pages step in `.github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml`"; .github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml:61 actually uses `JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4.5.0`.
findings.impact: Steps 1 and 3 of the four-step release cannot be executed as written -- the maintainer opens the Zenodo "New version" dialog with nothing to upload and no instructions to regenerate the bundle (RELEASE.md:20-32 has the generating call, but the v3.10.0 checklist does not reference it). The wrong action name sends anyone debugging the Pages deployment to the wrong workflow step.
findings.action: Replace the two "already built at" claims with the commands that produce the artefacts (`devtools::build()` for the tarball; `edaphos_zenodo_release(output_dir = "tools/zenodo_release", include_tarball = TRUE, zip = TRUE)` per RELEASE.md:20-32 for the bundle) and record the checksums instead of the paths. Correct RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:91-92 to `JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4.5.0`.

findings.title: 32 of the last 33 NEWS releases have no git tag, violating the project's own documented release policy
findings.correction: none — counts verified independently: `git tag -l` = 18 tags (v0.1.0–v0.9.0, v1.0.0–v1.6.0 incl. v1.3.1, v3.10.0); `grep -c '^# edaphos' NEWS.md` = 43; the 32 untagged versions match exactly; CONTRIBUTING.md:87 reads "Every release gets a git tag (`vX.Y.Z`) and a NEWS.md entry."; NEWS.md:1787 is `# edaphos 0.8.0` (oldest); README.md:279 says "`NEWS.md` back to v0.1.0"; only 3 workflows exist. SEVERITY IS INFLATED, not the facts: the release actually being prepared (v3.10.0) IS tagged, so nothing about CRAN/rOpenSci/Zenodo is blocked. This is retrospective hygiene fixable by a for-loop over `git tag`. The GitHub-release-badge sub-claim ("most likely renders 'no releases'") is unverifiable offline and is speculation.
findings.evidence: `git tag -l` returns 18 tags: v0.1.0-v0.9.0, v1.0.0, v1.1.0, v1.2.0, v1.3.0, v1.3.1, v1.4.0, v1.5.0, v1.6.0, and v3.10.0. NEWS.md contains 43 version sections. Per-version check: TAGGED only for 0.8.0, 0.9.0, 1.0.0, 1.1.0, 1.2.0, 1.3.0, 1.3.1, 1.4.0, 1.5.0, 1.6.0, 3.10.0. UNTAGGED: 1.7.0, 1.7.1, 1.7.2, 1.8.0, 1.8.1, 1.8.2, 1.9.0, 1.9.1, 1.9.2, 2.0.0, 2.1.0, 2.1.3, 2.2.0, 2.2.1, 2.3.0, 2.4.0, 2.5.0, 2.6.0, 2.7.0, 2.8.0, 2.9.0, 2.9.1, 3.0.0, 3.1.0, 3.2.0, 3.3.0, 3.4.0, 3.5.0, 3.6.0, 3.7.0, 3.8.0, 3.9.0 (32 versions). CONTRIBUTING.md:87 states the policy explicitly: "Every release gets a git tag (`vX.Y.Z`) and a NEWS.md entry." The reverse gap also exists: tags v0.1.0 through v0.7.0 exist with NO NEWS section (NEWS.md's oldest heading is `# edaphos 0.8.0` at NEWS.md:1787), while README.md:279 claims "`NEWS.md` back to v0.1.0". There is no release-automation workflow: `.github/workflows/` contains only R-CMD-check.yaml, pkgdown.yaml, test-coverage.yaml.
findings.impact: Two years of claimed releases (v1.7.0 -> v3.9.0) are not addressable by ref. `remotes::install_github('...@v2.8.0')`, `@v3.0.0`, `@v3.9.0` all fail. Any reader trying to reproduce a NEWS claim, diff two releases, or cite a specific version cannot check out that version. The GitHub-release badge at README.md:8 (`img.shields.io/github/v/release/...`) reads GitHub *Releases*, of which there is no evidence any exist (tags alone do not create Releases, and no workflow publishes them) -- so that badge most likely renders "no releases" on the public README.
findings.action: Retro-tag the 32 missing versions from the commits that bumped DESCRIPTION (`git log -L 3,3:DESCRIPTION` gives the exact commit per version, e.g. 46df3d8=3.10.0, 5ceb86f=3.9.0, 71cd79f=3.8.0, ... , 41360ee=2.9.1) and push tags. Add a `.github/workflows/release.yaml` triggered on `v*` tags that publishes a GitHub Release with the matching NEWS.md section, so the policy at CONTRIBUTING.md:87 is enforced rather than aspirational. Backfill or delete the v0.1.0-v0.7.0 tags and fix the false claim at README.md:279.

findings.title: Dockerfile self-identifies as v2.1.0 and pins a 2026-04-23 CRAN snapshot, but installs HEAD
findings.correction: The v2.1.0 label/tag mismatch is real and every cited line checks out (Dockerfile:1, :9, :15, :19, :28, :41-43, :66-70 with ARG EDAPHOS_REF=main). But the load-bearing impact claim is wrong: "the frozen CRAN date means the image cannot install the dependency set that 3.10.0 actually needs" is false. `R_CRAN_WEB` is a *dated snapshot*, not a version whitelist — RcppArmadillo has been on CRAN since 2010 and Matrix ships with the R distribution, so both are trivially available at 2026-04-23. Moreover Dockerfile:67-70 does not pass `repos = Sys.getenv('R_CRAN_WEB')` at all, so `install_github(..., dependencies = TRUE)` resolves LinkingTo/Imports from the rocker image's own repo, not the pinned snapshot. What remains is a stale label on an image that builds current HEAD.
findings.evidence: Dockerfile:1 "# edaphos reproducibility Dockerfile  (v2.1.0)", :9 `docker build -t edaphos:2.1.0 .`, :15 and :19 run examples using `edaphos:2.1.0`, :28 OCI label `org.opencontainers.image.version="2.1.0"`, :41-43 "# CRAN deps (pin to the date of the edaphos v2.1.0 release so every rebuild is byte-reproducible)" with `ENV R_CRAN_WEB="https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/jammy/2026-04-23"`. But Dockerfile:66-70 installs `remotes::install_github('HugoMachadoRodrigues/edaphos', ref = '${EDAPHOS_REF}')` with `ARG EDAPHOS_REF=main`, i.e. whatever HEAD is at build time (currently 3.10.0+16 commits). The 2026-04-23 snapshot also predates dependencies the package now requires: `RcppArmadillo` (added to LinkingTo at v3.5.0, DESCRIPTION:86-88) and `Matrix` (Pilar 10 sparse GAT, v3.6.0) are not in the install list at Dockerfile:45-54. cran-comments.md:15 cites this Dockerfile as a test environment for v3.10.0.
findings.impact: An image tagged edaphos:2.1.0 containing edaphos 3.10.0+ is a reproducibility trap: the label lies about its contents, and the frozen CRAN date means the image cannot install the dependency set that 3.10.0 actually needs. cran-comments.md:15 offers this as evidence of a clean cross-platform check, so a CRAN reviewer building it gets a different package than the one under review.
findings.action: Derive the version instead of hardcoding it: parameterise Dockerfile:9,15,19,28 from a single `ARG EDAPHOS_VERSION`, set `ARG EDAPHOS_REF=v3.10.0` so the image pins the tag rather than a moving branch, advance the R_CRAN_WEB snapshot at Dockerfile:43 to the actual release date, and add RcppArmadillo and Matrix to the install list at Dockerfile:45-54.

findings.title: v1.8.3 (expand LLM gold standard from 72 to 300 claims) is untouched — still 30 abstracts / 72 claims
findings.correction: none — I parsed the file: inst/extdata/cerrado_gold_standard_v1.jsonl has 30 records with fields abstract_id,title,abstract_text,year,topic,claims and `sum(sapply(x$claims, NROW))` = exactly 72; the _draft is also 30 lines; inst/extdata/cerrado_claims_real_corpus.jsonl is 301 lines of machine `{cause,effect,source,evidence,confidence,timestamp}` tuples from openalex.org with no human label. README.md:1715 still marks v1.8.3 📝 and README.md:1659 states the 72→300+ goal. One extra data point the finding misses and that sharpens it: `git rev-list v3.10.0..HEAD` contains fd4ab0b "data(v1.8.3): expand cerrado_claims_real_corpus.jsonl from 210 -> 301 claims (closes the v1.8 roadmap promise)" — so the promise was declared closed against the unlabelled corpus, not the gold standard, while the roadmap row still says 📝. SEVERITY DEFLATED: this is an openly-tracked, self-declared 📝 roadmap item, not a concealed defect, and nothing ships claiming otherwise.
findings.evidence: README.md:1715 `| v1.8.3  | Expand gold-standard to 300 real claims (via v1.8.2 tool) | 📝    |`; README.md:1659 says the annotation vignette exists "to scale gold-standard from 72 to 300+ claims". Measured: `inst/extdata/cerrado_gold_standard_v1.jsonl` has 30 lines and, summing the `claims` arrays, exactly 72 claims (fields per record: abstract_id, title, abstract_text, year, topic, claims). `cerrado_gold_standard_v1_draft.jsonl` is also 30 lines. The 301-line `inst/extdata/cerrado_claims_real_corpus.jsonl` is NOT a gold standard — its records are machine-extracted `{cause, effect, source, evidence, confidence, timestamp}` tuples from OpenAlex, with no human label. The enabling tooling shipped long ago (`inst/shiny-apps/annotation/app.R`, `llm_preannotate*`, `data-raw/annotation_tool_demo.R`).
findings.impact: Every LLM-extractor quality number the package publishes (NEWS 1.8.0 / .zenodo.json: Claude F1 0.82, Gemma 4 free, GPT-4o-mini 5x faster, pairwise Cohen's kappa) rests on 72 claims from 30 abstracts. The roadmap itself flags that n as too small, and the tool built to fix it has been available since v1.8.1 without being used. This is the single clearest case of "tooling delivered, promised output not produced".
findings.action: Either run the v1.8.2 annotation tool over ~120 more abstracts to reach 300 claims and regenerate `inst/extdata/cerrado_gold_standard_v1.jsonl` + the benchmark RDS, or explicitly re-scope README.md:1715 and :1659 to the achievable n and state the resulting confidence-interval width on the F1 figures.

findings.title: V1_3_2_HANDOFF.md instructs the maintainer to cd into a directory named after a different project
findings.evidence:
`tools/pretrain/V1_3_2_HANDOFF.md:22-25`:
```bash
cd /path/to/GeoVersa
Rscript data-raw/pretrain_cerrado_train_v2.R
```
"GeoVersa" appears nowhere else in the repository (`grep -rn GeoVersa` matches only this line). The package, its DESCRIPTION, its URL (`https://github.com/HugoMachadoRodrigues/edaphos`) and every other path are `edaphos`.
findings.impact: The first command of the critical-path hand-off names a project that does not exist, suggesting the document was carried over from a predecessor repo. Combined with the stale "resuming from epoch 110000" figures at :32 (real state ~114 440) and the "~2 hours" budget at :20 (now ~1.9 h), the hand-off's step-1 preconditions cannot be trusted as written.
findings.action: Change `cd /path/to/GeoVersa` to `cd /path/to/edaphos` and refresh the resume step / duration figures at :20, :32 and :165 from the actual `state.rds$next_epoch` before the maintainer next picks this up.

findings.title: Documentation promises that point at content which does not exist: cheatsheets "on the pkgdown site", P8/P9 benchmarks "in vignettes/"
findings.evidence: `cheatsheets/README.md:22-24`: "These cheatsheets are NOT shipped in the CRAN tarball (.Rbuildignore excludes the cheatsheets/ directory) -- they live on the GitHub repo and the pkgdown site". `grep -rn cheatsheet _pkgdown.yml .github/` returns nothing: pkgdown has no `cheatsheets` navbar entry, no article group, and no mechanism to copy the directory into `docs/`. `INTRO.md:116-118`: "P2, P3, P8, P9 target depth profiles, temporal stacks, and raster patches respectively; they have their own task-appropriate benchmarks in `vignettes/`." `grep -rln 'no_fno_fit|no_deeponet_fit|dm_fit|dm_sample' vignettes/` matches only `vignettes/getting-started.Rmd` — there is no P8 or P9 vignette or benchmark anywhere in `vignettes/`. `INTRO.md:124` also advertises `vignette("getting-started")` as a "200-line tour of all 10 pilares"; it does cover 7-10 (lines 135-183) but skips P3 and P4 execution entirely (:96-97, :103-104).
findings.impact: The cheatsheets are the ONLY narrative documentation for pillars 7-10 that a reader can find, and the document describing them tells readers to look somewhere they are not published. INTRO.md's claim that P8/P9 have their own benchmarks is the justification given for excluding them from the head-to-head table at :99-106 — so the omission is defended by a non-existent artifact.
findings.action: Either wire `cheatsheets/` into the pkgdown site (a `navbar` menu of raw GitHub links, or copy them into `vignettes/articles/` as rendered pages) or correct `cheatsheets/README.md:22-24` to say GitHub-only. Correct `INTRO.md:116-118` to state that P8/P9 are covered only by unit tests and `getting-started`, or add the missing benchmarks.

findings.title: package_v2_for_zenodo.R fails with a cryptic stopifnot before its own step-count guard, and drops the resume hint from its error message
findings.correction: Both defects verified. tools/pretrain/package_v2_for_zenodo.R:25-27 runs three `stopifnot(file.exists(...))` on encoder_q.pt / metadata.json / loss_history.rds BEFORE reading state.rds at :30 and the step-count check at :31-37, and data-raw/pretrain_cerrado_train_v2.R writes exactly those artefacts only after the training call returns (torch_save encoder_q.pt at :84-85, saveRDS loss_history.rds at :86, write_json metadata.json at :121, .sha256 at :126-129) — so on any incomplete run the script dies at :25 with `file.exists(...) is not TRUE`, contradicting V1_3_2_HANDOFF.md:61 ("Verifies the v2 dir actually contains a 200k-step checkpoint (errors out otherwise)"). The sprintf bug reproduces: one `%d` with two arguments emits `WARN: one argument not used by format` and silently drops the `Rscript data-raw/pretrain_cerrado_train_v2.R` line. Scoped down because this is a maintainer-only helper in .Rbuildignore'd tools/ (.Rbuildignore:12) that never reaches a user.
findings.evidence: `tools/pretrain/package_v2_for_zenodo.R:25-27` runs `stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(V2_DIR, "encoder_q.pt")))` etc. BEFORE the step-count pre-flight at `:30-37`. `data-raw/pretrain_cerrado_train_v2.R:85-86,120,126` shows `encoder_q.pt`, `loss_history.rds`, `metadata.json` and the `.sha256` are only written AFTER the full 200 000-step loop finishes — and indeed none of them exist in the maintainer's `edaphos-cerrado-moco-v2/` directory today. Additionally `:32-36` is `stop(sprintf("Encoder still at step %d / 200000.  Resume training first via\n", ck$next_epoch - 1L, "  Rscript data-raw/pretrain_cerrado_train_v2.R"))` — one format spec, two arguments. Verified in R: this emits `WARN: one argument not used by format` and silently discards the `Rscript ...` line.
findings.impact: tools/pretrain/V1_3_2_HANDOFF.md:61 promises the script "Verifies the v2 dir actually contains a 200k-step checkpoint (errors out otherwise)". Run today it instead dies at line 25 with `Error: file.exists(file.path(V2_DIR, "encoder_q.pt")) is not TRUE` — no mention of steps, no resume instruction. Even on the intended path the helpful command is stripped from the message; under `options(warn = 2)` the sprintf warning becomes the error and masks the real diagnosis.
findings.action: Move the `readRDS(state.rds)` + `ck$next_epoch <= 200000L` guard above the three `stopifnot()` calls, and guard the readRDS itself for a missing checkpoint. Fix the sprintf: either use two `%s` specs or concatenate with `paste0`. Add the same 200k assertion to `wire_up_v2_doi.R` so Step 4 cannot run against an undertrained encoder.

findings.title: Roadmap table and NEWS were never updated for the last two feature commits; DESCRIPTION 3.10.0 conflicts with the 3.11.0 baked into the weights registry
findings.correction: Duplicates finding #1 (and #19) on the v3.11.0-vs-3.10.0 conflict. Its own new facts check out -- README.md:1713 still marks v1.9.3 as pending, NEWS.md has no 1.9.3 / 1.3.2 / 1.8.3 / 3.11.0 section, R/foundation_weights.R:82 and R/foundation_embed_coords.R:186/204/220 -- but two cites are wrong: the install_github("...@v2.8.0") instruction is at README.md:339, not :344 (:344 is `install.packages("torch")`), and `version = {2.8.0}` is at README.md:1735 inside the bibtex block at :1730-1740, not at :1741-1752 (which is the Zhang2026causal entry).
findings.evidence: Commit 05cb516 is titled "feat(v1.9.3): close roadmap promise -- IV refit with real 31-channel SoilGrids+WorldClim+SRTM stack" and its body reports `used_real_stack flag : TRUE  (was FALSE)`; the code landed (`R/foundation_embed_coords.R:186,204,220` document the new `schema=` argument "As of v3.11.0"). Yet README.md:1713 still reads `| v1.9.3  | Real geodata download path (EDAPHOS_IV_REAL_STACK) + refit    | 📝   |`. `grep '^# edaphos' NEWS.md` shows no `1.9.3`, no `1.3.2`, no `1.8.3` and no `3.11.0` section — newest is `# edaphos 3.10.0` at NEWS.md:1. Meanwhile `R/foundation_weights.R:82` declares `edaphos_version = c("1.2.0", "3.11.0")` and `R/foundation_embed_coords.R:186,204,220` reference "v3.11.0", while DESCRIPTION:3 says `Version: 3.10.0`. README.md:344 still instructs `install_github("HugoMachadoRodrigues/edaphos@v2.8.0")` and the citation block at :1741-1752 says `version = {2.8.0}`.
findings.impact: The README roadmap table — the document a reader uses to answer "what is left to do" — is wrong in both directions: it shows a closed item as open (v1.9.3) and offers no trace of the two most recent commits. `foundation_weights_list()` reports a v2 encoder as belonging to a version of edaphos that does not exist and has no NEWS entry, so a user cannot tell whether the row is aspirational or shipped. New users following README installation instructions get a package 8 minor versions old.
findings.action: Flip README.md:1713 to ✅ and add NEWS.md sections for 1.9.3 (31-channel stack + IV refit numbers from the 05cb516 commit body) and 3.11.0 (resume support + v2 registry row + the three tools/pretrain scripts). Decide the version story: either bump DESCRIPTION to 3.11.0 or change `R/foundation_weights.R:82` and the three `R/foundation_embed_coords.R` references to 3.10.0. Update the README install pin and citation block to the current version.

findings.title: Stale dead-end in data-raw/causal_iv_benchmark.R blocks a path that v1.9.1 already delivered
findings.evidence: `data-raw/causal_iv_benchmark.R:166-167`: `# raster stacks; deferred to v1.9.1 when the v2 encoder is published.` / `stop("MoCo v2 patch extraction not yet implemented; see v1.9.1 roadmap.")`. But v1.9.1 shipped: README.md:1706 marks `v1.9.1 Real MoCo v2 patch extraction (foundation_embed_at_coords) — Sargan passes empirically` as ✅, and `foundation_embed_at_coords` is exported (NAMESPACE:155) with `R/foundation_embed_coords.R` behind it. A separate live runner exists at `data-raw/causal_iv_benchmark_real.R`. Similarly `data-raw/causal_discovery_benchmark.R:177` still defers an algorithm to "a future release" with no roadmap row tracking it.
findings.impact: A reader auditing the data-raw runners is told a capability is missing that has existed for 8+ minor versions, and the stop() makes the older benchmark script unrunnable for no current reason. The comment also mis-attributes the blocker to "when the v2 encoder is published", conflating v1.9.1 (done) with v1.3.2 (genuinely open).
findings.action: Either delete `data-raw/causal_iv_benchmark.R:166-167` and route the script through `foundation_embed_at_coords()`, or delete the script in favour of `data-raw/causal_iv_benchmark_real.R` and note the supersession. Add a roadmap row for the deferred causal-discovery algorithm at `data-raw/causal_discovery_benchmark.R:177` or drop the promise.

findings.title: Pilar 7 was promised as INLA/Stan and delivered as a hand-rolled Gibbs sampler; the substitution is never disclosed
findings.evidence: `NEWS.md:1192-1199` "### Deferred (explicit roadmap entries)" lists `* v2.3.0 — Pilar 7: Bayesian hierarchical spatial models (INLA / Stan)`. What shipped (README.md:274, NEWS.md `# edaphos 2.3.0` section) is a "self-contained Gibbs sampler + optional spBayes::spLM backend" with "Profile-MLE phi for closed-form conditionals". Neither `INLA` nor `rstan`/`cmdstanr` appears anywhere in DESCRIPTION. `_pkgdown.yml:161-163` describes Pilar 7 as "Gaussian process + Gibbs sampler (R fast-path / RcppArmadillo / spBayes)" — the current reality — but no document records that the INLA/Stan promise was consciously dropped, and the one non-R backend that IS advertised (spBayes) has no working `predict()` (see R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:355-357).
findings.impact: A reader tracing the NEWS deferred-list forward cannot tell whether INLA/Stan support is still coming, was rejected on purpose, or was quietly replaced. Combined with the broken spBayes predict path, Pilar 7 currently has exactly one usable backend where three are advertised across the docs.
findings.action: Add one line to the roadmap (README.md table or the new pillars_roadmap.R row 7) stating that the INLA/Stan backend was superseded by the profile-MLE Gibbs sampler + RcppArmadillo fast path, and whether it is dropped or deferred. If deferred, give it a version row so it is tracked.

findings.title: Promised production-scale outputs never produced: the 10k-abstract LLM-KG run and the 6-pillar benchmark wrapper set
findings.evidence: NEWS.md:44-62 documents `data-raw/llm_kg_10k_pipeline.R` as "the ready-to-run end-to-end orchestrator for a 10 000+ abstract production extraction" with a "6-11 hours for 10 000 abstracts" budget, but the only evidence of execution is the "Live smoke test" at NEWS.md:33-42 on the bundled 10-abstract corpus (`inst/extdata/cerrado_abstracts.jsonl`, 10 lines -> 41 nodes / 30 edges). No 10k-scale output artifact exists in `inst/extdata/` (largest claim file is the 301-line `cerrado_claims_real_corpus.jsonl`). Separately, `_pkgdown.yml:199-202` titles a group "Benchmark wrappers (v3.1.0) — Plug-and-play wrappers for the 6-pilar WoSIS Cerrado benchmark" but only three exist (NAMESPACE:92-94: `benchmark_fit_p1_causal`, `benchmark_fit_p6_quantum`, `benchmark_fit_p10_gat`); `data-raw/benchmark_wosis_6pilar.R:35,61,77` re-reads P4/P5/P7 rows from the pre-computed `inst/extdata/benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7.rds` rather than refitting them.
findings.impact: The v3.10.0 headline feature ("production harness for 10k+ LLM-KG extraction runs") has been validated at 10 abstracts — 0.1 % of its stated scale — so the resumability, throttle/retry and error-log paths that justify the release have no large-run evidence. And a "6-pilar" benchmark that can only refit 3 of the 6 pillars cannot be regenerated end-to-end from source; the P4/P5/P7 numbers quoted in INTRO.md:99-106 and README.md:246-252 are frozen in an .rds with no live wrapper.
findings.action: Either execute one large LLM-KG run (the 301-line real corpus is a reasonable intermediate) and record the wall-clock/error-rate in NEWS, or downgrade the NEWS.md:44 wording from "ready-to-run production orchestrator" to "untested at scale". Add `benchmark_fit_p4_*`, `benchmark_fit_p5_*`, `benchmark_fit_p7_*` wrappers (the fitting code already exists in `data-raw/benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7.R`) or rename the `_pkgdown.yml:199` group to reflect the three that exist.

findings.title: foundation_embed_at_coords() converts a failed raster block read into an all-zero patch that is indistinguishable from a real embedding
findings.correction: none on the code path — R/foundation_embed_coords.R:144-148 is the `tryCatch(terra::values(...), error = function(e) matrix(NA_real_, patch_size * patch_size, C))`, :153-157 rewrites every NA to 0 after z-scoring, `out` is pre-filled NA only for coords excluded by the `valid_idx <- which(is_valid)` screen at :122-123, and the encoded row is written at :168 (cited :167) identically to a successful read, with no warning/counter/flag. SEVERITY DEFLATED: the tryCatch is a narrow path — the validity screen at :112-114 already excludes every coordinate within `half` of a raster edge, which is the dominant cause of out-of-window reads, so a surviving coordinate whose block read still errors implies a corrupt/unreadable raster rather than routine operation. The broader and more likely silent behaviour the finding brushes past is `v[is.na(v)] <- 0` mean-imputing ordinary NoData pixels for every patch, failed or not.
findings.evidence:
R/foundation_embed_coords.R:144-156. A failed `terra::values()` read becomes an all-NA block, which the very next loop rewrites to zeros:
```r
blk <- tryCatch(
  terra::values(stack, row = r0, nrows = patch_size,
                 col = c0, ncols = patch_size, mat = TRUE),
  error = function(e) matrix(NA_real_, patch_size * patch_size, C)
)
patch_arr <- aperm(array(blk, dim = c(patch_size, patch_size, C)), c(3L, 1L, 2L))
for (ch in seq_len(C)) {
  v <- (patch_arr[ch, , ] - means[ch]) / sds[ch]
  v[is.na(v)] <- 0
  patch_arr[ch, , ] <- v
}
```
The zeroed patch is then encoded and written into the output at :167 (`out[b_idx, ] <- emb_mat`) exactly like a successful read. Because `out` is pre-filled with NA only for coordinates already flagged invalid (:122-123, `valid_idx <- which(is_valid)`), a coordinate that passed the validity screen but whose block read failed receives a real-looking numeric embedding row. No `warning()`, no counter, no flag in the return value.
findings.impact: Every failed block read yields the encoder's embedding of an all-zero patch -- a specific, systematic vector that is identical for every failure and carries zero information about the site. Downstream consumers (the IV benchmark, `qf_embed_reduce`, `foundation_fit_regressor`) cannot detect it: it is finite, in-range, and not NA. A handful of these silently pull PCA components and regression fits toward a phantom cluster. The `tryCatch` also swallows the underlying cause (bad window bounds vs. corrupt raster vs. missing file), so the failure is undiagnosable after the fact.
findings.action: Count failures in the tryCatch handler at R/foundation_embed_coords.R:144-148 and mark the affected rows: set `out[i, ] <- NA_real_` for a failed read rather than encoding zeros, and after the batch loop emit `warning(sprintf("%d of %d coordinates could not be read from the raster; their embeddings are NA.", n_failed, length(valid_idx)))`. At minimum, re-raise `conditionMessage(e)` in a warning so the cause is visible.

findings.title: foundation_build_cerrado_stack() calls digest::digest() unguarded, but digest is Suggests-only -- the exported function dies on a clean install
findings.correction: Verified: R/foundation_embed_coords.R:231-241 guards terra and geodata then reaches `digest::digest(c(bbox, target_res), algo = "md5")` at :240, after `dir.create(cache_dir)` at :238; digest is Suggests-only (DESCRIPTION:45); `grep -rn 'digest::' R/` shows this is the sole unguarded call site (foundation_weights.R:139 is guarded at :130, edaphos_zenodo_release.R:154 is inline-guarded, llm_annotation.R:93 is in tryCatch); and R/foundation_tiles.R:17-19 states the graceful-failure contract. Downgraded because the function already requires terra + geodata (a ~200 MB live-download path), digest is a tiny ubiquitous package, and the failure is an immediate unambiguous "there is no package called 'digest'".
findings.evidence:
R/foundation_embed_coords.R:231-241. The preflight checks exactly two packages, then reaches an unguarded third:
```r
if (!requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE))
  stop("Install `terra` to build raster stacks.", call. = FALSE)
if (!requireNamespace("geodata", quietly = TRUE))
  stop("Install `geodata` to download SoilGrids / WorldClim / SRTM.", ...)
schema <- match.arg(schema)
...
tag <- sprintf("cerrado_stack_%s_%s.tif",
                schema,
                digest::digest(c(bbox, target_res), algo = "md5"))   # line 240
```
`digest` appears only in DESCRIPTION:45 under Suggests. The package's own convention is to guard it -- R/foundation_weights.R:130 (`if (!requireNamespace("digest", ...))`) and R/edaphos_zenodo_release.R:153 (`sha <- if (requireNamespace("digest", ...))`) both do; R/llm_annotation.R:93 wraps it in tryCatch. Line 240 is the sole unguarded call site. The file header at R/foundation_tiles.R:17-19 states the design contract this violates: "All heavy dependencies ... are Suggests. Every public function fails gracefully with a clear install / authentication hint when they are not available."
findings.impact: On any machine with terra + geodata but not digest -- a completely ordinary state given digest is Suggests -- this exported function dies at line 240 with base R's `there is no package called 'digest'`, after passing two install-hint guards that imply the dependency check is complete. The failure is also late: it happens after `dir.create(cache_dir)` at line 238, so it leaves a directory behind. Because `digest` is only used to build a cache filename, the failure is entirely avoidable.
findings.action: Add a third `requireNamespace("digest")` guard alongside the terra/geodata guards at R/foundation_embed_coords.R:231-235, or replace line 240's hash with a base-R alternative (e.g. `paste0(sprintf("%.4f", c(bbox, target_res)), collapse = "_")`, or `substr(tools::md5sum(tf), 1, 8)` on a temp serialisation) so the function has no Suggests dependency for cache naming at all.

findings.title: Off-by-one in the RcppArmadillo Gibbs sampler's w_post_mean accumulation makes the rcpp backend disagree with the R backend it claims to reproduce
findings.correction: Duplicate of the later, more accurate off-by-one finding; the bug itself is real (src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:103 0-based loop + :132-134 `if (iter > burn)` accumulates nmcmc-burn-1 terms over a divisor of nmcmc-burn, vs R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:276/:314). Wrong cites here: the kriging consumer is R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:389-391, not :381-383 (:381-383 is the posterior-draw index sampling); the equivalence assertion is src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:14-15, not :15-16; the thinning loop is at :141, not :140-143. Also, the nmcmc=50/burn=20 example at test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:62-63 runs the default "gibbs" backend, so that 3.3% figure is not actually exercised by the rcpp path.
findings.impact: `w_post_mean` from the rcpp backend is systematically shrunk toward zero by a factor of `(nmcmc - burn - 1) / (nmcmc - burn)` relative to the gibbs backend, and drops one legitimate post-burn draw. At the default `nmcmc = 2000, burn = 1000` the bias is 0.1%; at the small settings the tests and vignettes actually use (`nmcmc = 50L, burn = 20L` in tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:62) it is 3.3%. `w_post_mean` is the latent spatial field used for every kriging prediction (R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:381-383, `t(R_cross) %*% R_tr_inv %*% object$w_post_mean`), so the two backends produce measurably different maps while the docs claim they are interchangeable. The loose 0.2 tolerance on beta cannot detect it.
findings.action: Change src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:132 from `if (iter > burn)` to `if (iter >= burn)` to match the R loop's post-burn window, then recompile. Add a regression test to tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-rcpp.R asserting `expect_equal(fit_rcpp$w_post_mean, fit_gibbs$w_post_mean, tolerance = 0.05)` on a fixed seed so the equivalence claim in src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:15-16 is actually enforced.

findings.title: Two exported functions ship without \value in man/, contradicting the NEWS claim of 0 R CMD check notes
findings.correction: The Rd scan is exactly right — I re-ran it over every man/*.Rd with a `\usage{}` block and got precisely five hits: man/br_amazon.Rd, man/br_cerrado.Rd, man/br_pantanal.Rd (datasets, correctly using \format), man/foundation_tile_source_era5.Rd and man/no_deeponet_fit.Rd. Sources confirmed: R/foundation_tiles.R:181 gives modis an `@return` while era5 (:193-201) has none, and R/pilar8_neural_operators.R:98 gives `no_fno_fit` `@return An `edaphos_no_fno` fit.` while `no_deeponet_fit` at :394-395 has `@export` and no `@return`. WHAT IS OVERSTATED is "Two guaranteed `R CMD check --as-cran` findings": missing \value is characteristically a CRAN *reviewer* request ("please add \value to all exported functions"), not a reliable automated NOTE, so calling them guaranteed check output is not established. Meanwhile the "0 notes" claim is already conclusively falsified by the ~13 MB installed size (finding 7), which makes this a duplicate contribution to the same conclusion via a weaker mechanism.
findings.evidence:
Scanned every `man/*.Rd` with a `\usage{}` block for a missing `\value{}`. Two are exported functions (the other three hits -- man/br_amazon.Rd, man/br_cerrado.Rd, man/br_pantanal.Rd -- are datasets, where `\format`/`\source` is the correct pattern):
1. man/foundation_tile_source_era5.Rd -- has `\usage{foundation_tile_source_era5(...)}` and `\arguments{}` but no `\value{}`. Source: R/foundation_tiles.R:193-201 has `@param ... Ignored.` and `@export` but no `@return`. Its sibling stub DOES have one -- R/foundation_tiles.R:181, `#' @return Nothing; always stops with an install-hint message.` -- so the omission is an oversight, not a policy.
2. man/no_deeponet_fit.Rd -- `\title{Fit a DeepONet for depth-profile operators}`, `\usage{}` present, no `\value{}`. Source: R/pilar8_neural_operators.R:394-395 has `@export` at :394 with no `@return`; its FNO counterpart has one at R/pilar8_neural_operators.R:98 (`#' @return An `edaphos_no_fno` fit.`).
NEWS.md's v3.10.0 section claims "R CMD check: 0 errors / 0 notes". `R CMD check --as-cran` reports missing `\value` for exported functions, and RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md lists CRAN submission as a remaining step.
findings.impact: Two guaranteed `R CMD check --as-cran` findings standing between the package and the CRAN submission the release checklist is waiting on, in a repo whose NEWS already asserts a clean check. `no_deeponet_fit` is a headline Pillar 8 export, so a user reading `?no_deeponet_fit` is not told what the function returns -- they must infer the `edaphos_no_deeponet` class from the examples. This also means the "0 notes" claim was never verified against `--as-cran` on the current tree.
findings.action: Add `#' @return Nothing; always stops with an install-hint message.` at R/foundation_tiles.R:200 (mirroring :181) and `#' @return An \code{edaphos_no_deeponet} fit.` at R/pilar8_neural_operators.R:393, then `devtools::document()`. Run `R CMD check --as-cran` once before trusting the NEWS claim, and record the actual output in cran-comments.md.

findings.title: Stale forward-looking version markers and dead code left in shipped R/ sources
findings.evidence:
Five "future work" markers name milestones that have since shipped or long passed, all in files installed with the package:
- R/pilar8_neural_operators.R:28 -- "an API-stable reference for a future torch implementation (v2.4.1)"; R/pilar8_neural_operators_torch.R exists.
- R/pilar9_diffusion_models.R:77 -- "A U-Net port is v2.5.1 future work"; R/pilar9_diffusion_torch.R:1 is "torch/autograd DDPM with a 2-D U-Net denoiser" and defines `.torch_ddpm_unet` at :46.
- R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:26-27 -- "A torch-autograd port with full-gradient training is scheduled for v2.6.1"; R/pilar10_graph_nn_torch.R:1-5 is that port (v2.7.0).
- R/foundation_simclr.R:14-16 -- production-scale training "scheduled for 0.1.0+", in a package at Version 3.10.0.
- R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:357 -- a user-facing error message reading "use the pure-R gibbs backend for v2.3.0", shipped at v3.10.0.
Two dead statements:
- R/piml_quantum_bridge.R:94 -- `pred_fn <- tryCatch(stats::predict, error = function(e) NULL)`; `grep -n pred_fn R/*.R` returns this line only, so the variable is assigned and never read (and the tryCatch is vacuous -- referencing `stats::predict` cannot error).
- R/foundation_weights.R:206-209 -- `if (httr2::resp_status(resp) >= 400L) stop(...)` after `httr2::req_perform()`, which already throws on HTTP >= 400 by default, so the branch is unreachable.
findings.impact: Low individually, but collectively they misinform. A reader of R/pilar9_diffusion_models.R:77 concludes no U-Net exists when one ships in the same package; a user hitting R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:357 is told to target a version eight minor releases old, which reads like an abandoned code path rather than a deliberate backend restriction. The two dead statements are small but signal unreviewed code in files that are otherwise carefully written.
findings.action: Update the five comments to point at the files that fulfilled them (e.g. R/pilar9_diffusion_models.R:77 -> "A U-Net port ships in R/pilar9_diffusion_torch.R since v2.5.1"), reword the R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:357 message to drop the version reference, delete R/piml_quantum_bridge.R:94, and either delete R/foundation_weights.R:206-209 or convert it to an explicit `httr2::req_error(req, is_error = ...)` policy if the intent was to handle status codes manually.

findings.title: quantum_kernel() with the default rcpp backend has only a warning where it needs a hard cap, and silently returns an all-ones kernel for reps <= 0
findings.correction: none on the mechanics — R/quantum_kernel.R:180 is `if (n > 12L && backend == "r")` (the finding's 167-181 range is ~13 lines low), the default is `backend = c("rcpp", "r")` at :163, src/quantum_kernel_rcpp.cpp:133-136 warns at `n > 20` then computes `const size_t dim = (size_t) 1 << n`; the reps loop is cpp:95 `for (int r = 0; r < reps; ++r)` against |0…0> set at :92-93, and the R path is :76 `for (r in seq_len(as.integer(reps)))`. I confirmed `seq_len(0L)` gives length 0 and `seq_len(-1L)` errors "argument must be coercible to non-negative integer", so `reps = -1` does diverge (R errors, C++ returns ones). Reachability via R/quantum_foundation.R:55 `n_pcs >= 1L` → :167 `qf_krr_fit` → qf_embed_reduce → quantum_kernel is confirmed. SEVERITY DEFLATED: both triggers require the user to override documented defaults — R/quantum_foundation.R:45-47 states 8 is "the largest `n` for which `quantum_kernel()` stays classically simulable on a laptop", and `reps <= 0` is nonsense input no workflow produces. Note also that at `reps = 0` the two backends AGREE (both return all-ones), so the backend-divergence claim narrows to the single value -1.
findings.impact: (a) An n_pcs or ncol(X) a user considers reasonable kills the R session with an OS OOM (or triggers UB), past a warning that only says "may". The R-side guard that would have caught it is scoped to the backend nobody uses by default. (b) `reps = 0` returns a rank-1 all-ones Gram matrix -- a mathematically degenerate kernel that will still feed through `quantum_krr_fit` and produce a fitted model and metrics with no error, so a typo silently invalidates results. The two backends disagree on `reps = -1`, contradicting R/quantum_kernel.R:146-147's claim that `"r"` is a "pure-R reference implementation".
findings.action: In `quantum_kernel()` (R/quantum_kernel.R:163-181), add backend-independent validation before dispatch: `stopifnot(reps >= 1L)` and a hard `if (n > 20L) stop(sprintf("quantum_kernel() needs 2^%d complex amplitudes per sample (%.1f GB); reduce the feature/PC count to <= 20.", n, ...))`. Promote src/quantum_kernel_rcpp.cpp:133-135 from `Rcpp::warning` to `Rcpp::stop`, and add `if (reps < 1) Rcpp::stop("reps must be >= 1")` there as defence in depth. Add an upper bound to `n_pcs` in R/quantum_foundation.R:54-55.

findings.title: 12 duplicated, semantically divergent torch skip helpers shadow the canonical helper-torch.R; the package's own runtime guards never check torch_is_installed()
findings.correction: Counts verified: helper-torch.R:7 defines `.skip_if_no_torch()` (18 call sites) and 12 test files redefine a non-dotted `skip_if_no_torch()`; `grep -rn torch_is_installed R/` returns zero hits and all 13 package-side gates use bare `requireNamespace("torch")`. But "semantically divergent" and "correct in exactly one file, approximated in twelve" are wrong. Flavour (a) — test-foundation-weights.R:3-8, test-foundation-posterior.R:3, test-foundation-finetune.R:7, test-piml-neural-ode-ensemble.R:3 — is `skip_if_not_installed("torch")` followed by `if (!torch::torch_is_installed()) skip(...)`, i.e. functionally IDENTICAL to helper-torch.R:8-9 (which differs only by `isTRUE()`). Criticism (ii), that flavour (a) calls `torch::torch_is_installed()` "unguarded", applies verbatim to the canonical helper it praises. Flavour (b), `tryCatch(torch::torch_tensor(1), ...)`, actually allocates a tensor and is a stronger probe than either. So this is duplication/DRY debt, not a correctness asymmetry. The R/-side one-level check is a genuine (small) UX gap.
findings.evidence: tests/testthat/helper-torch.R defines the canonical, correctly-documented `.skip_if_no_torch()` (dot-prefixed, torch package + `torch::torch_is_installed()` Lantern probe) and explains exactly why the two-level check is needed. It is used 18 times.
