But 12 test files each redefine a *non*-dot-prefixed `skip_if_no_torch()` locally, in three different flavours: (a) `if (!torch::torch_is_installed()) skip(...)` -- test-foundation-finetune.R:7, test-foundation-posterior.R:3, test-piml-neural-ode-ensemble.R:3, test-foundation-weights.R:3; (b) `tryCatch(torch::torch_tensor(1), error = function(e) skip(...))` -- test-piml-hierarchical.R:1, test-foundation.R:1, test-piml-neural.R:1, test-foundation-tiles.R:2, test-foundation-moco.R:1, test-temporal.R:1; (c) `isTRUE(tryCatch(torch::torch_is_installed(), error = function(e) FALSE))` -- test-piml-posterior.R:3, test-temporal-posterior.R:3. Blind spots: (i) `grep -rn torch_is_installed R/` returns ZERO hits -- all five package-side guards (.moco_require_torch R/foundation_moco.R:29, .foundation_require_torch R/foundation_simclr.R:19, .piml_require_torch R/piml_neural_ode.R:12, .temporal_require_torch R/temporal_convlstm.R:13, .ft_require_torch R/foundation_finetune.R:41) check only `requireNamespace("torch")`, so the exact CI configuration (torch installed, Lantern absent) passes every guard and then dies deep inside with 'Lantern is not loaded' instead of the intended actionable message; (ii) flavour (a) calls `torch::torch_is_installed()` unguarded after only `skip_if_not_installed("torch")`, so a torch package whose load itself errors takes the test down rather than skipping; (iii) none of the helpers checks reticulate, which is why finding #2 is invisible.
findings.impact: The gating strategy is correct in exactly one file and approximated in twelve. The asymmetry between test-side (2-level) and package-side (1-level) detection means the suite is systematically blind to the single most common real-world state -- torch installed, libtorch not -- which is precisely the state of every CI runner and of any user who installed torch from CRAN without running install_torch().
findings.action: Delete the 12 local `skip_if_no_torch` definitions and call `.skip_if_no_torch()` from tests/testthat/helper-torch.R everywhere. Then add the Lantern probe to the package guards: in each of the five `.require_torch` helpers, follow the `requireNamespace` check with `if (!isTRUE(torch::torch_is_installed())) stop("libtorch is not installed; run torch::install_torch() once.", call. = FALSE)`. Add one torch-free test asserting each guard's message so the branch is covered by CI.

findings.title: 44 print/summary S3 methods, zero snapshot tests, 15 expect_output calls -- half of them behind torch/qiskit gates
findings.correction: none — `grep -c "^S3method(print,\|^S3method(summary," NAMESPACE` = 44; `tests/testthat/_snaps` does not exist; `expect_output|expect_snapshot|expect_print` = 15 hits across exactly 12 files, of which test-foundation-moco.R, test-foundation.R, test-piml-hierarchical.R, test-temporal.R, test-temporal-posterior.R (torch) and test-quantum-vqe.R (qiskit) are gated off on CI. This is a coverage gap rather than a defect — print methods are not wholly unexercised (9 assertions do run), and nothing is currently broken.
findings.evidence: NAMESPACE registers 44 `S3method(print, ...)` / `S3method(summary, ...)` entries. `ls tests/testthat/_snaps` -> the directory does not exist, so there are zero `expect_snapshot` tests. Total `expect_output|expect_snapshot|expect_print` calls: 15, spread over 12 files -- and 6 of those files are gated so they do not run on CI: test-foundation-moco.R, test-foundation.R, test-piml-hierarchical.R, test-temporal.R, test-temporal-posterior.R (torch) and test-quantum-vqe.R (qiskit). Effective print/summary output coverage on a CI runner is therefore roughly 9 assertions against 44 methods.
findings.impact: The console surface -- which for a package pitched at researchers IS the primary interface, and which 14 vignettes render -- is essentially unverified. A malformed `print` (NA in a header, a dropped field, a broken sprintf) ships silently and only shows up as ugly vignette output.
findings.action: Add `expect_snapshot(print(fit))` / `expect_snapshot(summary(fit))` for the S3 classes constructible without torch or Python -- edaphos_bhs, edaphos_al_model, edaphos_causal_effect, edaphos_causal_kg, edaphos_quantum_krr, edaphos_posterior, edaphos_gnn_gat (R backend), edaphos_no_fno/no_deeponet (R backend), edaphos_dm (R backend) -- which covers the majority of the 44 methods on a torch-free runner. Commit tests/testthat/_snaps and let CI diff it.

findings.title: .batchbald_aleatoric_var() silently falls back to in-sample random-forest residuals whenever any OOB prediction is NA
findings.correction: The code reads exactly as quoted (R/active_batchbald.R:67-77) and the silent two-branch design is real, but the fallback is unreachable for any model `al_fit()` can produce, so the impact does not exist. `al_fit` -> `.fit_core` always calls `ranger::ranger(..., quantreg = TRUE, keep.inbag = TRUE)`, and ranger itself enforces `minoob <- min(rowSums(inbag.counts == 0)); if (minoob < 10) stop("Error: Too few trees for out-of-bag quantile regression.")` — I read this in the installed ranger 0.18.0 source. That guarantees every observation has >= 10 OOB trees, hence zero NAs in `rg$predictions`, hence `length(na.omit(oob)) == length(y_train)` always holds and the OOB branch always wins. Verified empirically on ranger 0.18.0: n = 40 with num.trees = 50 and 500 both give length-40 predictions with 0 NAs. The claimed trigger regime ("small-n / small-num.trees") is precisely the regime where ranger refuses to fit at all rather than emitting NA OOB predictions — the two failure modes are mutually exclusive, not co-located.
findings.impact: Random-forest in-sample residuals are drastically optimistic -- each tree has memorised its bootstrap sample -- so the fallback underestimates aleatoric variance by a large, data-dependent factor. `sigma_a2` feeds the BatchBALD acquisition at R/active_batchbald.R:285 (`sigma_a2 <- max(.batchbald_aleatoric_var(model), 1e-8)`), which is the term that separates epistemic from aleatoric uncertainty in the greedy log-det objective. Understating it inflates the apparent epistemic share and biases site selection toward noisy rather than genuinely informative locations -- silently degrading the headline Pillar 5 v-feature (`al_query_batchbald()`, R/pillars_roadmap.R:14) with no diagnostic.
findings.action: Replace the length comparison at R/active_batchbald.R:71 with NA-aware pairing: `keep <- !is.na(rg$predictions); if (sum(keep) >= 2L) stats::var(y_train[keep] - rg$predictions[keep])` so partial OOB coverage still uses OOB residuals. Keep the in-sample branch only for the case where no OOB predictions exist at all, and emit a `warning()` when it is taken.
